(a) Should an individual be appointed on the basis of any one qualification, and subsequently lose or be stripped of said qualification, they are subject to immediate dismissal at the discretion of the Chief Medical Examiner.

sections.heading: The Chief Medical Examiner may dismiss members of the Medical Review Board for convicted crimin
sections.text: The Chief Medical Examiner may dismiss members of the Medical Review Board for convicted criminal activity, or conduct contrary to a clearly defined and internally announced set of policies.

sections.heading: The Medical Review Board may, with a ¾ majority vote, expel one of its members compelling the C
sections.text: The Medical Review Board may, with a ¾ majority vote, expel one of its members compelling the Chief Medical Examiner to dismiss the expelled board member.

sections.heading: The Chief Medical Examiner shall review, and retain exclusive jurisdiction on, the activity or
sections.text: The Chief Medical Examiner shall review, and retain exclusive jurisdiction on, the activity or lack thereof, of public officials and public servants regardless of political subdivision.

sections.heading: The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board, shall launch medical investigations ba
sections.text:
The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board, shall launch medical investigations based on reports or suspicions of inactivity from public servants or government officials.

(a) Any individual(s) contracted to assist with a medical investigation shall be temporarily afforded the investigative authority and jurisdiction of the Medical Review Board for the duration of said investigation.

(b) Individuals contracted to a medical investigation may be severed from the investigation at any time, at the discretion of the residing Coroner, or Chief Medical Examiner.

sections.heading: The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board with the consent of the Chief Medical E
sections.text:
The Chief Medical Examiner, or the Medical Review Board with the consent of the Chief Medical Examiner, shall have the authority to subpoena access to any channel or section of any official Discord server, provided that it is pursuant to an investigation related to their duties, or for the aims of finding any signs of life.

(a) Should any section or channel be classified, said section must remain under seal, viewable only by the Chief Medical Examiner and investigating Medical Review Board.

(b) Any investigating party under the Medical Review Board must provide reasonable justification for the subpoena of information and show that it is relevant to their duties.

(c) The Medical Review Board cannot subpoena access to internal channels or communications without first proving that an individual has been inactive within all public forums for a minimum of thirty days without an excuse of absence.

(d) Any written documentation created or issued by the medical review board that utilizes evidence from channels classified under the State Secrets Act shall only contain the timestamp and author of a communication. Furthermore, no message content that was posted within classified communications shall be present in any written documentation, regardless of redaction.

sections.heading: In drastic circumstances, as so determined by the Chief Medical Examiner, they may issue compul
sections.text:
In drastic circumstances, as so determined by the Chief Medical Examiner, they may issue compulsory warrants, with written signature from a member of the judiciary, for the physical in-game presence of a person, to appear before the Medical Review Board as proof of life.

(a) The Coroner responsible for said jurisdiction shall be tasked with delegating or assuming the duties of delivering the notice of, and the execution of said warrant for the person.

sections.heading: Should an individual have no evidence of activity within the State of Mayflower for a period of
sections.text: Should an individual have no evidence of activity within the State of Mayflower for a period of thirty consecutive days, either in the Lee County game, or any of the official State of Mayflower Discord servers as listed in the #information channel of the State of Mayflower Discord server, they shall be deemed inactive.

sections.heading: Upon the Chief Medical Examiner finding evidence of an inactive person, the Medical Review Boar
sections.text:
Upon the Chief Medical Examiner finding evidence of an inactive person, the Medical Review Board shall meet to review the report. If the Medical Review Board, with a unanimous vote, concludes that the evidence is sufficient to take action, the board shall write a death certificate and present it to the Chief Medical Examiner.

(a) Periods of inactivity automatically expire if a person communicates in any official Mayflower Discord server, or are seen in-game.

(i) Said person must then be removed from the registry, typically without notice, and are not protected from death investigations.

(ii) A person may refile for scheduled inactivity if this occurs.

sections.heading: Death certificates are unenforceable until signed by the Chief Medical Examiner
sections.text: Death certificates are unenforceable until signed by the Chief Medical Examiner.

sections.heading: The Chief Medical Examiner is required to contact the recipient of the certificate where the re
sections.text:
The Chief Medical Examiner is required to contact the recipient of the certificate where the recipient has a period of forty-eight (48) hours to contest the death certificate. If the recipient fails to respond within said period, the Chief Medical Examiner may formally sign the death certificate.

(a) The Chief Medical Examiner shall be required to attempt to contact the recipient via Discord direct messages.

(i) If the Chief Medical Examiner is unable to directly message the recipient, the Chief Medical Examiner shall publicly announce the death certificate in a relevant official Discord server. No other means of contacting the recipient need be exhausted.

(b) In the event the recipient wishes to contest the certificate, the Chief Medical Examiner shall be unable to sign the death certificate, unless;

(i) The Chief Medical Examiner may obtain a written signature from a Justice or the Chief Justice of the Mayflower Supreme Court to override any contest.

sections.heading: The State Medical Examiner’s Office shall maintain a line of communication in which both inacti
sections.text: The State Medical Examiner’s Office shall maintain a line of communication in which both inactivity can be reported, and death certificates can be challenged in the event that the recipient has been falsely flagged. The State Medical Examiner’s Office shall be compelled to revoke death certificates if the individual challenges the certificate, provided Section V. (b) (iii), is not met.

sections.heading: The recipient of a death certificate
sections.text:
The recipient of a death certificate; if employed in a public agency, department, judiciary, elected office, or any other official position within the State of Mayflower; shall have those positions forfeited and made vacant.

(a) If the recipient wishes to return to activity, they may not be denied the ability to be appointed, elected, or employed in public office because of the issuance of a death certificate alone.

(b) Employers shall not further prohibit the recipient from reentering employment within a public agency unless other factors listed in the Public Servants Act disqualify their entry into a department.

sections.heading: The Attorney General shall create forms for public use that will allow citizens to submit tips
sections.text:
The Attorney General shall create forms for public use that will allow citizens to submit tips on crime; submit tips on law enforcement misconduct; submit tips on arbitrary administrative actions; and submit tips on public corruption.

(a) The Attorney General may offer monetary incentives in exchange for the submission of a tip.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may administer oaths, examine witnesses, take depositions, and receive evi
sections.text: The Attorney General may administer oaths, examine witnesses, take depositions, and receive evidence.

sections.text: The Attorney General may issue subpoenas, and; order the taking of depositions and order responses to written interrogations.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may through motion vacate an arrest, citation or other form of detention o
sections.text: The Attorney General may through motion vacate an arrest, citation or other form of detention on the basis that there exists insufficient probable cause for such arrest, citation or detention. No court shall review the contents of the vacature order nor deny for any reason except insofar as to determine if the motion is in proper form and certified by the Attorney General. The order of vacature by Court shall be res judicata.

sections.heading: The Attorney General has the ability to refuse to defend a government official in suits of offi
sections.text: The Attorney General has the ability to refuse to defend a government official in suits of official misconduct - if that Attorney General follows up the case with a criminal investigation against the individual, as well as provide injunctive relief in the form of an order that repairs the injury caused.

sections.heading: Whenever any person, sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, cooperative, joint venture,
sections.text: Whenever any person, sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, cooperative, joint venture, freelance, non-profit, or other commercial business entity, registered or unregistered, engages in repeated fraudulent or illegal acts, or otherwise demonstrates persistent fraud or illegality in the carrying on, conducting, or transaction of business, whether it be public, or other private business, the Attorney General may apply to the Mayflower District Court for an order enjoining the continuance of such business activity or any fraudulent or illegal acts, directing restitution and damages. The court may award the relief applied for or so much thereof as it may deem proper. The word "fraud" or "fraudulent" as used herein shall include any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud, and any deception, misrepresentation, concealment, suppression, false pretense, false promise, or unconscionable contractual provisions. The term "persistent fraud" or "illegality" as used herein shall include the continuance or carrying on of any fraudulent or illegal act or conduct. The term "repeated" as used herein shall include the repetition of any separate and distinct fraudulent or illegal act, or conduct that affects more than one person.

sections.heading: In connection with any such application, the Attorney General is authorized to take proof, make
sections.text: In connection with any such application, the Attorney General is authorized to take proof, make a determination of the relevant facts, issue subpoenas, and administer oaths. If a person subpoenaed to attend upon such inquiry fails to obey the command of a subpoena without reasonable cause, or if a person in attendance upon such inquiry shall, without reasonable cause, refuse to be sworn or to be examined or to answer a question or to produce a book or paper, when ordered so to do by the officer conducting such inquiry, he shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1503. The Attorney General or their designated officer in the Department of Justice is authorized to prosecute any person for perjury committed during the course of any investigation conducted pursuant to this section.

sections.heading: In any case where the Attorney General has the authority to initiate a civil action or proceedi
sections.text: In any case where the Attorney General has the authority to initiate a civil action or proceeding to enforce a law of this state, the Attorney General may, in lieu of such action, accept an assurance of discontinuance from any person engaged in or who has engaged in the act or practice violating that law. This assurance may include a stipulation for the voluntary payment by the alleged violator of the reasonable costs and expenses incurred by the Attorney General during the investigation. Evidence of a violation of this assurance shall serve as prima facie proof of a violation of the applicable law in any subsequent civil action or proceeding initiated by the Attorney General.

sections.heading: An investigative agency shall be defined as any agency that
sections.text: An investigative agency shall be defined as any agency that: Investigates complaints of misconduct against its own agents; Investigates complaints of criminal activity in general; Investigates complaints of criminal activity against its own agents. To ensure a proper case and court pipeline, the Attorney General shall have general oversight abilities over such investigative agencies.

sections.text: The Attorney General may promulgate rules for investigations and ethics.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may sanction investigative agencies that fail to follow rules and procedur
sections.text: The Attorney General may sanction investigative agencies that fail to follow rules and procedure by revoking that agency’s ability to petition the courts for warrants, submit cases to be prosecuted, or other tools provided by law that investigative agencies get to enjoy.

sections.heading: Any good standing investigative agency shall, upon the finding of any criminal action, refer th
sections.text: Any good standing investigative agency shall, upon the finding of any criminal action, refer the case files to the Attorney General for prosecution.

sections.text: The Attorney General shall retain oversight over all investigative agencies, and their caseflow.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may issue memorandums to investigative agencies or departments directing t
sections.text: The Attorney General may issue memorandums to investigative agencies or departments directing the agency to investigate and submit cases as part of the prosecutorial doctrine of the Attorney General’s Office.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may define the means and ways it wishes to prosecute certain crimes
sections.text: The Attorney General may define the means and ways it wishes to prosecute certain crimes. The Attorney General may also establish priorities in which he wishes to prosecute some crimes more than others by realm of their importance to the general welfare of the people.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may choose to, if he has adequate constitutional backing, declare provisio
sections.text: The Attorney General may choose to, if he has adequate constitutional backing, declare provisions of a law “unenforceable” by transmitting in writing the reasons for such declaration to the Governor and presiding officer of the State Senate.

sections.heading: The Attorney General may choose to, if evaluated so in his priorities, not prosecute specific c
sections.text: The Attorney General may choose to, if evaluated so in his priorities, not prosecute specific crimes due to the crime not having priority over other prosecutions the state is bringing.

sections.heading: The Attorney General shall have the ability to appoint a special counsel to investigate any Sta
sections.text:
The Attorney General shall have the ability to appoint a special counsel to investigate any State Senator, department head, an individual running for election, or other government officials at the State, County, or Municipal levels.

(a) The Attorney General shall not appoint a special counsel to investigate a private citizen.

sections.text: The Special Counsel, while within his jurisdiction, shall have the authority and ability to exercise investigative and prosecutorial functions as the Attorney General.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel shall determine whether and to what extent to inform or consult the Attorne
sections.text: The Special Counsel shall determine whether and to what extent to inform or consult the Attorney General about the conduct of their responsibilities pursuant to the guidelines set by the Attorney General in the appointment order.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel shall comply with all rules and procedures of the Attorney General’s Office
sections.text: The Special Counsel shall comply with all rules and procedures of the Attorney General’s Office.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel shall not be subject to any day-to-day supervision by a member of the Attor
sections.text: The Special Counsel shall not be subject to any day-to-day supervision by a member of the Attorney General’s Office.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel and staff shall be subject to disciplinary action for misconduct and breach
sections.text: The Special Counsel and staff shall be subject to disciplinary action for misconduct and breach of ethical duties under the same standards and to the same extent as are other employees of the Attorney General’s Office.

sections.heading: A Special Counsel may request the assignment of appropriate Attorney General’s Office employees
sections.text: A Special Counsel may request the assignment of appropriate Attorney General’s Office employees to assist the Special Counsel. The Attorney General’s Office shall gather and provide the Special Counsel with the names and resumes of appropriate personnel available for detail.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel may also request the details of specific employees, and the office for whic
sections.text: The Special Counsel may also request the details of specific employees, and the office for which the designated employee works shall make reasonable efforts to accommodate the request.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel shall assign the duties and supervise the work of such employees while they
sections.text: The Special Counsel shall assign the duties and supervise the work of such employees while they are assigned to the Special Counsel. If necessary, the Special Counsel may request that additional personnel be hired or assigned from outside the Attorney General’s Office.

sections.heading: All personnel in the Attorney General’s Office shall cooperate to the fullest extent possible w
sections.text: All personnel in the Attorney General’s Office shall cooperate to the fullest extent possible with the Special Counsel.

sections.heading: The Special Counsel may hire special investigators as he sees fit to investigate a claim under
sections.text: The Special Counsel may hire special investigators as he sees fit to investigate a claim under his jurisdiction.

sections.heading: In this Chapter, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pron
sections.text: In this Chapter, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pronouns, regardless of gender. Terms such as 'he,' 'him,' or 'his' shall be deemed to include 'she,' 'her,' 'hers,' 'they,' 'them,' 'theirs,' or any other pronoun as applicable. This inclusive interpretation applies to all provisions, ensuring gender neutrality and inclusivity throughout this Chapter.

sections.text: The Attorney General may declare a state of civil disorder in any county upon a finding that widespread violence, rioting, or coordinated unlawful assemblies substantially endanger public safety, property, or essential government functions. Such declaration shall remain in effect until rescinded by the Attorney General or by resolution of the State Senate, approved by a simple majority.

sections.text: LONG TITLE. An act to ensure democratic process with the appointment and removal of municipal department heads.

sections.text: SHORT TITLE. This act shall be known and may be cited as the “Municipal Department Heads Act.”

sections.heading: The term “Municipal Department” shall be defined as
sections.text:
The term “Municipal Department” shall be defined as:

(a) Any government agency primarily operating or based out of a city or township within the State of Mayflower.

sections.text:
The term “Municipal Department Head” shall be defined as:

(a) The leader or chief executive of any Municipal Department.

sections.heading: The term “County Executive” shall be defined as
sections.text:
The term “County Executive” shall be defined as:

(a) The elected head of a County Government’s executive branch within the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The term “County Board” shall be defined as
sections.text:
The term “County Board” shall be defined as:

(a) An elected member member of a county legislature within the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The term “Functional County Government” shall be defined as
sections.text:
The term “Functional County Government” shall be defined as:

(a) The government of a County within the State of Mayflower that has both an elected County Executive currently serving a term in that office, and a body of County Board members currently serving a term in that office.

sections.heading: The term “Functional Municipal Government” shall be defined as
sections.text:
The term “Functional Municipal Government” shall be defined as:

(a) The government of a city or township within the State of Mayflower that has both an elected Mayor or Executive currently serving a term in that office, and a body of elected legislators currently serving a term in that office.

sections.text: When a Municipal Department Head’s Office becomes vacant, in the absence of a Functional Municipal Government, the County Executive shall nominate their replacement. This replacement must be vetted and ratified by a ⅔ majority vote by that County’s Board or legislature.

sections.heading: The terms “Agency for International Intelligence” and “International Intelligence Agency” shall
sections.text: The terms “Agency for International Intelligence” and “International Intelligence Agency” shall refer to the same body and may be used interchangeably.

sections.heading: The Governor may grant exceptions to Title 3, Subtitle 1, Chapter XI of the Mayflower State Cod
sections.text: The Governor may grant exceptions to Title 3, Subtitle 1, Chapter XI of the Mayflower State Code as it pertains to the Agency for International Intelligence and foreign intelligence activity. Such exceptions will be documented and in writing, but not necessarily entered into the official record if such documentation would be pernicious to state security interests.

sections.heading: The Agency for International Intelligence shall exist as a hybrid state security organization p
sections.text: The Agency for International Intelligence shall exist as a hybrid state security organization possessing both military and civilian attributes, operating under civilian control while supporting military operations.

sections.heading: The Agency for International Intelligence shall be organizationally housed under the Governor’s
sections.text:
The Agency for International Intelligence shall be organizationally housed under the Governor’s Office and report to the Governor.

(a) The Director of the Agency for International Intelligence shall work in tandem with the Director of State Intelligence to plan foreign intelligence priorities, yet shall not be obliged to follow direction or order from the Director of State Intelligence.

sections.heading: In the interests of the security of the foreign intelligence activities of the State of Mayflow
sections.text: In the interests of the security of the foreign intelligence activities of the State of Mayflower, the Agency for International Intelligence shall be exempt from Title 3, Chapter XI of the Mayflower State Code to the extent directed by the Governor.

sections.heading: There shall be a Director of the Agency for International Intelligence, appointed by the Govern
sections.text: There shall be a Director of the Agency for International Intelligence, appointed by the Governor, with the advice and consent of the State Senate.

sections.heading: The Director of the Agency for International Intelligence shall be the Department Head of the A
sections.text: The Director of the Agency for International Intelligence shall be the Department Head of the Agency for International Intelligence.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 1 § 10302. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Director shall sit on the State Security Council and Cabinet at the discretion of the Gover
sections.text: The Director shall sit on the State Security Council and Cabinet at the discretion of the Governor.

sections.heading: The Director shall hold authority to classify information as “O” Classification, and to access
sections.text: The Director shall hold authority to classify information as “O” Classification, and to access such information as defined under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(d).

sections.heading: The Director may be either a civilian or commissioned military officer
sections.text:
The Director may be either a civilian or commissioned military officer.

(a) If a military officer, the Director shall wear such rank and exercise the privileges, authority, and precedence appertaining thereto as directed by the Adjutant General while so serving, but shall not thereby exercise command authority over forces of the armed services except as otherwise provided by law or regulation.

sections.heading: The Adjutant General may, with concurrence of the Director, detail military commissioned and no
sections.text: The Adjutant General may, with concurrence of the Director, detail military commissioned and noncommissioned officers for service in the Agency, in which case such detailed personnel shall continue to be bound by all expectations and standards of the National Guard while reporting to appropriate military and Agency superiors.

sections.heading: With the consent of the Adjutant General, the Director may dispatch civilian employees of the A
sections.text: With the consent of the Adjutant General, the Director may dispatch civilian employees of the Agency to receive initial military training in order to transfer into status under § 10306.

sections.heading: The Director of the International Intelligence Agency is authorized to—
The Director shall organize the Agency for International Intelligence at his discretion in a ma
sections.text: The Director shall organize the Agency for International Intelligence at his discretion in a manner conducive to the mission of the Agency.

sections.heading: The Director shall, at least quarterly, brief and report to the State Security Council regardin
sections.text: The Director shall, at least quarterly, brief and report to the State Security Council regarding the activities of the Agency for International Intelligence in such quarterly period.

sections.heading: The Director may–
sections.text:
The Director may–

(a) Liaise directly with federal intelligence, law enforcement, military, and diplomatic entities without intermediary approval.

(b) Determine, in consultation with the Attorney General, the legality of intelligence activities conducted under this statute.

(c) Classify, declassify, and control the dissemination of information produced or held by the Service.

(d) Grant temporary clearances for no more than 7 days to employees of the Agency for International Intelligence for information and intelligence used by the Service.

sections.heading: To provide compensation for assets, informants, non-public employees, and asylum seekers to adv
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 1 § 10404. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: There shall be established an Office of State Intelligence
sections.text: There shall be established an Office of State Intelligence.

sections.heading: The Office of State Intelligence shall be headed by the Director of State Intelligence, which s
sections.text:
The Office of State Intelligence shall be headed by the Director of State Intelligence, which shall be appointed by the Governor with the advice and consent of the State Legislature.

(a) Upon the enactment of this act, individuals nominated for this position must possess at least:

(i) 20 days of consecutive service within any county, state, inter-state, inter-county, or federal law enforcement investigative body, or 30 days as the head of an investigative body within any of the aforementioned jurisdictions.

sections.heading: After February 1st, 2026, individuals nominated for this position must possess at least
sections.text: (b) After February 1st, 2026, individuals nominated for this position must possess at least:

sections.heading: 80 days of consecutive service within any county, state, inter-state or federal law enforcement
sections.text: (i) 80 days of consecutive service within any county, state, inter-state or federal law enforcement investigative body, or 90 days as the head of an investigative body within any of the aforementioned jurisdictions.

sections.heading: The Office of State Intelligence shall be a cabinet-level office, with the Director of State In
sections.text: The Office of State Intelligence shall be a cabinet-level office, with the Director of State Intelligence being a Cabinet officer, reporting directly to the Governor and participating in Cabinet deliberations.

sections.heading: The Office of State Intelligence shall serve as the central coordinating body for intelligence,
sections.text: The Office of State Intelligence shall serve as the central coordinating body for intelligence, counterintelligence, and investigative oversight operations across all state agencies.

sections.heading: The Director of State Intelligence shall serve as the Governor’s chief advisor and coordinator
sections.text: The Director of State Intelligence shall serve as the Governor’s chief advisor and coordinator for matters concerning state intelligence and interagency intelligence integration.

sections.heading: In the event the Director of State Intelligence becomes incapacitated, resigns, or is otherwise
sections.text:
In the event the Director of State Intelligence becomes incapacitated, resigns, or is otherwise unable to perform the duties of office, authority shall temporarily transfer to the Deputy Director of Intelligence until a new appointment is confirmed by the Governor.

(a) All active directives, memorandums, and orders issued by the Director shall remain in force during such interim period.

sections.heading: The Office of State Intelligence shall—
sections.text:
The Office of State Intelligence shall—

(a) Direct and coordinate intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination across all state agencies.

(b) Establish and enforce uniform standards for intelligence gathering, data security, and interagency information sharing.

(c) Assess and monitor threats to the security, stability, and interests of the State.

(d) Advise the Governor and Legislature on matters relating to intelligence, counterintelligence, and security policy.

(e) Ensure compliance with laws and policies protecting civil rights, civil liberties, and privacy in all intelligence activities.

(f) Issue such directives, regulations, and operational guidelines as are necessary to carry out the provisions of this section.

sections.heading: All departments and agencies of the State are hereby directed to cooperate fully with the Offic
sections.text: All departments and agencies of the State are hereby directed to cooperate fully with the Office of the State Intelligence Director in matters relating to intelligence collection, analysis, and coordination, subject to applicable law.

sections.heading: The State Intelligence Director shall have unrestricted access to all intelligence, surveillanc
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 1 § 11203. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The State Intelligence Director shall have authority to issue intelligence Directives and Memor
sections.text: The State Intelligence Director shall have authority to issue intelligence Directives and Memorandums to all intelligence or investigative agencies for the purpose of coordination, compliance, or information dissemination. These directives shall carry binding effect upon receipt unless revoked by the Governor.

sections.heading: The Director may establish temporary task forces for intelligence-gathering or special investig
sections.text: The Director may establish temporary task forces for intelligence-gathering or special investigative purposes, and assign personnel from any state law enforcement or defense agency to such operations as deemed necessary

sections.heading: The Director may issue operational restrictions, suspensions, or removals of security clearance
sections.text: The Director may issue operational restrictions, suspensions, or removals of security clearances from any intelligence or investigative personnel where credible risks are identified.

sections.heading: No agency may withhold information from the Director under the pretext of classification, privi
sections.text:
No agency may withhold information from the Director under the pretext of classification, privilege, or compartmentalization.

(a) Any state official, agency head, or employee who willfully obstructs, refuses, or delays compliance with a lawful order or directive of the State Intelligence Director shall be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including suspension, removal from office, or referral for criminal investigation as appropriate.

(b) The Director shall notify the Office of the Governor of any instance of noncompliance or obstruction for immediate executive review.

(c) The Governor reserves the authority to issue further orders to ensure enforcement and uphold the integrity of state intelligence operations.

sections.heading: The Director of State Intelligence shall, at least quarterly, submit a full and unabridged repo
sections.text:
The Director of State Intelligence shall, at least quarterly, submit a full and unabridged report to the Governor and the State Legislature, or a committee it has designated

(a)The report shall include, but shall not be limited to

(i) Summarizing the state’s threat environment

(ii) Summarizing interagency coordination and joint operations undertaken during the reporting period.

(iii) Major intelligence activities.

(iv) Recommendations for security policy.

sections.heading: The Director of State Intelligence shall immediately notify the Governor and the State Legislat
sections.text: The Director of State Intelligence shall immediately notify the Governor and the State Legislature, or a committee it has designated, of any credible and imminent threat to the safety, security, or sovereignty of the State.

sections.heading: The Governor or State Legislature may, by written request, direct the Director to prepare a spe
sections.text: The Governor or State Legislature may, by written request, direct the Director to prepare a special report concerning a specific security issue, intelligence matter, or operational concern. Such a report shall be submitted within thirty (30) days of the request, unless an extension is granted for good cause.

sections.heading: The Director of State Intelligence may hold public briefings or issue press statements concerni
sections.text: The Director of State Intelligence may hold public briefings or issue press statements concerning general threat trends or public safety advisories, provided that such communication does not disclose classified or law enforcement sensitive material.

sections.heading: The Director may issue Public Intelligence Reports, summarizing declassified information or gen
sections.text: The Director may issue Public Intelligence Reports, summarizing declassified information or general security assessments, to inform the public while preserving operational confidentiality.

sections.heading: The Director shall ensure that declassification decisions are documented, justified, and archiv
sections.text:
The Director shall ensure that declassification decisions are documented, justified, and archived within the Director of State Intelligence’s central records system.

(a) The Governor retains the authority to review, reverse, or delay any declassification decision where national or state security interests require continued secrecy

sections.heading: The Office of Oversight and Compliance is hereby established within the Office of State Intelli
sections.text: The Office of Oversight and Compliance is hereby established within the Office of State Intelligence to monitor, audit, and evaluate intelligence and investigative activities across all agencies.

sections.heading: The Office of Oversight and Compliance shall ensure all operations comply with state law, ethic
sections.text: The Office of Oversight and Compliance shall ensure all operations comply with state law, ethical standards, and internal regulations.

sections.heading: The Office of Oversight and Compliance shall investigate any allegations of abuse of authority,
sections.text: The Office of Oversight and Compliance shall investigate any allegations of abuse of authority, corruption, or unauthorized surveillance and report findings directly to the State Intelligence Director and the Governor.

sections.heading: The Director shall appoint a Chief Inspector for the Office of Oversight and Compliance, subjec
sections.text: The Director shall appoint a Chief Inspector for the Office of Oversight and Compliance, subject to gubernatorial approval.

sections.heading: The Director shall ensure all intelligence data is stored within secured state-operated systems
sections.text: The Director shall ensure all intelligence data is stored within secured state-operated systems under encryption standards determined by the Director of State Intelligence.

sections.heading: Unauthorized duplication, distribution, or deletion of classified records shall constitute an a
sections.text: Unauthorized duplication, distribution, or deletion of classified records shall constitute an act of tampering and result in disciplinary or criminal referral.

sections.heading: A centralized digital audit trail shall be maintained to track all access to classified materia
sections.text: A centralized digital audit trail shall be maintained to track all access to classified materials.

sections.heading: The Director shall conduct periodic audits of classified information handling to ensure complia
sections.text: The Director shall conduct periodic audits of classified information handling to ensure compliance across all state entities.

sections.heading: The Director may convene a Confidential Intelligence Advisory Council, consisting of senior off
sections.text: The Director may convene a Confidential Intelligence Advisory Council, consisting of senior officials from state defense, law enforcement, and legal offices, to provide guidance on long-term intelligence strategy.

sections.heading: The Council shall meet at least once per quarter or as directed by the Director or Governor
sections.text: The Council shall meet at least once per quarter or as directed by the Director or Governor.

sections.heading: The Director of State Intelligence shall establish and oversee interagency training programs to
sections.text:
The Director of State Intelligence shall establish and oversee interagency training programs to standardize intelligence operations, improve security awareness, and ensure adherence to classified handling procedures.

(a) All agencies engaged in intelligence or investigative work shall participate in such training as required by the Director of State Intelligence.

sections.heading: LONG TITLE
sections.text: LONG TITLE. An act to Balance Investigations, Surveillance, and Oversight for National Security.

sections.heading: SHORT TITLE
sections.text: SHORT TITLE. This chapter may be cited as the "BISONS Act.

sections.heading: The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authorit
sections.text:
The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authority to designate an organization, association, group of individuals, or individual, whether formal or informal, as a Terrorist Organization, with the advice and consent of the Attorney General, if:

(a) the Terrorist Organization conducts terrorist activity, or attempts to commit or commits the act of Treason, supported with articulable evidence; or

(b) it is an organization, association, or group of two or more individuals which acts in conjunction with a Terrorist Organization, supported with articulable evidence; and

(c) it poses a direct threat to the safety and security of the State, supported with articulable evidence; or

(d) it poses a direct threat to the interests of the State, supported with articulable evidence.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2201. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authorit
sections.text:
The Governor and Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation shall each have the authority to designate an organization, association, group of individuals, or individual, whether formal or informal, as a Terrorist Organization, with the advice and consent of the Secretary of State, if:

(a) the State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization conducts terrorist activity, or attempts to commit or commits the act of Insurrection, supported with articulable evidence; or

(b) it is an organization, association, or group of two or more individuals which acts in conjunction with a State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, supported with articulable evidence, supported with articulable evidence; and

(c) it is sponsored by a foreign government, supported with articulable evidence; and

(d) it poses a direct threat to the safety and security of the State, supported with articulable evidence; or

(e) it poses a direct threat to the interests of the State, supported with articulable evidence.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2202. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Secretary of State shall maintain a database of all Terrorist Organizations and State-Spons
sections.text: The Secretary of State shall maintain a database of all Terrorist Organizations and State-Sponsored Terrorist Organizations.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2203. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: For the purposes of this act, the term ‘terrorist activity’ shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this act, the term ‘terrorist activity’ shall be defined as:

(a) The act of committing Criminal Anarchy.

(b) The act of detonating an explosive at an official state event.

(c) The act of being in unlawful possession of a self-propelled explosive.

(d) The pattern of coordinated mass violence over a period of 72 hours.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited to employ any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or Stat
sections.text: It shall be prohibited to employ any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.

sections.heading: Any person who partakes in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization,
sections.text:
Any person who partakes in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, shall be disqualified from holding an office of trust or profit in the State of Mayflower for a duration as designated by the Governor.

(a) The Governor shall reasonably determine what offices are cabinet positions.

(b) The Governor may, with advice from the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation and articulable evidence that the individual is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, require a person to complete a counterintelligence assessment before a disqualification or employment prohibition is lifted.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2302. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: A database shall be maintained by the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation containing all persons
sections.text: A database shall be maintained by the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation containing all persons who have been disqualified from office under this legislation.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2303. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Any individual who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organiz
sections.text: Any individual who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be prohibited from being within 20 studs of any Airport or Heliport, or board an aircraft.

sections.heading: Any law enforcement officer with an active burn permit shall be further authorized to execute a
sections.text:
Any law enforcement officer with an active burn permit shall be further authorized to execute a controlled burn on vehicles used by a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization which are utilized to further any crime. Furthermore, Guardsmen may execute controlled burns on vehicles used by a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization when it is utilized to effectuate an attack on a guardsman or any military installation. This provision shall only take effect when authorized by the—

(a) Governor;

(b) Attorney General; or

(c) Director of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation if it is a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2305. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited for a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Or
sections.text: It shall be prohibited for a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to be issued a firearms license, and any active firearms license must be revoked.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited for a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Or
sections.text: It shall be prohibited for a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to be issued a pilot's license of any kind, and any active pilot’s license must be revoked.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited for three or more members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored
sections.text: It shall be prohibited for three or more members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to loiter if the purpose or effect of that behavior is to enable a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to establish control over identifiable areas, to intimidate others from entering those areas, or to conceal illegal activities.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited to display methods of joining, or participating in, a Terrorist Organiza
sections.text: It shall be prohibited to display methods of joining, or participating in, a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization through the use of advertisement boards.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited for members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Org
sections.text: It shall be prohibited for members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to own leased property within the State. Any leased property owned by a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be seized by the State.

sections.heading: There shall exist a “Terrorist Removal Court,” whose membership shall be composed of Judges, Ju
sections.text:
There shall exist a “Terrorist Removal Court,” whose membership shall be composed of Judges, Justices, or Magistrates of the State of Mayflower as assigned by the Chief Justice.

(a) The Chief Justice may assign retired justices and retired judges in active service to serve on the Court.

sections.heading: It shall be the duty of the Attorney General, upon affidavit showing good cause therefor, to in
sections.text: It shall be the duty of the Attorney General, upon affidavit showing good cause therefor, to institute proceedings in the Alien Terrorist Removal Court for the purpose of revoking and setting aside the order admitting such person to citizenship and canceling the certificate of naturalization on the ground that such order and certificate of naturalization were illegally procured or were procured by concealment of a material fact or by willful misrepresentation, or that the holder of the certificate of naturalization is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, and such revocation and setting aside of the order admitting such person to citizenship and such canceling of certificate of naturalization shall be effective as of the original date of the order and certificate, respectively.

sections.heading: As applied in this section, “good cause” shall refer to
sections.text:
As applied in this section, “good cause” shall refer to:

(a) The resident whose denaturalization is sought has been a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization.

sections.heading: The Union of Columbia Immigrations and Customs Force shall cooperate with the State of Mayflowe
sections.text: The Union of Columbia Immigrations and Customs Force shall cooperate with the State of Mayflower in the removal of such individuals.

sections.heading: This section shall not be construed to inhibit the power of the Governor to deport any resident
sections.text: This section shall not be construed to inhibit the power of the Governor to deport any resident of the State, for any reason not prohibited by law.

sections.heading: Financial bank records of individuals who are a member of a—
sections.text:
Financial bank records of individuals who are a member of a—

(a) Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization may be subpoenaed by the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2501. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may conduct covert searches of property belonging to a me
sections.text:
The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may conduct covert searches of property belonging to a member of a Terrorist Orgaization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, when approved in the same manner as a regular search warrant.

(a) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may temporarily commandeer vehicles owned by the target of the covert search for the purpose of this provision.

(b) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may delay notifying the target of the covert search, and providing the search receipt, for up to 14 days after the execution of the covert search, as decided by the judge who authorized the covert search warrant.

(c) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation must notify the Senate Standing Committee on Military & Intelligence Affairs prior to its execution.

(d) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may not be authorized to seize any items, regardless of its legality, except for firearms and explosives.

(e) The Mayflower Bureau of Investigation may temporarily detain the target of the covert search in order to execute such a search.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2502. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Every month, the designated Senate Standing Committee shall review the implementation of this A
sections.text: Every month, the designated Senate Standing Committee shall review the implementation of this Act to ensure that there is no abuse of power. If there is no such Senate Standing Committee, the Senate as a whole shall be responsible for the review of the implementation of this act.

sections.heading: The Department of State and Department of Justice shall each have an Inspector General who shal
sections.text: The Department of State and Department of Justice shall each have an Inspector General who shall do independent audits of their respective departments implementation of this act.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2702. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Governor, or a designated executive official, shall inform the State Legislature of all for
sections.text: The Governor, or a designated executive official, shall inform the State Legislature of all foreign intelligence operations conducted by the State, including details on objectives, scope, and outcomes, subject to applicable classification restrictions.

sections.heading: The Governor, or a designated executive official, shall inform the State Legislature of all dom
sections.text: The Governor, or a designated executive official, shall inform the State Legislature of all domestic intelligence operations conducted by the State, including details on objectives, scope, and outcomes, subject to applicable classification restrictions.

sections.heading: Any person who participates in or incites an armed rebellion or violent resistance against the
sections.text: Any person who participates in or incites an armed rebellion or violent resistance against the government or laws of the state shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1106 Insurrection.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2801. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who participates in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organizati
sections.text: Any person who participates in a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2802. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who directs or organizes a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organ
sections.text: Any person who directs or organizes a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 5104 Direction of a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2803. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who gives material or financial support to a Terrorist Organization or a State-Spons
sections.text: Any person who gives material or financial support to a Terrorist Organization or a State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, or violates Section VI of this act, shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 5105 Supporting a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2804. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: If two or more members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization ar
sections.text: If two or more members of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization are conducting crime together, or aiding each other to do crime, they shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2805. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organizatio
sections.text: Any person who is a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization and is in possession of a firearm shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 6102 Unlicensed possession of a firearm.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2806. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who loiters with two or more other individuals who are a member of a Terrorist Organ
sections.text: Any person who loiters with two or more other individuals who are a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, while also being a member of a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization themself, if the purpose or effect of that behavior is to enable a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization to establish control over identifiable areas, to intimidate others from entering those areas, or to conceal illegal activities, and who ignores an order to disperse from a peace officer, shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 4105 Unlawful assembly.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2807. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any person who utilizes advertisement boards in order to display how to join, or how to partici
sections.text: Any person who utilizes advertisement boards in order to display how to join, or how to participate in, a Terrorist Organization or State-Sponsored Terrorist Organization, shall be subject to arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 5103 Engagement in a Terrorist Organization.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2808. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual who, owing allegiance to a foreign nation state, participates in acts of war aga
sections.text: Any individual who, owing allegiance to a foreign nation state, participates in acts of war against the State shall be liable for conviction and arrest for 1 M.S.C. § 1107 Participation of War as a Foreign Actor.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2809. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The Governor shall have the power to temporarily deport the following officials of a Foreign Na
sections.text:
The Governor shall have the power to temporarily deport the following officials of a Foreign Nation-State during a state of war that has been declared on them:

(a) State Governor and Lieutenant Governor, or its equivalents.

(b) Secretary of State, or its equivalent.

(c) Members of their State Legislature, or its equivalents.

(d) Head and deputy head of their military body.

(e) Head and deputy head of their intelligence body.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 2 § 2901. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: No individual shall be deported unless they
sections.text:
No individual shall be deported unless they:

(a) Have been convicted of a crime under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter I of the Mayflower Criminal Code.

(b) Are a member of a military or intelligence organization of a Nation-State which Mayflower is at war with.

(c) Are sentenced to death.

sections.heading: This section shall not be construed to inhibit the power of any other act, law, or provision wh
sections.text: This section shall not be construed to inhibit the power of any other act, law, or provision which permits deportations for any reason not prohibited by law.

sections.heading: The term “Presiding Officer” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “Presiding Officer” shall refer to:

(a) The President of the Senate or, in the absence of the President, the President pro tempore to a convened session of the Senate at-large; and

(b) The chair of a Standing Senate Committee or any member designated by the chair to preside in the chair’s absence to a convened meeting of a Standing Senate Committee.

sections.heading: The term “convened Senate or Senate Committee” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “convened Senate or Senate Committee” shall refer to:

(a) A session of the Senate at-large, who are present and roll called to be in session; or

(b) A hearing, session, or meeting of any Standing Senate Committee who are present and roll called to be in session and convened.

sections.heading: The term “Sergeant-at-Arms” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “Sergeant-at-Arms” shall refer to:

(a) Any state-certified peace officer who is currently employed in a law enforcement agency, who is in good standing with the agency, and who is appointed by the President of the Senate to head the Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms, or the deputies under the Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms appointed by the Sergeant-at-Arms.

sections.heading: The term “gallery” shall refer to
sections.text: The term “gallery” shall refer to:

sections.heading: Any area within the Senate chamber or committee room designated for public observation of proce
sections.text: (a) Any area within the Senate chamber or committee room designated for public observation of proceedings.

sections.heading: The term “classified information” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “classified information” shall refer to:

(a) Any information to be means any information that is classified as:

(i) "Top Secret" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a);

(ii) "Secret" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(b); or

(iii) "Confidential" under 4 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(c).
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1105. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: A convened Senate or Senate Committee may, by resolution—
sections.text:
A convened Senate or Senate Committee may, by resolution—

(a) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1502, "Contempt of Senate," if the individual:

(i) Does not comply with a subpoena, writ, or order issued by a convened Senate or Senate Committee; or

(ii) Willfully obstructs a convened Senate or Senate Committee while it conducts an investigation, inquiry, or legislative action.

(b) And decide on a reasonable punishment as dictated by the Mayflower Criminal Code.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Should a resolution pass, the Sergeant-at-Arms of the Mayflower Legislature shall be responsibl
sections.text: Should a resolution pass, the Sergeant-at-Arms of the Mayflower Legislature shall be responsible for the serving of the resolution.

sections.heading: The Presiding Officer of a convened Senate or Senate Committee, without a resolution, may direc
sections.text:
The Presiding Officer of a convened Senate or Senate Committee, without a resolution, may direct the Sergeant-at-arms to—

(a) Remove any individual from the chamber, committee room, gallery, or any area under Senate control, if the individual:

(i) Disrupts a convened Senate or Senate Committee or its functions; acts disorderly therein; or, after having been removed previously therefrom by the Sergeant-at-Arms returns to the chamber or committee room during that same convened session.

(ii) A sudden disruptive demonstration occurs in the gallery, to which only the participating demonstrators may be cleared from the floor.

(b) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1502, "Contempt of Senate or 1 M.S.C. § 1506, "Disorderly Conduct before the Senate” if the individual:

(i) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(i)

(ii) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(ii)

(c) Clear the gallery of a convened Senate or Senate Committee and seal it if:

(i) A sudden reveal of classified information has occurred in a convened Senate or Senate Committee to which the public are present.

(ii) Commits the acts listed in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1201(a)(ii)

(d) Hold an individual in violation of 1 M.S.C. § 1318, "Obstruction of Senate", if the individual commits the acts defined in 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1303.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 3 § 1301. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual(s) removed or held in contempt under this subchapter may file a written appeal t
sections.text: Any individual(s) removed or held in contempt under this subchapter may file a written appeal to the Standing Senate Committee on Ethics within forty-eight (48) hours; the appeal shall not stay the removal, citation, or arrest unless the committee votes in a two-thirds majority to stay it pending review.

sections.heading: Any person who knowingly and willfully
sections.text: Any person who knowingly and willfully; influences, obstructs, or impedes, or endeavors to influence, obstruct, or impede, the due exercise of the Senate's powers, including any inquiry, investigation, or proceeding; corruptly alters, destroys, mutilates, or conceals any document, record, or evidence with intent to impair its integrity or availability for use in a Senate proceeding; fails to comply with a lawful subpoena, order, or writ issued by the Senate; obstructs, hinders, or impedes the Sergeant-at-arms in the course of their duties as instructed by the Presiding Officer, or by resolution; intimidates, threatens, or corruptly persuades another person, or attempts to do so, with intent to influence, delay, or prevent testimony or the production of evidence in a Senate proceeding; or provided false, misleading, or incomplete information to the Senate with intent to deceive or obstruct shall be guilty of "Obstruction of Senate"

sections.heading: The State Legislature may, by resolution, refer to the Committee on State Security to initiate
sections.text:
The State Legislature may, by resolution, refer to the Committee on State Security to initiate an investigation into any activities of the National Guard that the State Legislature determines may exceed statutory authority, pose risks to public safety, or warrant legislative review due to suspected irregularities or concerns.

(a) Such investigations may include, but are not limited to:

(i) Review of deployment records, operational reports, and incident summaries.

(ii) Subpoena of witnesses, documents, or other evidence related to Guard activities.

(iii) Hearings on matters involving potential civilian impacts, operational overreach, or compliance with state law.

sections.heading: The Governor, the Adjutant General of the National Guard, and other relevant military officials
sections.text: The Governor, the Adjutant General of the National Guard, and other relevant military officials shall cooperate fully with any such investigation, providing timely access to information unless prohibited by state law or state security classifications.

sections.heading: “Commission” means the State Archive Commission created under this Act
sections.text: “Commission” means the State Archive Commission created under this Act.

sections.heading: “State Archivist” means the chief executive officer of the Commission
sections.text: “State Archivist” means the chief executive officer of the Commission.

sections.heading: “Archive” means any record, document, file, communication, digital item, or preserved material
sections.text: “Archive” means any record, document, file, communication, digital item, or preserved material under the custody of the Commission.

sections.heading: “Restricted Archive” means any record designated as restricted by the State Archivist pursuant
sections.text: “Restricted Archive” means any record designated as restricted by the State Archivist pursuant to this Act. A restricted archive is one which can not be publicly accessible.

sections.heading: “Reasonable period of time” means a timeframe determined by the State Archivist and communicate
sections.text: “Reasonable period of time” means a timeframe determined by the State Archivist and communicated in writing to the person or office required to submit materials.

sections.heading: There shall be an established independent government agency known as the “State Archive Commiss
sections.text: There shall be an established independent government agency known as the “State Archive Commission”.

sections.heading: The “State Archive Commission” shall only report to the Senate Committee on Ethics when formall
sections.text: The “State Archive Commission” shall only report to the Senate Committee on Ethics when formally requested.

sections.heading: The commission shall be directed by the “State Archivist" who shall be recommended by the gover
sections.text: The commission shall be directed by the “State Archivist" who shall be recommended by the governor, with the advice and consent of the Mayflower State Senate. The “State Archivist" holds the authority to manage operations, archiving and all affairs of the commission

sections.heading: The State Archivist may appoint employees and administrative officers as necessary for the oper
sections.text: The State Archivist may appoint employees and administrative officers as necessary for the operation of the Commission and shall supervise their performance.

sections.heading: If any required office or position becomes vacant, the State Archivist shall assume the respons
sections.text: If any required office or position becomes vacant, the State Archivist shall assume the responsibilities of that office until it is filled.

sections.heading: The State Archivist shall appoint the following officers to assist in fulfilling Commission dut
It shall be the responsibility of the State Archivist to maintain a platform where all archives
sections.text: It shall be the responsibility of the State Archivist to maintain a platform where all archives can be placed.

sections.heading: The State Archivist may classify any archive or item as “Restricted” if
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the legislative under each congress. This includes; bills, members, record of senate officers, and all other information authorised by the State Archivist.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require a member of the senate, or a senate officer to submit all required materials to the state archive.

(b) Any member of the senate, or a senate officer may submit a request to the State Archivist to send, or archive requested materials.

sections.heading: There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of all pardons, reprieves and commutations.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

sections.heading: There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of medals or commendations awarded by the Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of State, and the Order of Mayflower.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

(b) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require any government official or citizen, to submit all required materials to the state archive which is in regards to medals or commendations awarded.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 3 M.S.C. 3 § 2403. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the Supreme Court and District Court. This includes; opinions and rulings, orders and judgments, court administrative records or other information authorised by the State Archivist.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the Chief Judge of the District, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

sections.heading: There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the governor. This includes; works and records of Governors, and all other information authorised by the State Archivist.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

sections.heading: There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the de
sections.text:
There shall be an established archive, maintained and managed by the State Archivist, or the designated office which shall keep a record of business completed by the governor. This includes; all oaths of office for elected officers or officers appointed by the Governor, and all other information authorised by the State Archivist.

(a) The State Archivist, shall uphold the authority to require the governor, or a delegate to submit all required materials to the state archive.

(b) It lays the responsibility of the governor, or a delegate to inform and submit all required information to the State Archive Commission within a reasonable period of time.

sections.heading: The State Archivist may authorise the establishment of further archived materials or items
sections.text: The State Archivist may authorise the establishment of further archived materials or items. The State Archivist, requires any citizen, or government official (or a delegate) to submit required information requested by the State Archive Commission.

sections.heading: The "Guard" shall be known as the Mayflower National Guard, or any known variation thereof
sections.text: The "Guard" shall be known as the Mayflower National Guard, or any known variation thereof.

sections.heading: The Adjutant General shall be defined as the head of the Mayflower National Guard
sections.text: The Adjutant General shall be defined as the head of the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: The Deputy Adjutant General shall be defined as the deputy head of the Mayflower National Guard
sections.text: The Deputy Adjutant General shall be defined as the deputy head of the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: Command Group shall be defined as the central command of the Mayflower National Guard designate
sections.text: Command Group shall be defined as the central command of the Mayflower National Guard designated by the Adjutant General and the Deputy Adjutant General.

sections.heading: Senior Officer shall be defined as any guardsman at or above the rank of O4/Major within the Ma
sections.text: Senior Officer shall be defined as any guardsman at or above the rank of O4/Major within the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: Defense Policy shall be defined as any official written policy instituted by the Adjutant Gener
sections.text: Defense Policy shall be defined as any official written policy instituted by the Adjutant General, the Deputy Adjutant General, or any member of Command Group.

sections.heading: The terms ‘on-duty guardsman,’ ‘guardsman’ and ‘active duty’ for the purposes of this document
sections.text: The terms ‘on-duty guardsman,’ ‘guardsman’ and ‘active duty’ for the purposes of this document shall refer to persons that are on the Mayflower Army National Guard team in-game and actively serving or representing the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subtitle, ‘Misconduct’ or ‘Mishandling’ of proceedings shall be define
sections.text: For the purposes of this subtitle, ‘Misconduct’ or ‘Mishandling’ of proceedings shall be defined as any unethical overtures, instances of corruption or favor based on status, failing to include reasonable arguments and/or evidence, failing to file charges for reported incidents, or other such instances as one may reasonably believe to be prosecutorial misconduct.

sections.heading: In this subtitle, a Military Installation means any of the following properties below
In this subtitle, the "Military Exclusion Zone" or "MEZ" shall be defined as the land surroundi
sections.text:
In this subtitle, the "Military Exclusion Zone" or "MEZ" shall be defined as the land surrounding the Fort Standish and Camp Bryant properties within the perimeter formed by appropriate signage and/or perimeter fencing.

(a) This shall extend to any river or stream directly below a perimeter fence or posted sign and open water within 1000 studs of any perimeter fence or posted sign.

sections.heading: Unauthorized individual” shall refer to any individual who enters a Military Exclusion Zone whi
sections.text: Unauthorized individual” shall refer to any individual who enters a Military Exclusion Zone while not explicitly authorized by an on-duty Senior Officer, or Military Police Officer to enter that Military Exclusion Zone.

sections.heading: “Drawn firearm” shall refer to any firearm that is being held using at least one hand and is no
sections.text: “Drawn firearm” shall refer to any firearm that is being held using at least one hand and is not contained wholly within a storage device.

sections.heading: A “Military Arrest Order (‘MAO’)” shall be defined as
sections.text:
A “Military Arrest Order (‘MAO’)” shall be defined as:

(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person arrested for a specific charge that falls under military jurisdiction.

sections.heading: A “Military Seizure Order (‘MSO’)” shall be defined as
sections.text:
A “Military Seizure Order (‘MSO’)” shall be defined as:

(a) Any issued order, by a sitting Judge within the State of Mayflower, to have a person and/or their property inspected for any military property to be seized, or any other articles that fall under military jurisdiction.

sections.heading: The term “Military Housing” or “Military Home” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “Military Housing” or “Military Home” shall refer to:

(a) “Any Residential Property within a Military Exclusion Zone, as defined within Title 3, Chapter VII of the Mayflower State Code.”

sections.heading: The term Forward Operating Base or FOB shall be defined as the public land temporarily utilized
sections.text: The term Forward Operating Base or FOB shall be defined as the public land temporarily utilized by the National Guard as a military base.

sections.heading: Militia shall refer to an organisation of civilians who wish to exercise their 2nd Amendment ri
sections.text: Militia shall refer to an organisation of civilians who wish to exercise their 2nd Amendment rights in a regulated manner.

sections.heading: A General Officer shall refer to an individual holding the rank of Brigadier General or higher,
sections.text: A General Officer shall refer to an individual holding the rank of Brigadier General or higher, excluding the Commander-in-Chief.

sections.heading: Honor Guard shall refer to the ceremonial unit established and maintained by the Mayflower Nati
sections.text: Honor Guard shall refer to the ceremonial unit established and maintained by the Mayflower National Guard pursuant to 3 M.S.C. 4 § 8101, tasked with rendering honors at official events and state functions, safeguarding designated sites, and upholding ceremonial drill proficiency.
