sections.text: “Senior Member” shall refer to any member of a Criminal Organization who holds a position of command in such an organization and is capable of directing subordinates to take part in organized criminal activity.

sections.heading: The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Criminal Organizat
sections.text: The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Criminal Organization as he deems fit and appropriate, however such orders may be overturned by the Governor (with such overturns being open to counter-overturning by the Senate).

sections.heading: The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Criminal O
sections.text: The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Criminal Organization, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of senior criminals.

sections.heading: The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Street Gang as he
sections.text: The Attorney General shall have the power to designate any organization as a Street Gang as he deems fit and appropriate.

sections.heading: The Attorney General shall maintain an up-to-date, publicly available database displaying infor
sections.text: The Attorney General shall maintain an up-to-date, publicly available database displaying information pertaining to Street Gangs, their operations and their known members.

sections.heading: The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Street Gan
sections.text: The Governor shall wield the power to revoke the residency of any senior member of a Street Gang, with the advice of the State Security Council and other such advisors with knowledge as to the capabilities and identities of such Street Gang leaders.

sections.heading: This chapter is established to provide provisional laws pertaining to the authority, training,
sections.text: This chapter is established to provide provisional laws pertaining to the authority, training, and accountability of private security firms and the services which they provide.

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as the “Security Services Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as the “Security Services Act.”

sections.heading: A proprietary security guard shall be defined as an employee who is employed exclusively by any
sections.text: A proprietary security guard shall be defined as an employee who is employed exclusively by any one employer whose primary duty is to provide security services for his or her employer, whose services are not contracted out to any other entity.

sections.heading: A proprietary private security employer shall be defined as a person who has one or more employ
sections.text: A proprietary private security employer shall be defined as a person who has one or more employees who provide security services for the employer and only the employer. A person who employs proprietary security guards pursuant to this definition at more than one location owned and operated by the employer shall still be considered a single employer

sections.heading: A security guard or security officer shall be defined as an employee of a private patrol operat
sections.text: A security guard or security officer shall be defined as an employee of a private patrol operator who is licensed to and performs the duties of a private patrol operator in compliance with the provisions of this Chapter.

sections.heading: A private patrol operator and or any other variation thereof shall be defined as a person and o
sections.text: A private patrol operator and or any other variation thereof shall be defined as a person and or organization, who, for any consideration whatsoever; agrees to furnish, or furnishes a security officer or guard, or other person to protect persons or property to prevent the theft, loss, embezzlement, or concealment of any goods, merchandise, money, or property of any kind; or performs the service of a security officer or guard for any of these purposes.

sections.heading: The Department of State shall form a commission responsible for the enforcement of the provisio
sections.text: The Department of State shall form a commission responsible for the enforcement of the provisions of this Chapter. Furthermore this commission shall be uniquely responsible for the issuance, suspension, and revocation of security licenses in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1301. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Department of State shall draft, maintain and issue an examination of which the passing of
sections.text: The Department of State shall draft, maintain and issue an examination of which the passing of shall be required for an individual to acquire a security license from the Department of State.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1302. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Department of State shall be provided a document titled the “Power to Arrest Training Manua
sections.text:
The Department of State shall be provided a document titled the “Power to Arrest Training Manual,” which shall detail the provisions of this Chapter in an attempt to educate those seeking a security license from the Department of State. Using this document, the State Department shall either be responsible for the administration of the required curriculum. Or, they may permit a registered business to do so on behalf of the State, so long as they meet all the same curriculum requirements the Department of State upholds.

(a) The Department of State shall maintain a roster of businesses that have been given permission to render security training.

(b) The Department of State shall maintain a publicly accessible form for businesses to request a training waiver.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1303. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Commission which the State Department designates to oversee the management of security lice
sections.text:
The Commission which the State Department designates to oversee the management of security license shall be permitted to modify license status only in the following situations:

(a) A security license may be issued only if an individual has completed the required training process and passed the required examination, or otherwise has an exemption provided by this Chapter.

(b) A security license may be suspended if the holder has failed to maintain citizenship status, or is the subject of official investigation by the State Department or the investigative unit of any law enforcement agency, or representative of the Department of Justice.

(c) For a security license to be revoked, the specific license holder must meet one the following criteria:

(i) Previous active conviction in a court of law of any criminal offense other than an infraction.

(ii) Four in total or more active misdemeanor records and/or three in total or more active felony records, of which are not actively being disputed or in the process to do so through a court of law.

(iii) Conviction by a court of a felony violation or multiple (or consecutive) violations of state law within twenty-four (24) hours, where such violations are determined by the Commission.

(iv) Repeated, or serious violation of the Security Services Act or any other private security regulation promulgated by the Department of State.

(d) A security license may be suspended as a result of an investigation conducted by the Department of State for a time specified in the investigation report that does not exceed thirty (30) days.

(i) A security license may be suspended for the duration of a criminal trial in which the holder is charged with any criminal offense other than an infraction.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1304. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: An individual applicant may not be issued a security license by the State Department if the app
sections.text: An individual applicant may not be issued a security license by the State Department if the applicant meets one of the criterion found within 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1304(c) that would normally warrant a license revocation.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1305. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: A license may not be issued to an applicant without active residency
sections.text: A license may not be issued to an applicant without active residency.

sections.heading: The State Department shall be permitted to, on an individual basis, exempt an applicant from th
sections.text: The State Department shall be permitted to, on an individual basis, exempt an applicant from the required training and examination if the applicant is an active peace officer as defined by the State code, or an otherwise honorably discharged person which previously held such a position.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1307. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Training Waiver shall be defined as, “A waiver granted to businesses permitting them to render
sections.text: Training Waiver shall be defined as, “A waiver granted to businesses permitting them to render security training themselves as opposed to through the Department of State.”
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1308. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Any individual seeking employment as a security officer employed by a private patrol operator,
sections.text:
Any individual seeking employment as a security officer employed by a private patrol operator, or wishing to incorporate or otherwise establish an organization defined as a private patrol operator shall be required to maintain an active security license from the Department of State.

(a) Proprietary security guards shall be required to maintain an active security license to carry a firearm while acting in the capacity of a proprietary security guard.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1401. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Previous to being issued a license the applicant shall complete a course of training in the exe
sections.text: Previous to being issued a license the applicant shall complete a course of training in the exercise of the power of arrest, a course in the training of carrying and use of firearms, and the general use of force regarding specialized tools and equipment.

sections.heading: An individual representing the organization of which they are employed and acting in the capaci
sections.text:
An individual representing the organization of which they are employed and acting in the capacity of a security officer or proprietary security guard shall be required to display a unique uniform compliant with this Chapter designated by their employer.

(a) For the purpose of this code, a uniform shall be considered compliant if it aligns with all of the following components:

(i) A uniform which bears at least one patch, badge, ID, logo, or otherwise emblem visible at all times clearly identifying the employing company.

(ii) Authorized officers may perform duties regulated under this chapter in 'non uniformed' status on a limited special assignment basis, and only when duty circumstances or special requirements of the client necessitate such dress. Licensees who are performing bodyguard or executive protection services may choose to carry their authorized equipment while in non uniformed status as needed in the conduct of such services.

(b) Security officers and or proprietary security guards which fail to comply with the uniform mandate shall not receive any protection or exemption by the provisions of this act.

sections.heading: A licensed private security officer or licensed proprietary security guard which has in their p
sections.text: A licensed private security officer or licensed proprietary security guard which has in their possession a valid firearms license shall be permitted to carry and display in public and/or in a restricted or otherwise firearms freezone, if the aforementioned restricted or otherwise firearms freezone is within the reasonable scope of their duties, a loaded firearm.

sections.heading: A licensed security officer shall be permitted to carry on their person and utilize, when on du
sections.text: A licensed security officer shall be permitted to carry on their person and utilize, when on duty and conducting official security duties, and in accordance with provisions of State law the following articles of equipment and their respective ammunition or otherwise essential components; extendable, fixed and straight batons, stun guns or taser devices, pepper-spray or other similar chemical self-defense items, encrypted handheld radios, fixed or chain connected handcuffs; and the Bennetti 17 pistol.

sections.heading: A private security officer specifically directed to do so by an on-duty peace officer as define
sections.text: A private security officer specifically directed to do so by an on-duty peace officer as defined by the State Code may be permitted to assist in the detainment, arrest, or capture of a criminal wrongdoer; however, security officers shall never, under any circumstances, be authorized to engage or assist directly or indirectly, in a vehicular pursuit. Private security officers may be permitted to close or block public roadways if authorized to do so by an on-duty supervisor of a law enforcement agency to ensure public safety during significant emergencies.

sections.heading: A security officer may only protect an asset, property or person when the security entity they
sections.text: A security officer may only protect an asset, property or person when the security entity they are employed by has a contract or signed agreement to protect such asset, property or person and said security officer is authorized by his employer to provide such protective services.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this Subchapter, the term “authorized officer” shall be defined as a securi
sections.text: For the purposes of this Subchapter, the term “authorized officer” shall be defined as a security officer, or proprietary security guard.

sections.heading: Peace officers defined by the State code discharging the authority of arrest on behalf of the S
sections.text: Peace officers defined by the State code discharging the authority of arrest on behalf of the State involved in the secondary duty of an authorized officer shall be exempt from the provisions of this Subchapter.

sections.heading: An authorized officer shall be permitted to hold an individual within their custody only under
sections.text:
An authorized officer shall be permitted to hold an individual within their custody only under the following conditions:

(a) For an codified offense of the State code punishable by arrest committed or attempted within the presence of an authorized officer.

(b) For a codified felony offense of the State code which the authorized officer has evidence of such an offense although not not committed within their presence.

(c) When ordered to do so by a peace officer as defined by the State code. Such a detention shall be considered an action on behalf of the peace officer rather than the authorized officer.

sections.heading: Upon effecting an arrest, an authorized officer shall be required to contact a peace officer wi
sections.text: Upon effecting an arrest, an authorized officer shall be required to contact a peace officer within a reasonable timeframe to take custody of the violator and provide the peace officer with evidence of the offense which the individual was arrested for.

sections.heading: An authorized officer shall have the sole authority to conduct an arrest with reasonable and pl
sections.text: An authorized officer shall have the sole authority to conduct an arrest with reasonable and plausible cause to do so. Upon affecting an arrest a authorized officer may not release a violator unless ordered to do so by a peace officer or due to emergent circumstances. Unlike a peace officer, an authorized officer shall not be permitted to detain a person for investigative purposes, and as such may only hold a person within their custody to effect an arrest.

sections.heading: Upon an arrest being effected, an authorized officer must immediately inform the individual whi
sections.text: Upon an arrest being effected, an authorized officer must immediately inform the individual which is within their custody of the crime which they are being arrested for, and their authority to do so.

sections.heading: An authorized officer attempting to effect an arrest may utilize handcuffs or similar devices t
sections.text: An authorized officer attempting to effect an arrest may utilize handcuffs or similar devices to hold an individual within their custody. Furthermore authorized officers shall be permitted to use a reasonable amount of force to prevent the evasion, or resistance of such an arrest.

sections.heading: An authorized officer may transit an arrested individual within their custody to a holding room
sections.text: An authorized officer may transit an arrested individual within their custody to a holding room or hold them within a marked security vehicle whilst awaiting peace officer arrival.

sections.heading: An authorized officer may search the person of an arrested individual though may only remove we
sections.text: An authorized officer may search the person of an arrested individual though may only remove weapons, and must transfer seized items to a peace officer upon arrival. Additionally an authorized officer may search the person of any individual which consents to such a search.

sections.heading: The authority granted under 4 M
sections.text:
The authority granted under 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1603 (a) and (b) shall only be exercised under the following conditions:

(a) The authorized officer is actively engaged in the protection of a contracted property, person, or asset, and is either on, in, or in the immediate vicinity of that property, person, or asset; or

(b) When not in the immediate vicinity of a property, person, or asset they are contracted and authorized to protect, but during exigent circumstances to protect human life. This subsection shall not be construed to allow authorized officers to patrol or seek out criminal wrongdoers not within the scope of their official security duties to protect a contracted property, asset, or person.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1610. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual who without a license attempts to, or operates a private patrol operator service
sections.text: Any individual who without a license attempts to, or operates a private patrol operator service shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business” and/or 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer” if applicable.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1701. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any private patrol operator which knowingly employs an individual without a security license as
sections.text: Any private patrol operator which knowingly employs an individual without a security license as a security officer within their organization shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1406 “Unlawful Operation of a Business.“
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1702. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual which acts in the capacity of a security officer without having in their possess
sections.text: Any individual which acts in the capacity of a security officer without having in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 1318 “Impersonation of a Private Security Officer."
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1703. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: A proprietary security guard which carries on their person a firearm whilst representing the pr
sections.text: A proprietary security guard which carries on their person a firearm whilst representing the proprietary security employer and does not have in their possession an active security license shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 6102 “Unlicensed Possession of a Firearm.”
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1704. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual which attempts to exercise the exemptions or authority of a security officer, pr
sections.text: Any individual which attempts to exercise the exemptions or authority of a security officer, proprietary security guard, or private patrol operator without total compliance with the provisions of this Chapter shall receive no exemption or protection from liability which is found therein.

sections.heading: An act to establish regulations around financial reporting for larger companies within the Stat
sections.text: An act to establish regulations around financial reporting for larger companies within the State of Mayflower and implementing financial crimes within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

sections.heading: this act may be cited as "The Second Finance Act
sections.text: this act may be cited as "The Second Finance Act."

sections.heading: A fiscal period is a single month, starting on the first of the month and ending the last day o
sections.text: A fiscal period is a single month, starting on the first of the month and ending the last day of the month.

sections.heading: A fiscal quarter shall be defined as follows, with the quarter starting on the first day of the
sections.text:
A fiscal quarter shall be defined as follows, with the quarter starting on the first day of the specified month and ending on the last day of the other specified month:

(a) Quarter 1: October to December.

(b) Quarter 2: January to March.

(c) Quarter 3: April to June.

(d) Quarter 4: July to September.

sections.heading: A fiscal year shall be defined as the 12-month period beginning 1 October and ending 30 Septemb
sections.text: A fiscal year shall be defined as the 12-month period beginning 1 October and ending 30 September the following year.

sections.heading: References for fiscal years shall be made as “The [fiscal/financial] year of [the calendar year
sections.text: References for fiscal years shall be made as “The [fiscal/financial] year of [the calendar year the fiscal year started in]”.

sections.heading: The term "commercial instrument" shall be defined to mean any document or item utilized in the
sections.text: The term "commercial instrument" shall be defined to mean any document or item utilized in the course of commercial transactions or business operations that holds legal or financial significance that evidences, constitutes, or facilitates a business or financial transaction.

sections.heading: All Financial Statements that are required by law must meet requirements adopted by the Governo
sections.text:
All Financial Statements that are required by law must meet requirements adopted by the Governor’s Office.

(a) The Governor shall be obligated to create a position within his office to accommodate this.

sections.heading: All businesses registered with the Department of State that offer stocks, bonds or investment c
sections.text:
All businesses registered with the Department of State that offer stocks, bonds or investment contracts are obligated to prepare and publish the following financial statements every fiscal quarter:

(a) A Statement of Cash Flows

(b) A Balance Sheet

(c) Income Statement
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 2302. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: All required Financial Statements must be made public within three (3) days of the end of each
sections.text: All required Financial Statements must be made public within three (3) days of the end of each fiscal quarter.

sections.heading: All financial statements submitted to the SEC must be complete and accurate
sections.text: All financial statements submitted to the SEC must be complete and accurate.

sections.heading: CASINO FINANCIALS
sections.text: CASINO FINANCIALS. This chapter/Subchapter of the State Code is established to provide laws pertaining to the oversight, regulation, fairness, transparency, and accountability of Casino and Online Games websites and operations run within, or operating within, the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: Businesses conducting gambling or casino like operations, herein “Casino” must be responsible f
sections.text:
Businesses conducting gambling or casino like operations, herein “Casino” must be responsible for transparency with their financials, and shall be obligated to prepare and publicly announce the following Financial Statements every fiscal quarter:

(a) A Statement of Cash Flows.

(b) A Balance Sheet.

(c) Income Statement.

(d) Ledger of Cash Disbursements.

sections.heading: A Casino may not permit an individual user to withdraw more than $7,000,000 of their deposits/w
sections.text: A Casino may not permit an individual user to withdraw more than $7,000,000 of their deposits/winnings at the casino in a 7 day period.

sections.heading: CONSUMER PROTECTIONS
sections.text: CONSUMER PROTECTIONS. Businesses conducting casino-like operations must be responsible for listing odds for all games. Whether it is in percentile or fraction format, the odds for all games. The odds must be displayed in a manner that a reasonable person would be able to properly read from a reasonable distance.

sections.heading: Casinos must disclose publicly and visibly any and all games in which the “house” or the busine
sections.text: Casinos must disclose publicly and visibly any and all games in which the “house” or the business is favored to win the game, or in other words, where the person has a 49% chance or less to win.

sections.heading: Casinos must publicly report changes in odds, gameplay, or any other mechanic that may alter th
sections.text: Casinos must publicly report changes in odds, gameplay, or any other mechanic that may alter the experience of the casino in any way when the changes are made and in a monthly report. If there is no alteration as described above, a monthly report need not be published.

sections.heading: Any advertisement or promotion for Casinos must provide, in visible font and coloring that a re
sections.text: Any advertisement or promotion for Casinos must provide, in visible font and coloring that a reasonable person can see from a reasonable distance, a support website for chronic gambling addictions.

sections.heading: Should there be discrepancies or inaccuracies the Attorney General or District Attorney should
sections.text: Should there be discrepancies or inaccuracies the Attorney General or District Attorney should direct an investigative agency to investigate the matter.

sections.heading: The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement through civil and/or criminal co
sections.text: The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

sections.heading: Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result
sections.text:
Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

(a) This shall primarily fall under Negligent and Economic Torts but shall not be limited to such.

sections.heading: Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result
sections.text:
Businesses that fail to comply with the prescribed Financial Reporting requirements will result in the business owner(s) being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1406 (Unlawful Operation of a Business) if—

(a) The business in question has been non-compliant with Financial Reporting requirements prescribed by law for a cumulative period of twenty one (30) days.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 2504. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: A new Chapter within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be created
sections.text: A new Chapter within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be created: “Financial Crimes."

sections.heading: All crimes within Section IV of the Financial Reporting and Crimes Act shall be classified as F
sections.text: All crimes within Section IV of the Financial Reporting and Crimes Act shall be classified as Financial Crimes.

sections.heading: The following crimes shall be created and codified within the Mayflower Criminal Code
sections.text: The following crimes shall be created and codified within the Mayflower Criminal Code:

sections.heading: “Bank Robbery” shall be created and defined as follows
sections.text:
“Bank Robbery” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person whether by force or intimidation, that takes any property or money in the care, custody, control, etc. of any bank, credit union, or savings and loan institution.

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 30 minutes in prison.

(c) This statue shall be set to active within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

sections.heading: “Money Laundering” shall be created and defined as follows
“Embezzlement” shall be created and defined as follows
sections.text:
“Embezzlement” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) A person who shall, having lawful custody of property not his or her own, appropriate the same to his or her own use, with intent to deprive the owner thereof;

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 50 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $5,000 or twice the value of the property involved in the transaction, whichever is greater.

(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

sections.heading: “Counterfeiting” shall be created and defined as follows
sections.text:
“Counterfeiting” shall be created and defined as follows:

(a) Any person, with intent to defraud, falsely makes, forges, counterfeits, or alters any obligation or other security of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia;

(b) Shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 120 minutes in prison.

(c) This statue shall be set to By Conviction within the Mayflower Criminal Code.

sections.heading: 1 M
sections.text: 1 M.S.C. § 1301 “Bribery” shall be reclassified as a Financial Crime.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 2608. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: “Loan Sharking” shall be added and defined as follows
sections.text: “Loan Sharking” shall be added and defined as follows: Any Lender who provides a loan not in accordance with Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions shall be guilty of a felony and sentenced to 25 minutes in prison and/or face a fine of not more than $20,000 or twice the value of the loan, whichever is greater.

sections.heading: Commercial instrument falsification in the second degree’ shall be defined as follows
sections.text: Commercial instrument falsification in the second degree’ shall be defined as follows: Any person who, with intent to defraud, knowingly falsifies, alters, or forges any commercial instrument shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

sections.heading: A “Borrower” shall be defined as a person or business who is loaned money from a Lender
sections.text: A “Borrower” shall be defined as a person or business who is loaned money from a Lender.

sections.heading: A “Lender” shall be defined as a business which loans money to a Borrower
sections.text: A “Lender” shall be defined as a business which loans money to a Borrower.

sections.heading: A “loan” shall be defined as a sum of money or other asset provided by a Lender to a Borrower u
sections.text: A “loan” shall be defined as a sum of money or other asset provided by a Lender to a Borrower under an agreement that it will be repaid in the future, typically with interest as compensation for the use of the funds.

sections.heading: An “interest rate” shall be defined as “the percentage charged or paid on the principal amount
sections.text: An “interest rate” shall be defined as “the percentage charged or paid on the principal amount of a loan or deposit, calculated over a specified period, as agreed between the Lender and Borrower or deposit holder and institution.”

sections.heading: A “collateral” shall be defined as an asset or property offered by a Borrower to be given to th
sections.text: A “collateral” shall be defined as an asset or property offered by a Borrower to be given to the Lender should the Borrower fail to repay the loan.

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as the "Loan Shark Extinction Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as the "Loan Shark Extinction Act."

sections.heading: A Lender must have the loan readily available to the Borrower upon effect of the loan
sections.text: A Lender must have the loan readily available to the Borrower upon effect of the loan.

sections.heading: The Borrower must repay the loan and in full to the Lender by the conclusion of the loan
sections.text: The Borrower must repay the loan and in full to the Lender by the conclusion of the loan.

sections.heading: A Lender may request collateral from a Borrower as a security against a loan
sections.text:
A Lender may request collateral from a Borrower as a security against a loan.

(a) The collateral must be agreed in writing in the same document the loan is signed on.

(b) Should the Borrower fail to repay the loan, the collateral shall automatically be transferred to the ownership of the Lender.

sections.heading: A loan may only be offered by a Lender where the Borrower can repay the loan in whole, or at an
sections.text: A loan may only be offered by a Lender where the Borrower can repay the loan in whole, or at an agreed rate or repayment of weekly, fortnightly, monthly, once every two months, quarterly, once every 6 months, or yearly.

sections.heading: An interest rate may not be larger than
sections.text:
An interest rate may not be larger than:

(a) 40% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is of weekly or fortnightly recurrence.

(b) 35% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is monthly, once every two months, or quarterly.

(c) 30% of a principle where the loan rate of repayment is once every 6 months, or yearly.

sections.heading: A loan may not include
sections.text:
A loan may not include:

(a) Hidden fees.

(b) Clauses that waive the rights of a Borrower.

(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.

sections.heading: A Lender may not
sections.text:
A Lender may not:

(a) Use methods of threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments.

(b) Offer a loan where the Borrower has no reasonable method to repay it.

sections.heading: Borrowers that fail to repay a loan as agreed by the Lender shall be liable to be subjected to
sections.text: Borrowers that fail to repay a loan as agreed by the Lender shall be liable to be subjected to various civil penalties as outlined by the Mayflower Tort Claims Act.

sections.heading: The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement of Usury Laws through civil and/
sections.text: The Attorney General or District Attorney may take enforcement of Usury Laws through civil and/or criminal court as prescribed by law.

sections.heading: Lenders that fail to comply with the prescribed Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions will result in
sections.text: Lenders that fail to comply with the prescribed Usury Laws or Loan Prohibitions will result in the business owners being subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 1606 “Loan Sharking”.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 3503. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Lenders that use threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments shall
sections.text: Lenders that use threats, coercion, harassment or intimidation to collect loan repayments shall be subject to criminal investigation and prosecution for 1 M.S.C. § 2308 “Extortion”.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 3504. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The term “Insurance Policy” shall refer to an agreement between a Policyholder and Insurance Bu
sections.text: The term “Insurance Policy” shall refer to an agreement between a Policyholder and Insurance Business where the Insurance Business agrees that they will payout a Policyholder as a result of a successful Claim.

sections.heading: The term “Policyholder” shall refer to a person or organization which is issued an insurance po
sections.text: The term “Policyholder” shall refer to a person or organization which is issued an insurance policy by an Insurance Business.

An Insurance Business may not:

sections.text: Should the premium of an Insurance Policy be changed, a Policyholder who is already covered by the Insurance Policy shall not have their premium affected for more or less until they are required to pay their Premium again.

sections.heading: An Insurance Policy may not include
sections.text:
An Insurance Policy may not include:

(a) Hidden fees;

(b) Clauses that waive the right of the Policyholder; and

(c) Clauses that unfairly benefit the Lender.

sections.text:
A premium may not be more than:

(a) 10% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is monthly, or shorter; or

(b) 15% of the maximum Claim if the premium is paid at an increment of time that is longer than monthly.

sections.heading: An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is not a result of financial issues, mus
sections.text:
An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is not a result of financial issues, must:

(a) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.

(b) Notify Policyholders fourteen days before shutting down.

(c) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within fourteen days of shutting down.

(d) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.

(e) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.

(f) Publicly publish a balance sheet.

(g) Publicly publish a summary claims report.

sections.heading: An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is a result of financial issues, must—
sections.text:
An Insurance Business which intends to shutdown, which is a result of financial issues, must—

(a) Attempt to rectify the issue by:

(i) Raising the required capital.

(ii) Submitting a new prospective business report which has a reduced maximum Claim amount, and/or maximum Policyholders amount which is not smaller than the amount of Policyholders that are currently on an Insurance Policy.

(iii) Refuse to accept new Policyholders.

(iv) Notifying the Commerce Office.

(b) Conduct the following actions if they fail to rectify the issue:

(i) Notify the Commerce Office seven days before shutting down.

(ii) Notify Policyholders seven days before shutting down.

(iii) Refuse to accept new Policyholders within seven days of shutting down.

(iv) Refuse to collect any Premiums within seven days of shutting down.

(v) Pay outstanding Claims.

(vi) Publicly publish a statement of cash flows.

(vii) Publicly publish a balance sheet.

(viii) Publicly publish a summary claims report.

(ix) Turn over all financial documents to the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 6 § 4702. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: If a business owner who no longer meets the requirements prescribed by the Commerce Office to l
sections.text:
If a business owner who no longer meets the requirements prescribed by the Commerce Office to legally own a business, is the owner of an Insurance Business, then:

(a) The ownership of the Insurance Business shall automatically be transferred to the Secretary of State.

(b) The original business owner must transfer the capital of the Insurance Business to the Secretary of State.

(i) The Department of Justice may direct law enforcement to seize assets owned by the original owner and sell them off to recuperate the capital.

(c) The Commerce Office must find a new owner for the business.

(i) The Commerce Office may sell the ownership in whole or in portions.

(d) The Commerce Office must cease the operations of the business until the new owner(s) are decided.

sections.text:
Transportation Service Companies shall be obligated to implement policy that details potential administrative action against employees who in any instance have met all of either sections of the following criteria:

(a) the employee had a passenger in the vehicle;

(b) the employee drove recklessly and in a manner that endangered other drivers and pedestrians; or

(c) the employee was arrested for a Misdemeanour or Felony against the Mayflower Vehicle Code, whilst in the commission of his transportation service vehicle.

sections.text:
Demotion shall be considered the involuntary reduction of rank or grade.

(a) Transferring into a different unit and taking a reduction in rank shall be considered a voluntary action if the person knew that such reduction was a prerequisite for their transfer.

sections.text:
A voluntary general discharge may be issued upon request for resignation by an employee.

(a) For the purposes of this section, a voluntary general discharge is not an administrative action.

(b) Whether or not to give a voluntary general discharge or honorable discharge is up to the due discretion of the agency so long as they prescribe concrete rules and regulations to the degree each set of circumstances warrant.

sections.text:
An involuntary general discharge may be issued to a conditional employee, or to a non-conditional employee following—

(a) an internal affairs investigation, where—

(i) that investigation found wrongdoing; and

(ii) that the wrongdoing was in the form of negligence or recklessness;

(b) an employee’s failure to uphold mandated activity standards—without approved leave—defined within department policy in the form of Activity Check(s) and/or the submission of an Activity Log(s).

(b) a finding of wanton disregard for policy, statute, or regulation; or

(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the demerit; or

(b) the demerit was plainly and clearly arbitrary or its defined offense is ambiguous.

(a) the transfer was retaliatory;

sections.text: Suspension shall refer to the prevention of a person from executing their duties and collecting pay for either a set period of time or indefinitely.

sections.heading: Administrative leave shall be the indefinite suspension pending an investigation
sections.text:
Administrative leave shall be the indefinite suspension pending an investigation. A person may only be put on administrative leave for allegations which, if taken as true, would warrant a general discharge or dishonorable discharge.

(a) A person may only be on administrative leave for no longer than ten (10) days; however, a person may be put on administrative leave for longer if there is a criminal investigation supplemented by order from the Department of Justice for the person to be placed on administrative leave.

(b) Administrative leave may be used in extreme cases where the probable punishment of suspension – however, the length of suspension must have the days on administrative leave subtracted from it.

(c) Administrative leave may only be used if there is a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation.

(d) Any administrative leave imposed as a result of a pending misconduct investigation or criminal investigation shall last up to thirty (30) days or until the conclusion of the investigation, whichever occurs first.

(i) If, upon conclusion of a misconduct or criminal investigation, probable cause of a criminal violation is found and the matter is pending review for criminal charges by the Department of Justice, the administrative leave imposed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d) may be extended for a period not to exceed seven (7) additional days. Such extension shall not be subject to the thirty (30) day limit prescribed in 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d).

(e) Any administrative leave extended pursuant to 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i) may be further extended for an indefinite period if, during the seven (7) day extension, criminal charges are formally filed. In such cases, administrative leave shall continue until the conclusion of the subsequent criminal matter.

(b) the suspension has gone on longer than allowed under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(a); or

(c) the administrative leave extended under 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d), 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(d)(i), or 4 M.S.C. 7 § 1602(e) exceeds its respective limitations without criminal filing or conclusion of the investigation.

The principles of the merit system shall be as follows
sections.text:
The principles of the merit system shall be as follows:

(a) Recruitment should be from qualified individuals from appropriate sources in an endeavor to achieve a work force from all segments of society, and selection and advancement should be determined solely on the basis of relative ability, knowledge and skills, after fair and open competition which assures that all receive equal opportunity.

(b) All employees and applicants for employment should receive fair and equitable treatment in all aspects of personnel management without regard to political affiliation, race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, or handicapping condition, and with proper regard for their privacy and constitutional rights.

(c) All employees should maintain high standards of integrity, conduct, and concern for the public interest.

(d) The State workforce should be used efficiently and effectively.

(e) Employees should be retained on the basis of adequacy of their performance, inadequate performance should be corrected, and employees should be separated who cannot or will not improve their performance to meet required standards.

(f) Employees should be provided effective education and training in cases in which such education and training would result in better organizational and individual performance.

(g) Employees should be—

(i) protected against arbitrary action, personal favoritism, or coercion for political purposes; and

(ii) prohibited from using their official authority or influence for the purpose of interfering with or affecting the result of an election or a nomination for election.

sections.heading: Employees should be protected against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of information which t
sections.text: Employees should be protected against reprisal for the lawful disclosure of information which the employees reasonably believe evidences-- a violation of any law, rule, or regulation, or mismanagement, a gross waste of resources, an abuse of authority, or a substantial and specific danger to public safety.

(a) Likelihood that the individual is an alternate account; which shall be evaluated under reasonableness.

(b) Whether the individual has their inventory open.

(c) Whether the individual is involved with a criminal or terrorist organization which has been declared by the Attorney General.

(d) Whether the individual has a certain amount of records that exceed a threshold.

(e) Whether the individual has a criminal conviction.

(f) A dishonorable discharge from the department, or other departments.

(g) Severe Moderation action against them with the exception of appealed Moderation action.

(h) Extremely toxic behavior, unlawful activities [in real life] or harassment in other communities, games, or organizations.

(i) Whether the individual is not a resident within the state.

(j) Whether the individual defects would bring harm to the health of the department.

(k) Whether the individual has past disciplinary actions taken against them within the last two (2) months in a department in which they are currently or were previously employed in.

sections.heading: Administrative hearings have the following attributes
sections.text:
Administrative hearings have the following attributes:

(a) An administrative hearing may be called by any administrative court judge as remedy; or by an agency command member to review the factual basis of a claim.

(b) An administrative hearing shall be overseen by a tribunal which shall consist of two officers chosen by the department command, which may also be themselves; and an administrative court judge who shall preside.

(c) All claims of law shall be solely decided by the administrative court judge.

(d) All claims of fact shall be decided by the tribunal-at-large.

(e) The tribunal may recommend punitive action and to what degree. The command member who called the tribunal shall be able to reject or alter the action, however he may not increase it to a greater degree than what was recommended.

(f) All matters of the admittance of evidence or witnesses shall be solely decided by the presiding judge.

(g) The procedure for an administrative hearing shall be:

(i) Call to order by the presiding judge.

(ii) The presiding judge shall state the claims being made against him and present the claims in full.

(iii) The accused will be given a chance to introduce evidence of his own, and call witnesses as necessary.

(h) The accused will then be able to give a closing statement.

(i) The presiding judge shall adjourn the hearing.

(c) As a result of an administrative claim, a judge may use all remedies afforded to him by law.

(d) The Supreme Court shall provide for the process, through rule, as to how an administrative claim be made and heard by an administrative court.

If an administrative judge fails to commence a hearing, and the department acted in good faith to schedule the hearing, then the department may act in a matter that is reasonable – including using action normally restricted to the result of an administrative hearing.

(a) A decision by department command under this section may be appealed post-hoc in an administrative court.

(b) If a person enjoys a right for the given action to first be reviewed in an administrative hearing, however action is administered under this statute, they may invoke their right for an administrative hearing to review the action at any time.

(i) If the right to hearing is invoked under this statute, then the action will stay in-tact until declared otherwise.

For the purposes of 1 M.S.C. § 2303 "Aggravated Battery", “Protected person” shall refer to any person who: is employed by the Mayflower National Guard, the Department of Transportation or its subsidiary agencies, the Department of State, the Department of Justice, the Judicial Branch (including the District and Supreme Courts), the State Senate, the Public Broadcasting Service, the Parks and Wildlife Department, any Port Authority, any law enforcement agency or entity, any firefighting, emergency medical, or emergency response agency, any healthcare entity, any other government or quasi-government entity, or any licensed private patrol operator or proprietary private security employer; is acting within the scope of their official duties; and is reasonably identifiable by uniform, badge, patch, or other clear indication of their status.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 7 § 5501. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The fish known as the mini shark shall be the state fish
sections.text: The fish known as the mini shark shall be the state fish.

sections.heading: The State Anthem Shall be as follows and shall be played before any government event
sections.text: The State Anthem Shall be as follows and shall be played before any government event: “By the coastlines and the forests, where the hills rise high, we honor Mayflower under God's watchful sky. From the mountains tall to the waves that roar, in unity and growth, we strive evermore. With faith as our guide and strength in our hands, Mayflower's blessings shine across the land. God above, we praise your light, as we stand together, proud and bright."

sections.heading: The State Motto shall be as follows
sections.text: The State Motto shall be as follows: "Faith, Strength, and Prosperity."

sections.heading: The gem known as a diamond shall be the state's official gem
sections.text: The gem known as a diamond shall be the state's official gem.

sections.heading: There is hereby established an order of civil merit to be known as the Order of Mayflower, whic
sections.text: There is hereby established an order of civil merit to be known as the Order of Mayflower, which shall be the highest civilian honor awarded by the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The Order shall be composed of persons who have rendered exceptional service to the State of Ma
sections.text: The Order shall be composed of persons who have rendered exceptional service to the State of Mayflower in public life, the arts, sciences, education, civil society, or other fields of endeavor that contribute significantly to the well-being and identity of the State.

sections.heading: The State Registrar shall serve as the Chancellor and principal officer of the Order
sections.text: The State Registrar shall serve as the Chancellor and principal officer of the Order. Appointments shall be made by the Registrar on their own initiative, or by the Deputy State Registrar with the consent of the State Registrar, or on the advice of the Governor of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: Investitures shall take place in a public ceremony, and inductees shall be entitled to wear the
sections.text: Investitures shall take place in a public ceremony, and inductees shall be entitled to wear the insignia of the Order and use the post-nominal letters “OM” for life.

sections.heading: No person shall be admitted to the Order unless they are a citizen or lawful resident of the St
sections.text: No person shall be admitted to the Order unless they are a citizen or lawful resident of the State of Mayflower, except in extraordinary cases as determined by the Chancellor.

sections.heading: Further rules and administrative procedures concerning the operation of the Order may be prescr
sections.text: Further rules and administrative procedures concerning the operation of the Order may be prescribed by regulation issued by the State Registrar.

sections.heading: The term "conditional employment" means
sections.text:
The term "conditional employment" means:

(a) Employment that may be terminated at any point for any reason.

sections.heading: An employee shall be considered conditionally employed with a department from time of hire unti
sections.text: An employee shall be considered conditionally employed with a department from time of hire until which point they have successfully completed the requirements to become a full-time employee, as defined by department policy.

sections.heading: An employee shall be considered non-conditionally employed with a department after they have su
sections.text: An employee shall be considered non-conditionally employed with a department after they have successfully completed the requirements to become a full-time employee, as defined by department policy.

sections.heading: An employee shall be considered conditional for no more than one month past their initial hire
sections.text: An employee shall be considered conditional for no more than one month past their initial hire date.

sections.heading: Administrative action issued to a conditional employee maynot be reviewed by any administrative
sections.text:
Administrative action issued to a conditional employee maynot be reviewed by any administrative court, court of law, or court of equity. This shall not apply to a discharge of the conditional employee if one of the following are true:

(a) there is clear and present factual error in the issuance of the discharge; or

(b) the discharge was clearly retaliatory.

sections.heading: No employee shall be subject to any adverse administrative action, be coerced, or in any way pe
sections.text: No employee shall be subject to any adverse administrative action, be coerced, or in any way penalized for a failure to maintain activity or perform duties during a state holiday.

SHORT TITLE
sections.text: SHORT TITLE. This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Protect The Capitol Act.”

sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.text: DEFINITIONS. For the purposes of this chapter, the term “Mayflower State Police” shall refer to the States law enforcement agency that resides within the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The term “State Capitol Building” shall refer to any publicly owned building which the State Se
sections.text: The term “State Capitol Building” shall refer to any publicly owned building which the State Senate convenes for legislative business.

sections.heading: The term “Grounds of the State Capitol” shall refer to any publicly owned property where the St
sections.text: The term “Grounds of the State Capitol” shall refer to any publicly owned property where the State Capitol Building is situated, including public walkways and roadways directly surrounding the property.

sections.heading: The department head of the Mayflower State Police may initiate an emergency lockdown of the Sta
sections.text:
The department head of the Mayflower State Police may initiate an emergency lockdown of the State Capitol Building for no longer than 2 hours if there are credible concerns for its security.

(a) The Mayflower State Police must submit a public notice 5 minutes before it is enforced.

(b) Persons that are not an on-duty peace officer or government official may not enter the State Capitol Building without the consent of an on-duty peace officer, member of the State Legislature, or the Governor.

(c) Persons that enter the State Capitol Building without the aforementioned consent after a public notice has been given are liable to be arrested for trespass.

(d) After a lockdown is lifted, the Mayflower State Police must publish a report detailing the start and end time and date of the lockdown, purpose of the lockdown, what occurred during the lockdown, and the result of the lockdown within three days.

(i) Such a report may be redacted or sensitized, in part or in entirety, in accordance with State Security Act.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 8 § 1201. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Mayflower State Police may initiate a lockdown of the State Capitol Building in preparation
sections.text:
The Mayflower State Police may initiate a lockdown of the State Capitol Building in preparation for and for the purpose of a government event that is occurring within the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(a) The Mayflower State Police must submit a public notice 30 minutes before it is enforced.

(b) Persons that are not an on-duty peace officer or government official may not enter the State Capitol Building without the consent of an on-duty peace officer, member of the State Legislature, or the Governor.

(c) Persons that enter the State Capitol Building after a public notice has been given are liable to be arrested for trespass.

sections.heading: A peace officer may search any individual who wishes to gain entry to the State Capitol Buildin
sections.text:
A peace officer may search any individual who wishes to gain entry to the State Capitol Building.

(a) Any individual in possession of facial concealment devices, firearms, or objects capable of harm shall be refused entry to the State Capitol Building.

(b) Any individual who refuses a search shall be refused entry to the State Capitol Building.

(c) Any individual who gains access after being refused entry to the State Capitol Building by any peace officer is liable to be arrested for trespass.

sections.heading: After being searched, any individual may freely access
Any individual who accesses a room not listed in Section IV(c) is liable to be arrested for tre
sections.text: Any individual who accesses a room not listed in Section IV(c) is liable to be arrested for trespass.

sections.heading: The Mayflower State police shall be alerted 3 days before any protest within the Grounds of the
sections.text:
The Mayflower State police shall be alerted 3 days before any protest within the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(a) No protests may be conducted within the State Capitol Building.

(b) Any individual who protests within the State Capitol Building is liable for arrest for disturbing the peace.

sections.heading: The Mayflower State Police shall be alerted 12 hours before any government event occurs on the
sections.text: The Mayflower State Police shall be alerted 12 hours before any government event occurs on the Grounds of the State Capitol.

sections.heading: Public travel on the Grounds of the Capitol Building shall be restricted to paved surfaces
sections.text: Public travel on the Grounds of the Capitol Building shall be restricted to paved surfaces. Any individual who is not an on-duty peace officer or government official and does not remain on a paved surface is liable to be arrested for trespass.

sections.heading: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Grounds of the State Capitol is restricted to the sidew
sections.text: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Grounds of the State Capitol is restricted to the sidewalks and other paved surfaces.

sections.heading: It is unlawful and punishable by 1 M
sections.text:
It is unlawful and punishable by 1 M.S.C. § 1507 “Unlawful Conduct in a Protected Building” to:

(a) To offer or expose any article for sale in the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(b) To display a sign, placard, or other form of advertisement in the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(c) To solicit fares, alms, subscriptions, or contributions in the Grounds of the State Capitol.

(d) Parade, stand, or move in processions or assemblages in the Grounds of the State Capitol, or to display in the Grounds of the State Capitol a flag, banner, garment or device designed or adapted to bring into public notice a party, organization, or movement.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 4 M.S.C. 8 § 1302. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The Grounds of the State Capitol shall be a Firearm Free Zone and Melee Free Zone
sections.text: The Grounds of the State Capitol shall be a Firearm Free Zone and Melee Free Zone.

sections.heading: There shall be a Congressional Park, which shall be situated within the parkland east of the St
sections.text:
There shall be a Congressional Park, which shall be situated within the parkland east of the State Capitol.

(a) It shall be permitted to walk on non-paved surfaces within the Congressional Park.

(b) It shall be forbidden to swim within the lake situated within the Congressional Parks, which shall be known as Bear Memorial Lake.

(c) The Congressional Parks shall be considered as extensions of the Grounds of the State Capitol, but not the roads or pathways directly surrounding it which are not part of the dedicated Grounds of the State Capitol.

sections.heading: There shall be a State Memorial Grounds, which shall be situated within the graveyard east of t
sections.text:
There shall be a State Memorial Grounds, which shall be situated within the graveyard east of the Congressional Parks.

(a) It shall be permitted to walk on non-paved surfaces within the State Memorial Grounds.

(b) The State Memorial Grounds shall be considered as extensions of the Grounds of the State Capitol, but not the roads or pathways directly surrounding it which are not part of the dedicated Grounds of the State Capitol.

sections.heading: “Deadly force” shall refer to force that is intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily
sections.text: “Deadly force” shall refer to force that is intended or likely to cause death or serious bodily injury.

sections.heading: “Military Exclusion Zone” shall refer to an area formally designated and posted as off-limits t
sections.text: “Military Exclusion Zone” shall refer to an area formally designated and posted as off-limits to unauthorized civilians in accordance with applicable law.

sections.heading: “Military installation” shall refer to any base, armory, depot, range, or facility operated by
sections.text: “Military installation” shall refer to any base, armory, depot, range, or facility operated by the Mayflower National Guard.

sections.heading: “Line-of-sight” shall refer to unobstructed visual range from a military installation’s outer p
sections.text: “Line-of-sight” shall refer to unobstructed visual range from a military installation’s outer perimeter.

sections.heading: A law enforcement officer or other authorized agent of the State is authorized to use deadly fo
sections.text:
A law enforcement officer or other authorized agent of the State is authorized to use deadly force against a fleeing suspect only when all of the following conditions are met:

(a) The officer has probable cause to believe that the suspect has committed a felony involving the infliction or threatened infliction of death or serious bodily injury;

(b) The officer has probable cause to believe that the suspect poses a significant threat of death or serious bodily injury to the officer or to others if not immediately apprehended; and

(c) The use of deadly force is necessary to prevent escape, and no reasonably safe alternative exists.

sections.heading: Where feasible, a verbal warning should be given prior to the use of deadly force
sections.text: Where feasible, a verbal warning should be given prior to the use of deadly force.

sections.heading: A member of the Mayflower National Guard, when on active duty status under state authority, is
sections.text:
A member of the Mayflower National Guard, when on active duty status under state authority, is authorized to use deadly force consistent with subsections (a) and (b) of this section if the threat occurs within, or within direct line-of-sight of, a Military Exclusion Zone or active military installation and:

(a) The suspect has committed or is reasonably believed to have committed an offense posing an immediate threat to the safety or security of:

(i) The installation or its personnel, or

(ii) Nearby civilians or bystanders; and

(b) The use of force is immediately necessary to prevent the suspect’s escape or continued threat, and no reasonably safe alternative is available.

sections.heading: Nothing in this section shall be construed to grant standing law enforcement authority to Natio
sections.text: Nothing in this section shall be construed to grant standing law enforcement authority to National Guard personnel beyond that which is expressly conferred under state law and the Constitution of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The Bar of the State of Mayflower is hereby established as an administrative agency within the
sections.text: The Bar of the State of Mayflower is hereby established as an administrative agency within the judicial branch of government. It shall operate under the supervision of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial
sections.text: The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial officer to oversee and support the effective operation of the State Bar, ensuring it adheres to the provisions of this act and any relevant rules or regulations.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official us
sections.text: The State Bar shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official use and may not be used for any private purposes.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name
sections.text: The State Bar shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name.

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as the "Judiciary Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as the "Judiciary Act."

sections.heading: For the purposes of this section
sections.text:
For the purposes of this section:

(a) "State Bar" shall refer to the Bar of the State of Mayflower established under this act.

(b) "Supreme Court" shall refer to the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

(c) "Active Member" shall refer to an attorney who is fully licensed and authorized to practice law in the State of Mayflower.

(d) "Provisional License" shall refer to a temporary license granted under this act.

(e) "Disciplinary Proceedings" shall refer to actions initiated to address allegations of professional misconduct or attorney incapacity.

sections.heading: The statutory officers of the State Bar shall include
sections.text:
The statutory officers of the State Bar shall include:

(a) The State Bar Director.

sections.heading: These officers shall be elected by a majority vote of all Associate Justices of the Supreme Cou
sections.text: These officers shall be elected by a majority vote of all Associate Justices of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: If a vacancy arises unexpectedly, the Chief Justice may choose to appoint an interim Director(s
sections.text: If a vacancy arises unexpectedly, the Chief Justice may choose to appoint an interim Director(s) until a new election can be held.

sections.heading: The terms of the officers shall be determined by the Chief Justice
sections.text: The terms of the officers shall be determined by the Chief Justice.

sections.text: The State Bar shall keep detailed financial records and prepare an annual budget if it decides to impose a levy for its operations. The budget shall be subject to the approval of the Supreme Court.

sections.text:
In accordance with the Chief Justice having oversight of the State Bar statutory to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1101.1, the Chief Justice shall be granted automatic membership on the State Bar. This shall take it's effectiveness after:

(a) The Chief Justice swear's his or her's oath

sections.text: The State Bar shall keep detailed financial records and prepare an annual budget if it decides to impose a levy for its operations. The budget shall be subject to the approval of the Supreme Court.

sections.heading: The State Bar of the State of Mayflower shall have the delegated authority to examine, recommen
sections.text: The State Bar of the State of Mayflower shall have the delegated authority to examine, recommend and grant licensure to individuals seeking admission to practice law in this State.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall conduct all necessary evaluations, including the bar examination and charac
sections.text: The State Bar shall conduct all necessary evaluations, including the bar examination and character and fitness assessments, to determine an applicant’s qualifications.

sections.heading: No person shall be admitted to practice as an attorney or counselor in the State of Mayflower w
sections.text: No person shall be admitted to practice as an attorney or counselor in the State of Mayflower without fulfilling the requirements prescribed by the State Bar.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall retain ultimate and inherent authority over all matters concerning the admi
sections.text: The State Bar shall retain ultimate and inherent authority over all matters concerning the admission to the practice of law in this State with the State Bar carrying out its functions.

sections.heading: The State Bar of the State of Mayflower is authorized to grant provisional licenses to individu
sections.text: The State Bar of the State of Mayflower is authorized to grant provisional licenses to individuals who meet specific criteria established by the Bar, allowing them to engage in limited legal practice under supervision for a defined period.

sections.heading: Membership in the State Bar of Mayflower is divided into the following categories
sections.text:
Membership in the State Bar of Mayflower is divided into the following categories:

(a) Active Membership: Attorneys who are fully licensed and authorized to practice law.

(b) Inactive Membership: Attorneys not currently practicing law, who may be exempt from paying levies.

(c) Abeyance Membership: Attorneys whose membership is temporarily suspended due to disciplinary action, failure to meet obligations, or holding a position that places them under judicial trust. These members may not practice law until reinstated by the Bar.

(d) Provisional Membership: Attorneys holding a provisional license, allowing them to practice law under supervision. They must transition to active membership upon fulfilling all requirements for full licensure or when their provisional status expires.

sections.heading: The State Bar has the authority to adopt, implement, and enforce rules governing the practice o
sections.text: The State Bar has the authority to adopt, implement, and enforce rules governing the practice of law and the conduct of its members.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall establish and maintain the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct, which o
sections.text: The State Bar shall establish and maintain the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct, which outline the ethical and professional responsibilities of all attorneys licensed in this State.

sections.heading: In consultation of its committee members, the State Bar may also adopt additional rules, regula
Before adopting, amending, or repealing any rule, the State Bar shall
The State Bar shall develop and administer all bar examinations in a manner that ensures fairne
sections.text: The State Bar shall develop and administer all bar examinations in a manner that ensures fairness, transparency, and equal access for all applicants.

sections.heading: The State Bar must provide applicants with adequate resources and information regarding the exa
sections.text:
The State Bar must provide applicants with adequate resources and information regarding the examination, including:

(a) Published guidelines;

(b) Subjects tested, and relevant rules; and

(c) Information on examination dates, deadlines and procedures.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall establish and publish a clear grade boundary or passing score for the exami
sections.text: The State Bar shall establish and publish a clear grade boundary or passing score for the examination.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court of Mayflower has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to
sections.text: The Supreme Court of Mayflower has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to practice law. The Supreme Court holds sole authority to establish, amend, and enforce all standards and rules related to attorney admission.

sections.heading: The officers and directors of the State Bar of Mayflower do not have the authority to approve,
sections.text: The officers and directors of the State Bar of Mayflower do not have the authority to approve, disapprove, regulate, or administer any rule regarding admissions. All admissions standards, procedures, and requirements are prescribed and administered solely by the Supreme Court.

sections.heading: The State Bar has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to practice law and
sections.text: The State Bar has exclusive jurisdiction over rules governing the admission to practice law and holds sole authority to establish, amend, and enforce all standards and rules related to attorney admission. The State Bar’s role also includes executing the examination, character and fitness assessments, and other processes.

sections.heading: All attorneys admitted to practice law in the State of Mayflower are subject to the disciplinar
sections.text: All attorneys admitted to practice law in the State of Mayflower are subject to the disciplinary and disability jurisdiction of the State Bar, including its committees.

sections.heading: The State Bar has the authority to investigate, adjudicate, and impose appropriate sanctions fo
sections.text: The State Bar has the authority to investigate, adjudicate, and impose appropriate sanctions for violations of professional conduct or instances of attorney incapacity, following rules and procedures enacted.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court shall have the exclusive ability to appeal any investigations or actions take
sections.text: The Supreme Court shall have the exclusive ability to appeal any investigations or actions taken as repritorive or as a strict punishment on any Attorney within the State Bar.

sections.heading: In any disciplinary or disability proceeding, the person involved shall be afforded due process
sections.text: In any disciplinary or disability proceeding, the person involved shall be afforded due process, including a fair opportunity to present representations and defend against the allegations.

sections.heading: The person has the right to be notified of the charges, be represented by counsel, present evid
sections.text: The person has the right to be notified of the charges, be represented by counsel, present evidence, and call and cross-examine witnesses as part of their defense.

sections.heading: Upon receiving credible information that an attorney’s continued practice poses a substantial t
sections.text: Upon receiving credible information that an attorney’s continued practice poses a substantial threat to the public or the integrity of the legal profession, the State Bar or a delegated committee may suspend the attorney’s license pending further investigation.

sections.heading: An interim suspension under this Section may be imposed while the matter is under investigation
sections.text: An interim suspension under this Section may be imposed while the matter is under investigation. The subject shall be notified of the suspension without delay and afforded an opportunity to contest the suspension.

sections.heading: An interim suspension pursuant to this Section shall not exceed fourteen (14) calendar days fro
sections.text: An interim suspension pursuant to this Section shall not exceed fourteen (14) calendar days from the date of issuance. The suspension shall terminate automatically upon the period of expiration, unless, prior to expiration, an extension is granted by an extraordinary order upon showing good cause that the continued suspension is necessary to protect the public, or the integrity of the legal profession.

sections.heading: The State Bar shall provide notice of the interim suspension to the subject within two (2) hour
sections.text: The State Bar shall provide notice of the interim suspension to the subject within two (2) hours of its issuance, and shall be obligated to notify relevant judicial officers of such suspension to ensure affected clients are informed and provided adequate time to secure alternative counsel.

sections.heading: The State Bar, acting as a precepting authority under the direction of the Director, may impose
