sections.text: The State Bar, acting as a precepting authority under the direction of the Director, may impose and enforce a monthly levy payable by all attorneys registered to practice law in the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The amount of the levy and the payment schedule shall be determined by the State Bar, subject t
sections.text: The amount of the levy and the payment schedule shall be determined by the State Bar, subject to the approval of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: A levy cannot be imposed or amended without the support of at least 2/3rds of the sitting Justi
sections.text: A levy cannot be imposed or amended without the support of at least 2/3rds of the sitting Justices of the Supreme Court, and it may only be imposed on the “Active” class of membership.

sections.heading: The levy must be used strictly to fund the administration and operation of the State Bar, inclu
The Office of Public Defenders is hereby established as an administrative agency within the jud
sections.text: The Office of Public Defenders is hereby established as an administrative agency within the judicial branch of government. It shall operate under the supervision of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial
sections.text: The Chief Justice may, at their discretion, designate an Associate Justice or another judicial officer to oversee and support the effective operation of the Office ensuring it adheres to the provisions of this act and any relevant rules or regulations.

sections.heading: The Office shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official use a
sections.text: The Office shall have an official seal, which shall be reserved strictly for its official use and may not be used for any private purposes.

sections.heading: The Office shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name
sections.text: The Office shall have the legal capacity to sue and be sued under its own name.

sections.heading: The Office of Public Defenders shall be governed by an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court w
sections.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall be governed by an Associate Justice of the Supreme Court who shall serve as the supervising authority of the Office. The Justice shall be responsible for ensuring that the Office operates effectively and in accordance with the provisions of this act.

sections.heading: The Associate Justice, acting as supervisor, shall appoint a Chief Public Defender, who must be
sections.text: The Associate Justice, acting as supervisor, shall appoint a Chief Public Defender, who must be a member of the Mayflower State Bar, and shall manage the day-to-day operations of the Office, including the supervision of all public defenders and support staff.

sections.heading: The Chief Public Defender shall serve a term determined by the supervising authority and may be
sections.text: The Chief Public Defender shall serve a term determined by the supervising authority and may be reappointed at the discretion of the supervising authority.

sections.heading: The Office of Public Defenders shall provide legal representation to any individual who
sections.text:
The Office of Public Defenders shall provide legal representation to any individual who:

(a) is charged with a criminal offense in the State of Mayflower and faces potential incarceration; and

(b) is determined by the court to be financially unable to obtain private counsel.

sections.heading: The Office shall also provide representation in civil cases where such representation is mandat
sections.text: The Office shall also provide representation in civil cases where such representation is mandated by law or necessary to protect a fundamental right, subject to available resources.

sections.heading: The scope of representation shall include all stages of criminal and civil proceedings, from in
sections.text: The scope of representation shall include all stages of criminal and civil proceedings, from initial appearance through trial, sentencing, appeal, and post-conviction relief.

sections.heading: The Office may elect to create specialized units for complex cases where it deems necessary
sections.text: The Office may elect to create specialized units for complex cases where it deems necessary.

sections.heading: The Office of Public Defenders shall recruit and employ qualified attorneys as public defenders
sections.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall recruit and employ qualified attorneys as public defenders to ensure that it meets its obligations under this act.

sections.heading: The Chief Public Defender, in consultation with the Supervising Justice, shall be responsible f
sections.text: The Chief Public Defender, in consultation with the Supervising Justice, shall be responsible for overseeing the recruitment, selection, and appointment of public defenders.

sections.heading: Be members in good standing of the Mayflower State Bar
sections.text: Be members in good standing of the Mayflower State Bar;

sections.heading: Demonstrate intention or experience in criminal defense or the specific areas of law relevant t
sections.text: Demonstrate intention or experience in criminal defense or the specific areas of law relevant to their assigned duties; and

sections.heading: Possess a strong commitment to public service and the protection of clients' constitutional rig
sections.text: Possess a strong commitment to public service and the protection of clients' constitutional rights.

sections.heading: Eligibility for representation by the Office of Public Defenders shall be determined based on f
sections.text: Eligibility for representation by the Office of Public Defenders shall be determined based on financial guidelines established and approved by the Supreme Court of Mayflower.

sections.heading: A person is considered indigent if their income and assets are insufficient to afford private l
sections.text: A person is considered indigent if their income and assets are insufficient to afford private legal representation, considering the complexity of the case and associated costs.

sections.heading: The court shall make the determination of indigence, which shall be reviewed periodically and a
sections.text: The court shall make the determination of indigence, which shall be reviewed periodically and adjusted if the individual’s financial circumstances change.

sections.heading: The Office of Public Defenders shall operate independently from political influence, with publi
sections.text: The Office of Public Defenders shall operate independently from political influence, with public defenders performing their duties free from external pressures and in strict adherence to professional ethics.

sections.heading: Public defenders shall adhere to the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct and any additional
sections.text: Public defenders shall adhere to the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct and any additional ethical guidelines set forth by the State Bar.

sections.heading: The payment and compensation of all Public Defenders shall be set as equal to the compensation
sections.text: The payment and compensation of all Public Defenders shall be set as equal to the compensation of the average State Attorney.

sections.heading: Public defenders shall have the authority to make all decisions regarding representation, case
sections.text: Public defenders shall have the authority to make all decisions regarding representation, case strategy, and defense without interference from any external entity, including the Department of Justice, or the Attorney General and his respective officers, and sub-agents.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1206.4. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Chief Public Defender shall develop policies to ensure that caseloads are manageable and th
sections.text: The Chief Public Defender shall develop policies to ensure that caseloads are manageable and that public defenders can provide competent and diligent representation to each client.

sections.heading: The Office shall establish performance standards and regularly evaluate the effectiveness and q
sections.text: The Office shall establish performance standards and regularly evaluate the effectiveness and quality of the legal representation provided by public defenders.

sections.heading: The Office may elect to subcontract some of its legal services to a private law firm if such su
sections.text: The Office may elect to subcontract some of its legal services to a private law firm if such subcontracting is deemed necessary to ensure effective representation, manage caseloads, or address specialized legal needs.

sections.heading: Any subcontractor under section (c) of this Section must
sections.text:
Any subcontractor under section (c) of this Section must:

(a) be in good standing with the Mayflower State Bar;

(b) demonstrate a history of providing high-quality legal services, with particular experience in criminal defense or the specific area of law for which they are being engaged; and

(c) adhere to the same ethical and professional standards required of public defenders, including compliance with the Mayflower Rules of Professional Conduct.

sections.heading: The decision to subcontract services shall be made by the Chief Public Defender, in consultatio
sections.text:
The decision to subcontract services shall be made by the Chief Public Defender, in consultation with the Supervising Justice, and must be based on clear and documented criteria, including but not limited to:

(a) the need to address caseload overflow or conflicts of interest;

(b) the specialized expertise required for complex cases; and

(c) the availability of resources within the OPD to handle the case internally.

sections.heading: The subcontracting arrangement shall be subject to review to ensure compliance with this act an
sections.text: The subcontracting arrangement shall be subject to review to ensure compliance with this act and the delivery of high-quality legal services.

sections.heading: Any subcontracting must be provided with a notice under this section to the general public noti
sections.text: Any subcontracting must be provided with a notice under this section to the general public notifying them of such changes to services offered.

sections.heading: The subcontractor may not charge for any services from its client, but may receive appropriatio
sections.text: The subcontractor may not charge for any services from its client, but may receive appropriations from the Office if agreed upon.

sections.heading: The Supervising Justice may, at their discretion, initiate the removal or dismissal of the Chie
sections.text: The Supervising Justice may, at their discretion, initiate the removal or dismissal of the Chief Public Defender if it is determined that such action is necessary for the effective operation of the Office of Public Defenders.

sections.heading: Grounds for removal may include, but are not limited to
Before the Chief is removed or dismissed, the Supervising Justice must seek and obtain permissi
sections.text: Before the Chief is removed or dismissed, the Supervising Justice must seek and obtain permission from the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Mayflower. Upon approval by the Chief Justice, the Supervising Justice shall have the authority to immediately remove the Chief from their position and appoint an interim Chief until a permanent replacement is selected. The Supervising Justice shall then initiate the process to appoint a new Chief Public Defender as provided under Sections of this act.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court may appoint a marshal, who shall be subject to removal by the Court, and may
sections.text: The Supreme Court may appoint a marshal, who shall be subject to removal by the Court, and may fix his compensation.

sections.heading: The marshal may, with the approval of the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, appoint and
sections.text: The marshal may, with the approval of the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, appoint and fix the compensation of necessary assistants and other employees to attend the Court, and necessary custodial employees under his supervison.

sections.heading: There shall be a Supreme Court Police Division established within a department, as designated b
sections.text: There shall be a Supreme Court Police Division established within a department, as designated by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, with the approval of the Supreme Court of Mayflower and the Head of the relevant department that will house this division.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1301.3. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The marshal shall
In accordance with regulations prescribed by the Marshal of the Supreme Court and approved by t
(ii) any officer or employee of the Supreme Court while that officer or employee is performing
sections.text: (ii) any officer or employee of the Supreme Court while that officer or employee is performing official duties; and

sections.heading: (iii) any member of the immediate family of the Chief Justice, any Associate Justice, or any of
sections.text:
(iii) any member of the immediate family of the Chief Justice, any Associate Justice, or any officer of the Supreme Court if the Marshal determines such protection is necessary, or if directed by the Chief Justice.

(c) while performing duties necessary to carry out paragraph (1) or (2), to make arrests for any violation of State law and any regulation under State law; and

(d) to carry firearms as may be required while performing duties under this subchapter, part III of this subchapter, and subchapter IV.

sections.heading: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Supreme Court grounds is restricted to the sidewalks an
sections.text: Public travel in, and occupancy of, the Supreme Court grounds is restricted to the sidewalks and other paved surfaces.

sections.heading: It is unlawful—
sections.text:
It is unlawful—

(a) to offer or expose any article for sale in the Supreme Court Building or grounds;

(b) to display a sign, placard, or other form of advertisement in the Building or grounds; or

(c) to solicit fares, alms, subscriptions, or contributions in the Building or grounds.

sections.heading: It is unlawful to discharge a firearm or explosive, set fire to a combustible, make a harangue
sections.text: It is unlawful to discharge a firearm or explosive, set fire to a combustible, make a harangue or oration, or utter loud, threatening, or abusive language in the Supreme Court Building or grounds.

sections.heading: It is unlawful to parade, stand, or move in processions or assemblages in the Supreme Court Bui
sections.text: It is unlawful to parade, stand, or move in processions or assemblages in the Supreme Court Building or grounds, or to display in the Building and grounds a flag, banner, or device designed or adapted to bring into public notice a party, organization, or movement.

sections.heading: To allow the observance of authorized ceremonies in the Supreme Court Building and grounds, the
sections.text:
To allow the observance of authorized ceremonies in the Supreme Court Building and grounds, the Marshal of the Supreme Court may suspend for those occasions any of the prohibitions contained in this subchapter as may be necessary for the occasion if—

(a) responsible officers have been appointed; and

(b) the Marshal determines that adequate arrangements have been made—

(i) to maintain suitable order and decorum in the proceedings; and

(ii) to protect the Supreme Court Building and grounds and individuals and property in the Building and grounds.

sections.heading: An individual who violates this subchapter, or a regulation prescribed under part IV of this ti
sections.text: An individual who violates this subchapter, or a regulation prescribed under part IV of this title, shall be guilty for unlawful conduct in a protected building and shall be fined for no less than two hundred (200) dollars and not more than five hundred (500) dollars, or imprisoned not more than ten (10) minutes, or both. See 1 M.S.C. § 1507.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1303.6. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: In addition to the restrictions and requirements specified in part III, the Marshal of the Supr
sections.text:
In addition to the restrictions and requirements specified in part III, the Marshal of the Supreme Court may prescribe regulations, approved by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, that are necessary for—

(a) the adequate protection of the Supreme Court Building and grounds and of individuals and property in the Building and grounds; and

(b) the maintenance of suitable order and decorum within the Building and grounds.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court and all inferior Courts may issue all writs necessary or appropriate in aid o
sections.text: The Supreme Court and all inferior Courts may issue all writs necessary or appropriate in aid of their respective jurisdictions and agreeable to the usages and principles of law.

sections.heading: An alternative writ or rule may be issued by a justice or judge of a court that has jurisdictio
sections.text: An alternative writ or rule may be issued by a justice or judge of a court that has jurisdiction.

sections.heading: A quo warranto may be issued from the Mayflower District Court for the judicial district in whi
sections.text: A quo warranto may be issued from the Mayflower District Court for the judicial district in which the Capitol resides in the name of the State of Mayflower against a person who within the State of Mayflower usurps, intrudes into, or unlawfully holds or exercises, a franchise conferred by the State or a public office of the State of Mayflower, civil or military. The proceedings shall be deemed a civil action. No writ of quo warranto may be filed without the consent of the Attorney General.

sections.heading: The courts shall prescribe manner and method for the issuance of these writs
sections.text: The courts shall prescribe manner and method for the issuance of these writs.

sections.heading: A defendant in any criminal action has the right of appeal under the rules hereinafter prescrib
sections.text: A defendant in any criminal action has the right of appeal under the rules hereinafter prescribed, and provided, however, before the defendant who has been convicted upon either his plea of guilty or plea of nolo contendere before the court and the court, upon the election of the defendant, assesses punishment and the punishment does not exceed the punishment recommended by the prosecutor and agreed to by the defendant and his attorney may prosecute his appeal, he must have permission of the trial court, except on those matters which have been raised by written motion filed prior to trial.

sections.heading: The State is entitled to appeal an order of a court in a criminal case if the order
The State is entitled to a stay in the proceedings pending the disposition of an appeal under 5
sections.text: The State is entitled to a stay in the proceedings pending the disposition of an appeal under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1401.2.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1402.3. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: At any time, over any arrest, a person may petition the District Court for a writ of habeas cor
sections.text:
At any time, over any arrest, a person may petition the District Court for a writ of habeas corpus.

(a) The fact that a person was released from prison shall not hold bar or make moot any petition therein.

(b) The writ shall be directed to the person who has made the arrest, furthermore they shall also serve as the respondent to which a petition shall be served onto.

(c) The State shall serve as counsel for the respondent.

(i) The State may refuse to defend the respondent in a matter of a Habeas Corpus petition, if the State issues an order vacating the arrest which was the basis of the petition filed.

(d) Every provision relating to the writ of habeas corpus shall be most favorably construed in order to give effect to the remedy, and protect the rights of the person seeking relief under it.

(e) Notwithstanding any other law, a clerk of a court may not require a filing fee from an individual who files an application or petition for a writ of habeas corpus.

sections.heading: The following are the only authorized remedies
sections.text:
The following are the only authorized remedies:

(a) immediate release from prison or detainment if timely sought; and

(b) expungement of record.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court may promulgate rules pursuant to this statute
sections.text: The Supreme Court may promulgate rules pursuant to this statute.

sections.heading: The District Court may render a declaratory judgment having the effect of a final judgment as t
sections.text: The District Court may render a declaratory judgment having the effect of a final judgment as to the rights and other legal relations of the parties to a justiciable controversy whether or not further relief is or could be claimed. If the court declines to render such a judgment it shall state its grounds. Any such declaration shall have the force and effect of a final judgment or decree and shall be reviewable as such.

sections.heading: The common law and statutes of Pax Britannia, of a general and not local nature, as they existe
sections.text: The common law and statutes of Pax Britannia, of a general and not local nature, as they existed on the 4th Day of July, 1776, are hereby declared to be in force in this state, except as otherwise provided. Such laws shall remain in effect unless they are inconsistent with the Constitution and laws of the Union of Columbia or the acts of the state legislature.

sections.heading: All expungements are to be titled "Ex parte [name]," and take place as a proceeding against the
sections.text:
All expungements are to be titled "Ex parte [name]," and take place as a proceeding against the Department of Justice.

(a) Unless the Attorney General or his designee appears to argue against expunction after notice being provided to the Attorney General of the filing of such expunction, the expungement petition will continue to be heard ex parte.

(i) In lieu of appearing, the Attorney General or his designee may submit a statement in support or in opposition to the expungement petition, which will be enetered into the court record for consideration of the assigned judge.

(b) If the Attorney General or his designee appears, they shall argue for the interests of the State in regard to the expunction. The expungement petition shall instead be titled "[Name of Petitioner] v. State of Mayflower."
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1501.1. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: An individual who wishes to clear less than ten (10) records, and has demonstrated they are in
sections.text:
An individual who wishes to clear less than ten (10) records, and has demonstrated they are in good standing with the community, and have not committed any crimes in the last twenty (20) days shall have their petition granted.

(a) A hearing shall not be conducted, initiated, or required for this type of expungement.

sections.heading: An individual who wishes to clear less than sixty (60) records and has demonstrated they are in
sections.text:
An individual who wishes to clear less than sixty (60) records and has demonstrated they are in good standing in the community and have not committed any crimes in the last thirty (30) days shall have their petition granted.

(a) A hearing shall not be conducted, initiated, or required for this type of expungement.

sections.heading: An individual who wishes to clear more than 60 records, and has demonstrated they are in good s
sections.text:
An individual who wishes to clear more than 60 records, and has demonstrated they are in good standing with the community, and have not committed any crimes in the last 60 days. That individual must also demonstrate that they are pursuing programs and seeking help or assistance to be a good citizen, including but not limited to fresh start programs. They then, may have their petition discretionarily granted. A judge may offer an expungement on the condition that the petitioner successfully completes a community service program.

(a) A hearing shall not be conducted, initiated, or required for this type of expungement.

sections.heading: Expungement of any amount of citations may occur after ten (10) days of issuance of the last ci
sections.text:
Expungement of any amount of citations may occur after ten (10) days of issuance of the last citation to be expunged.

(a) A hearing shall not be conducted, initiated, or required for this type of expungement.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court may promulgate rules pursuant to this statute
sections.text:
The Supreme Court may promulgate rules pursuant to this statute.

(a) These rules may effectuate the following but are not limited to:

(i) Temporarily suspending or modifying the required crime-free period for the purpose of conducting "mass expungement" sessions.

sections.heading: A judge, upon the sentencing phase of a criminal case, shall set a period where a person must w
sections.text: A judge, upon the sentencing phase of a criminal case, shall set a period where a person must wait to expunge their conviction. Such a period shall be no longer than 8 months.

sections.heading: If no minimum period is specified explicitly, then a person must wait at least 4 months before
sections.text: If no minimum period is specified explicitly, then a person must wait at least 4 months before expunging their conviction.

sections.heading: A conviction may be expunged before the preset time upon consent of the government
sections.text: A conviction may be expunged before the preset time upon consent of the government.

sections.heading: Further requirements for a conviction expungement are
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a designated Associate Justice, is authorized to ass
sections.text: The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, or a designated Associate Justice, is authorized to assign any Supreme Court Justice to temporarily sit as a judge in a lower court, including the district courts.

sections.heading: The Chief Judge of a county shall submit a written notice to the Supreme Court of Mayflower for
sections.text: The Chief Judge of a county shall submit a written notice to the Supreme Court of Mayflower for temporary assignments to the lower court to alleviate a backlog of cases and to provide additional judicial resources in regions experiencing high caseloads.

sections.heading: The Chief Justice, in consultation with the Associate Justices, will review and approve or deny
sections.text: The Chief Justice, in consultation with the Associate Justices, will review and approve or deny requests for temporary assignments.

sections.heading: These assignments shall only be temporary and the duration is to be determined on a case-by-cas
sections.text: These assignments shall only be temporary and the duration is to be determined on a case-by-case basis. If there is a substantial need for aid from the Supreme Court, then the assignment duration may be extended.

sections.heading: Justices who sit as judges in a lower court shall have the full judicial authority of the lower
sections.text: Justices who sit as judges in a lower court shall have the full judicial authority of the lower court to which they are assigned, including the power to hear cases, issue rulings, and manage court procedures.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court Justice shall operate within the jurisdiction of the lower court, adhering to
sections.text: The Supreme Court Justice shall operate within the jurisdiction of the lower court, adhering to applicable procedural and substantive laws.

sections.heading: A Supreme Court Justice who has presided over a case during a temporary assignment in a lower c
sections.text: A Supreme Court Justice who has presided over a case during a temporary assignment in a lower court shall recuse themselves from hearing that case at the appellate level.

sections.heading: Any retired Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower or Associate Justice of the Supreme Court m
sections.text: Any retired Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower or Associate Justice of the Supreme Court may be designated and assigned by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower to perform such judicial duties in any county, including those of a district court judge, as he is willing to undertake.

sections.heading: Any retired district court judge may be designated and assigned by the chief judge of his count
sections.text: Any retired district court judge may be designated and assigned by the chief judge of his county, with permission from the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower, to perform such judicial duties within the circuit as he is willing and able to undertake. Any other retired judge of the State of Mayflower may be designated and assigned by the chief judge of his court to perform such judicial duties in such court as he is willing and able to undertake.

sections.heading: The Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower shall maintain a roster of retired judges of the St
sections.text: The Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower shall maintain a roster of retired judges of the State of Mayflower who are willing and able to undertake special judicial duties from time to time outside their own county. Any such retired judge of the State of Mayflower may be designated and assigned by the Chief Justice to perform such judicial duties as he is willing and able to undertake in a court outside his own county, in the case of a retired circuit or district judge, or in a court other than his own, in the case of any other retired judge of the State of Mayflower. Such designation and assignment to a district court shall be made upon the presentation of a certificate of necessity by the chief judge of the county wherein the need arises and to any other court of the State of Mayflower upon the presentation of a certificate of necessity by the chief judge of such court. No such designation or assignment shall be made to the Supreme Court.

sections.heading: No retired justice or judge shall perform judicial duties except when designated and assigned
sections.text: No retired justice or judge shall perform judicial duties except when designated and assigned.

sections.heading: A search warrant is an order in writing, in the name of the people, signed by a justice, judge,
sections.text: A search warrant is an order in writing, in the name of the people, signed by a justice, judge, or magistrate, directed to a peace officer, commanding him or her to search for a person or persons, a thing or things, or personal property, and, in the case of a thing or things or personal property, bring the same before the magistrate.

sections.heading: A search warrant may be issued upon any of the following grounds
sections.text:
A search warrant may be issued upon any of the following grounds:

(a) When the property was stolen or embezzled.

(b) When the property or things were used as the means of committing a felony.

(c) When the property or things are in the possession of any person with the intent to use them as a means of committing a public offense, or in the possession of another to whom he or she may have delivered them for the purpose of concealing them or preventing them from being discovered.

(d) When the property or things to be seized consist of any item or constitute any evidence that tends to show a felony has been committed, or tends to show that a particular person has committed a felony.

(e) When there is a warrant to arrest a person.

(f) When the property or things to be seized include a firearm or any other deadly weapon at the scene of, or at the premises occupied or under the control of the person arrested in connection with, a domestic violence incident involving a threat to human life or a physical assault.

(g) When the item or substance to be seized is unlawfully possessed or stored in any vehicle, domicile, or storage unit.

sections.heading: The property, things, person, or persons described in part I may be taken on the warrant from a
sections.text: The property, things, person, or persons described in part I may be taken on the warrant from any place, or from any person in whose possession the property or things may be.

sections.heading: Notwithstanding other provisions, arrest warrants may only be applied for during cases in which
sections.text: Notwithstanding other provisions, arrest warrants may only be applied for during cases in which exigent circumstances exist and the person has left the immediate presence of law enforcement officers [LTAA] who have probable cause to effectuate an arrest.

sections.heading: Arrest warrants may also be issued to a Defendant in a criminal matter, upon acceptance of the
Upon the warrant’s execution, the documents and records shall be made open to the public as a j
sections.text: Upon the warrant’s execution, the documents and records shall be made open to the public as a judicial record in a timely manner.

sections.heading: A search warrant may be made returnable before the issuing magistrate or his court
sections.text: A search warrant may be made returnable before the issuing magistrate or his court.

sections.heading: No warrant shall be issued by a justice, judge, or magistrate where they are employed by the sa
sections.text: No warrant shall be issued by a justice, judge, or magistrate where they are employed by the same law enforcement agency that filed for the warrant.

sections.heading: Unless otherwise deemed necessary by a judge, warrants shall be executed by the county law enfo
sections.text:
Unless otherwise deemed necessary by a judge, warrants shall be executed by the county law enforcement agency of the political subdivision in which the warrant was issued, except under the following:

(a) Any search warrant request that is submitted by an employee of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation as a result of affidavits filed by the bureau, or cases prosecuted by the Department of Justice, shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation and shall be directed as such for execution.

(b) Any search warrant that was submitted which involves goods and items relating to military-grade equipment, the Mayflower National Guard, Military Police shall have jurisdiction over its execution and shall be directed as such for execution.

(c) Any search warrant request that is submitted by an employee of the State Bureau of Investigations (SBI) as a result of affidavits filed by the SBI shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Mayflower State Police and shall be directed as such for execution.

(i) For the purposes of this section, the term “State Bureau of Investigations” shall be defined as: the division under the Mayflower State Police entitled the "State Bureau of Investigations."

(d) MILITARY ARREST ORDERS. Any arrest warrant or military arrest order issued pursuant to this Title which involves members of the Mayflower National Guard, their property, or matters under the jurisdiction of the Military Police thereof, shall be executed by the Mayflower National Guard Military Police.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 1802.1. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: When the officer takes property under the warrant, he must give a receipt for the property take
sections.text: When the officer takes property under the warrant, he must give a receipt for the property taken (specifying it in detail) to the person from whom it was taken by him, or in whose possession it was found; or, in the absence of any person, he must leave it in the place where he found the property.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this Chapter, the term "political subdivision" shall have the same meaning
sections.text: For the purposes of this Chapter, the term "political subdivision" shall have the same meaning as the definition adopted in Article III of the Constitution.

sections.heading: The State of Mayflower shall constitute a single judicial district for each political subdivisi
sections.text: The State of Mayflower shall constitute a single judicial district for each political subdivision.

sections.heading: The Governor, with and by consent of the Senate shall appoint district judges for the District
sections.text: The Governor, with and by consent of the Senate shall appoint district judges for the District Courts of the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The Chief Judge of the district shall be designated by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflo
sections.text: The Chief Judge of the district shall be designated by the Chief Justice of the State of Mayflower from the pool of incumbent district judges.

sections.heading: Business of court shall be distributed among the judges in accordance with rules and orders est
sections.text: Business of court shall be distributed among the judges in accordance with rules and orders established by the Court. The Chief Judge of the respective district court shall ensure the observance of such rules, orders, and shall be responsible for the allocation of business and assignment of causes, unless, there is a rule provided otherwise.

sections.heading: In the event of judges unable to agree on the adoption of a rule, or order by the respective Ch
sections.text: In the event of judges unable to agree on the adoption of a rule, or order by the respective Chief Judge, the Supreme Court shall be empowered to issue necessary orders.

sections.heading: A District Court may vote to adjourn, by majority vote, for no more than two (2) days, as a who
sections.text: A District Court may vote to adjourn, by majority vote, for no more than two (2) days, as a whole, for a national holiday.

sections.heading: When the office of a district judge becomes vacant, all pending process, pleadings, and proceed
sections.text: When the office of a district judge becomes vacant, all pending process, pleadings, and proceedings shall be continued by the clerk, as necessary, until a judge is appointed or designated to preside over the court.

sections.heading: If a party to any proceeding in a district court submits a timely and sufficient affidavit asse
sections.text: If a party to any proceeding in a district court submits a timely and sufficient affidavit asserting that the judge presiding over the matter has a personal bias or prejudice either against the party or in favor of an opposing party, that judge shall cease to proceed further in the case. Another judge shall then be assigned to hear the matter. The affidavit must show good cause and reason.

sections.heading: A court of the State of Mayflower shall have power to punish by fine or imprisonment, or both,
sections.text:
A court of the State of Mayflower shall have power to punish by fine or imprisonment, or both, at its discretion, such contempt of its authority, and none other, as—

(a) misbehavior of any person in its presence or so near thereto as to obstruct the administration of justice;

(b) misbehavior of any of its officers in their official transactions; or

(c) disobedience or resistance to its lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree, or command.

sections.heading: This section shall not be construed to circumvent the restrictions of the contempt authority of
sections.text: This section shall not be construed to circumvent the restrictions of the contempt authority of a magistrate judge, absent the approval of a district court judge.

sections.heading: No individual may be appointed as a magistrate unless they have been a member in good standing
sections.text: No individual may be appointed as a magistrate unless they have been a member in good standing of the bar of the State of Mayflower for at least two (2) months.

sections.heading: The term of a full time magistrate shall be three (3) months
sections.text: The term of a full time magistrate shall be three (3) months. Upon the expiration of their term, a magistrate may continue to perform duties until a successor is appointed, or fifteen (15) days, whichever is shorter.

sections.heading: A magistrate may be removed from office during their term solely on the grounds of incompetence
sections.text: A magistrate may be removed from office during their term solely on the grounds of incompetence, misconduct, neglect of duty, or physical or mental incapacity. Such removal shall require the concurrence of a majority of the appointing judges. The magistrate shall be provided with a detailed specification of the charges and afforded an opportunity to respond to the charges before any final decision is made.

sections.heading: Magistrates may not hold any civil office under the State of Mayflower unless specifically appr
sections.text: Magistrates may not hold any civil office under the State of Mayflower unless specifically approved by the Judicial Conference.

sections.heading: Magistrates are permitted to practice law in private or on behalf of the government
sections.text: Magistrates are permitted to practice law in private or on behalf of the government.

sections.heading: A candidate for magistrate may be appointed by the Governor, subject to the advice and consent
sections.text: A candidate for magistrate may be appointed by the Governor, subject to the advice and consent of the Senate.

sections.heading: Each magistrate appointed under this section shall have authority within the district where the
motions for injunctive relief
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 2203.1(a). Review: some legacy subsections omitted

sections.heading: A judge may reconsider any pretrial matter determined by a magistrate under this section where
sections.text: A judge may reconsider any pretrial matter determined by a magistrate under this section where it is demonstrated that the magistrate’s decision is clearly erroneous or contrary to law.

sections.heading: A judge may, by order, designate a magistrate to conduct hearings, including evidentiary hearin
sections.text: A judge may, by order, designate a magistrate to conduct hearings, including evidentiary hearings, and to submit to the judge proposed findings of fact and recommendations for the disposition of any matter excepted under this section.

sections.heading: At the conclusion of any hearing conducted under this section, the magistrate shall transmit to
sections.text:
At the conclusion of any hearing conducted under this section, the magistrate shall transmit to the judge all papers and documents relating to the case, including the magistrate's findings of fact and recommendations;
a statement confirming that notice of the findings and recommendations, along with the right to request a hearing before the judge, has been duly given to all parties.

sections.heading: The magistrate shall file with the court any proposed findings and recommendations made under t
sections.text: The magistrate shall file with the court any proposed findings and recommendations made under this section, and shall cause a copy thereof to be served upon all parties forthwith.

sections.heading: The judge shall adopt, modify, or reject the magistrate's recommendations no later than the fif
sections.text: The judge shall adopt, modify, or reject the magistrate's recommendations no later than the fifth working day after the date the judge receives the recommendations. If the judge does not take action within the time provided by this subsection, the recommendations of the magistrate shall be deemed adopted by the judge.

sections.heading: Any party may, within fourteen (14) days of being served with a copy of the proposed findings a
sections.text: Any party may, within fourteen (14) days of being served with a copy of the proposed findings and recommendations, file written objections thereto in accordance with the rules of court.

sections.heading: Upon consideration of any objections duly filed under this section, a judge shall make a de nov
sections.text: Upon consideration of any objections duly filed under this section, a judge shall make a de novo determination of the matters objected to, and may accept, reject, or modify, in whole or in part, the findings or recommendations made by the magistrate, receive further evidence, or remit the matter to the magistrate with directions.

sections.heading: A magistrate shall not be permitted or assigned to any category of cases that include
sections.text:
A magistrate shall not be permitted or assigned to any category of cases that include:

(a) questions of vast economic and political significance;

(b) cases in which the state is seeking imposition of capital punishment; or

(c) cases that involve a significant and complex constitutional issue.

sections.heading: A magistrate appointed under this act shall, within the jurisdiction prescribed by their appoin
sections.text: A magistrate appointed under this act shall, within the jurisdiction prescribed by their appointment, possess the authority to exercise contempt powers as set out in this section.

sections.heading: A magistrate shall have the authority to summarily punish, by fine or imprisonment, or both, an
sections.text: A magistrate shall have the authority to summarily punish, by fine or imprisonment, or both, any contempt committed in their presence that constitutes misbehavior obstructing the administration of justice for no more than . Such an order of contempt shall be issued in accordance with the applicable rules of criminal procedure.

sections.heading: In any case where a magistrate presides with the consent of the parties, or in any misdemeanor
sections.text: In any case where a magistrate presides with the consent of the parties, or in any misdemeanor case proceeding before a magistrate, the magistrate shall have the authority to punish criminal contempt involving disobedience or resistance to the magistrate’s lawful writ, process, order, rule, decree, or command, by fine or imprisonment, or both. Such contempt proceedings shall be conducted with appropriate notice and hearing, as provided by the rules of criminal procedure.

sections.heading: Appeals of a magistrate’s contempt order under this Clause shall be directed to the appropriate
sections.text: Appeals of a magistrate’s contempt order under this Clause shall be directed to the appropriate appellate court in cases proceeding with the consent of the parties, or to the higher court in other cases

sections.heading: A magistrate’s order imposing imprisonment for contempt shall not exceed twenty (20) minutes in
sections.text: A magistrate’s order imposing imprisonment for contempt shall not exceed twenty (20) minutes in total unless a District Court Judge co-signs the order. Any contempt order resulting in imprisonment beyond twenty (20) minutes shall be presented to a judge for review and co-signature.

sections.heading: No fine imposed by a magistrate for contempt shall exceed the amount of three hundred (300) dol
sections.text: No fine imposed by a magistrate for contempt shall exceed the amount of three hundred (300) dollars.

sections.heading: The assigned judge on a case may revoke a Magistrate's order to hold a subject in contempt if t
sections.text: The assigned judge on a case may revoke a Magistrate's order to hold a subject in contempt if there is a good reason and cause at any time.

sections.heading: The Chief Judge shall promptly review any complaint received against any District Judge
sections.text:
The Chief Judge shall promptly review any complaint received against any District Judge. In deciding appropriate recourse of action the Chief Judge may elect to run a limited inquiry to determine:

(a) if appropriate corrective action has or can be taken without formal investigation; and

(b) whether the facts in the complaint are manifestly untrue, or incapable to investigate.

sections.heading: The Chief Judge may request the judge concerned to provide a written response
sections.text: The Chief Judge may request the judge concerned to provide a written response. The response shall be confidential and not released. The Chief Judge shall refrain from making determination of fact on any matters that are reasonably contested.

sections.heading: Following the review, the Chief Judge may, by written order accompanied by stated reasons
sections.text:
Following the review, the Chief Judge may, by written order accompanied by stated reasons:

(a) Dismiss the complaints if it is found not to be directly concerned with a merit of a judicial decision, procedural ruling or be frivolous, unsupported by sufficient evidence to suggest misconduct, or consist of allegations that cannot be proven by investigation.

(b) Dismiss the complaint where the preliminary inquiry shows lack of foundation or conclusively disproved by objective evidence.

(c) Conclude the matter if corrective action has been taken.

sections.heading: Copies of any order made in relation to the judicial complaint must be made public
sections.text: Copies of any order made in relation to the judicial complaint must be made public.

sections.heading: Any party aggrieved by a final order, under this section may seek a review by petitioning to th
sections.text: Any party aggrieved by a final order, under this section may seek a review by petitioning to the Supreme Court.

sections.heading: The Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower may suspend any judge(s) power to continue hearing
sections.text: The Supreme Court of the State of Mayflower may suspend any judge(s) power to continue hearing cases pending disposition of a hearing.

sections.heading: Cases in the Supreme Court may be reviewed by the Supreme Court through the following means, bu
Any individual who intentionally and voluntarily caused the reasonable apprehension of an immed
sections.text: Any individual who intentionally and voluntarily caused the reasonable apprehension of an immediate harmful or offensive contact to another individual shall be liable for assault and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who brought about an unconsented harmful or offensive contact with a person or t
sections.text: Any individual who brought about an unconsented harmful or offensive contact with a person or to something closely associated with that person shall be liable for battery and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thirty thousand (230,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who, without legal authority or justification, restrains or restricts a person's
sections.text: Any individual who, without legal authority or justification, restrains or restricts a person's movement within an area, or restrains the person’s permission is false imprisonment and shall be liable for punitive damages up to three hundred thousand (300,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual or entity whose negligence, wrongful act, or breach of duty results in the death
sections.text: Any individual or entity whose negligence, wrongful act, or breach of duty results in the death of another person without that person’s consent, shall be liable for wrongful death and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one million (1,000,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Every person who, under color of any statute, ordinance, regulation, custom, or usage, subjects
sections.text: Every person who, under color of any statute, ordinance, regulation, custom, or usage, subjects, or causes to be subjected, any citizen of the State of Mayflower or other person within the jurisdiction thereof to the deprivation of any rights, privileges, or immunities secured by the Constitution and laws, shall be liable for deprivation of rights to the party injured in an action at law, suit in equity, or other proper proceeding for redress, except that in any action brought against a judicial officer for an act or omission taken in such officer’s judicial capacity, injunctive relief shall not be granted unless a declaratory decree was violated or declaratory relief was unavailable.

sections.heading: If two or more persons conspire, for the purpose of depriving, either directly or indirectly, a
sections.text: If two or more persons conspire, for the purpose of depriving, either directly or indirectly, any person or class of persons of the equal protection of the laws, or of equal privileges and immunities under the laws; or for the purpose of preventing or hindering the constituted authorities of the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions from giving or securing to all persons within the State the equal protection of the laws; in any case of conspiracy set forth in this section, if one or more persons engaged therein do, or cause to be done, any act in furtherance of the object of such conspiracy, whereby another is injured in his person or property, or deprived of having and exercising any right or privilege, the party so injured or deprived may have an action for the recovery of damages occasioned by such injury or deprivation, against any one or more of the conspirators.

sections.heading: If two or more persons conspire to deter, by force, intimidation, or threat, any party or witne
sections.text: If two or more persons conspire to deter, by force, intimidation, or threat, any party or witness in any court of the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions from attending such court, or from testifying to any matter pending therein, freely, fully, and truthfully, or to injure such party or witness in their person or property on account of their having so attended or testified; or if two or more persons conspire for the purpose of impeding, hindering, obstructing, or defeating, in any manner, the due course of justice in the State of Mayflower or its political subdivisions, with intent to deny to any citizen the equal protection of the laws, or to injure them or their property for lawfully enforcing, or attempting to enforce, the right of any person, or class of persons, to the equal protection of the laws, they shall be liable for civil conspiracy to obstruct justice and for damages arising therefrom.

sections.heading: Any individual who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent person would
sections.text: Any individual who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent person would under similar circumstances, resulting in harm to another individual, shall be liable for negligence and shall be liable for punitive damages up to five hundred thousand (500,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who violates a statute or regulation designed to protect a specific class of ind
sections.text: Any individual who violates a statute or regulation designed to protect a specific class of individuals from harm, and whose violation directly causes injury to another individual, shall be liable for negligence per se and shall be liable for punitive damages up to six hundred seventy five thousand (675,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who fails to perform a contractual obligation as agreed, without lawful excuse,
sections.text: Any individual who fails to perform a contractual obligation as agreed, without lawful excuse, and causes harm to the other party, shall be liable for breach of contract and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred fifty thousand (150,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any employer who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent employer would
sections.text: Any employer who fails to exercise the degree of care that a reasonably prudent employer would under similar circumstances in hiring an employee, resulting in harm caused by the employee to another individual, shall be liable for negligent hiring and shall be liable for punitive damages up to four hundred thousand (400,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who intentionally enters the land of another without lawful excuse shall be liab
sections.text: Any individual who intentionally enters the land of another without lawful excuse shall be liable for trespass to land and shall be liable for punitive damages up to seventy five thousand (75,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who intentionally interferes with the personal property of another shall be liab
sections.text: Any individual who intentionally interferes with the personal property of another shall be liable for trespass to chattels and shall be liable for punitive damages up to fifty thousand (50,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who intentionally interferes with the property of another with the intent to dep
sections.text: Any individual who intentionally interferes with the property of another with the intent to deprive the owner of the property shall be liable for conversion and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred thousand (100,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual or organization that spreads a false and unprivileged publication by writing, pr
sections.text: Any individual or organization that spreads a false and unprivileged publication by writing, printing, picture, effigy, or other fixed representation to the eye, which exposes any person to hatred, contempt, ridicule, or obloquy, or which causes him to be shunned or avoided, or which has a tendency to injure him in his occupation shall be liable for libel and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred fifty thousand (150,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who orally utters a false and unprivileged publication that exposes a person to
sections.text: Any individual who orally utters a false and unprivileged publication that exposes a person to hatred, contempt, or ridicule or which injures their reputation shall be liable for slander and shall be liable for punitive damages up to seventy five thousand (75,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who uses a legal process for an ulterior purpose, with the intention of achievin
sections.text: Any individual who uses a legal process for an ulterior purpose, with the intention of achieving a result not intended by the process, shall be liable for abuse of process and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who initiates a legal proceeding without probable cause, with malice or intent t
sections.text: Any individual who initiates a legal proceeding without probable cause, with malice or intent to harm, and the proceeding terminates in favor of the accused, shall be liable for malicious prosecution and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

sections.heading: It shall be unlawful for any governmental authority, or any agent thereof, or any person acting
sections.text:
It shall be unlawful for any governmental authority, or any agent thereof, or any person acting on behalf of a governmental authority, to engage in a pattern or practice of conduct by law enforcement officers that deprives persons of rights, privileges, or immunities secured or protected by the Constitution or laws of the State of Mayflower or Union of Columbia.

(a) Whenever the Attorney General has reasonable cause to believe that a violation of 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.5 has occurred, the Attorney General, for or in the name of the State of Mayflower, may in a civil action obtain appropriate equitable and declaratory relief to eliminate the pattern or practice.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.5. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual who is a public servant and commits an act relating to his office but constitute
sections.text:
Any individual who is a public servant and commits an act relating to his office but constitutes an unauthorized exercise of his official functions, where a reasonable person with his training, expertise, and experiences should know that such act is unauthorized; or refrains from performing a duty which is imposed upon him by law or is clearly inherent in the nature of his office.

(a) The plaintiff must prove that the official misconduct from that individual caused injury to himself, and that the plaintiff is entitled to relief from the courts.

(b) Any individual who is a public servant and commits the aforementioned shall be liable for compensatory damages; injunctive reliefs restraining the individual from performing a certain action, or orders instructing the individual to perform a certain action; and punitive damages up to $75,000

(c) Such suits shall proceed in a form of quasi-official capacity, such that the defendants shall be named as parties in official capacity; however if the courts or an arbitrator wish to provide monetary damages to the plaintiff, then it shall be the duty of the defendant’s individual capacity to pay such damages as ordered.

sections.heading: Any individual who willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or engages in a pa
sections.text:
Any individual who willfully, maliciously, and repeatedly follows, harasses, or engages in a pattern of conduct directed at another individual that would cause a reasonable person to feel fear for their own safety shall be liable for the tort of stalking and may be subject to punitive damages up to two hundred and fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

(a) The individual aggrieved by such conduct may seek relief in the form of an injunction or declaratory judgment.

(b) Upon a verified petition and showing of conduct that would support a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7, a court may issue a temporary injunction for protection against stalking, effective for no more than fourteen (14) days provided the petition establishes that the respondent’s conduct would cause a reasonable person to fear for their safety; such an order may be granted without notice to the other party. An injunction may be extended until final judgment only upon a showing of irreparable harm, or a substantial threat thereof, to the petitioner; such an order may only be granted with notice to the other party. A party must first initiate a claim under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7 to petition for an injunction under this subsection.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3104.7. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any individual who publicly discloses information about another that places the individual in a
sections.text: Any individual who publicly discloses information about another that places the individual in a false light, and where the false light would be highly offensive to a reasonable person and was made with knowledge of or reckless disregard for its falsity, shall be liable for false light invasion of privacy and punitive damages up to fifty thousand (50,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who knowingly makes a false representation with the intent to deceive another, a
sections.text: Any individual who knowingly makes a false representation with the intent to deceive another, and where such representation is reasonably relied upon and causes actual harm, shall be liable for fraud. The injured party may recover compensatory damages and, where appropriate, punitive damages up to seven hundred fifty thousand dollars (750,000).

sections.heading: Any individual who intentionally interferes with a contractual or business relationship between
sections.text: Any individual who intentionally interferes with a contractual or business relationship between other parties, causing harm to one of the parties, shall be liable for tortious interference and shall be liable for punitive damages up to one hundred seventy five (175,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who enters into an agreement with two or more parties to deprive a third party o
sections.text: Any individual who enters into an agreement with two or more parties to deprive a third party of legal rights or to deceive a third party in order to achieve an illegal objective, resulting in harm to the third party, shall be liable for civil conspiracy and shall be liable for punitive damages up to three hundred thousand (300,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who knowingly discloses or misappropriates confidential business information or
sections.text: Any individual who knowingly discloses or misappropriates confidential business information or trade secrets without authorization and with the intent to gain an unfair competitive advantage shall be liable for misappropriation of trade secrets and shall be liable for punitive damages up to two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who, with intent to obtain money, property, services, or other benefit, knowingl
sections.text: Any individual who, with intent to obtain money, property, services, or other benefit, knowingly threatens to expose, accuse, disgrace, or otherwise harm another unless such benefit is provided, and whose threat causes harm or coerced compliance, shall be liable for civil extortion and punitive damages up to three hundred seventy fifty thousand (375,000) dollars.

sections.heading: Any individual who, in breach of a fiduciary duty, acts contrary to the interests of the benefi
sections.text: Any individual who, in breach of a fiduciary duty, acts contrary to the interests of the beneficiary by engaging in self-dealing, nondisclosure, or other disloyal conduct resulting in harm, shall be liable for breach of fiduciary duty and subject to compensatory and punitive damages up to five hundred thousand dollars (500,000).

sections.heading: In all cases of tortious conduct, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek remedies that i
sections.text:
In all cases of tortious conduct, the aggrieved party shall be entitled to seek remedies that include but are not limited to, compensatory damages, punitive damages, injunctive relief, and any other relief deemed appropriate by the court. The availability of remedies for each tort is not exclusive or limiting, and the non-exclusion of any particular remedy does not preclude its application or availability in any specific case.

(a) Where the court finds that the tortious conduct was willful, malicious, reckless, or part of a pattern of repeated misconduct, it may, in the interest of justice, award punitive damages in excess of any statutory cap otherwise imposed by this title.

sections.heading: As used in this act, the term “state agency” includes the executive departments, the judicial a
sections.text: As used in this act, the term “state agency” includes the executive departments, the judicial and legislative branches, the military departments, independent establishments of the State of Mayflower, and corporations primarily acting as instrumentalities or agencies of the State of Mayflower, but does not include any contractor with the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: “Employee of the government” includes (1) officers or employees of any state agency, members of
sections.text: “Employee of the government” includes (1) officers or employees of any state agency, members of the National Guard while engaged in training or duty, and persons acting on behalf of a state agency in an official capacity, temporarily or permanently in the service of the state, whether with or without compensation, and (2) any officer or employee of a state public defender organization, except when such officer or employee performs professional services in the course of providing representation.

sections.heading: “Acting within the scope of his office or employment,” in the case of a member of the National
sections.text: “Acting within the scope of his office or employment,” in the case of a member of the National Guard means acting in line of duty.

sections.heading: The government shall be immune from all claims except those in this subchapter, and later laws
sections.text: The government shall be immune from all claims except those in this subchapter, and later laws in which liability is explicitly created against the government.

sections.heading: No monetary damage shall be awarded in a case against the government, cases where the governmen
sections.text: No monetary damage shall be awarded in a case against the government, cases where the government is a party, or cases where the government has intervened, unless the government has consented to it through a statutory waiver.

sections.heading: The Solicitor General may accept settlements on behalf of the government and issue orders or de
sections.text: The Solicitor General may accept settlements on behalf of the government and issue orders or decrees in line with those settlements such that they are within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

sections.heading: The Solicitor General may intervene with the government as a defendant in cases against one’s i
sections.text: The Solicitor General may intervene with the government as a defendant in cases against one’s individual capacity if they were in fact serving in an official capacity - or the government has a substantial interest in the outcome of the suit.

sections.heading: The Solicitor General may refuse to defend an agent of the government if they were clearly acti
sections.text: The Solicitor General may refuse to defend an agent of the government if they were clearly acting in an individual capacity, or in a capacity that is not in line with the laws, directives, orders, policies, or standard operating procedures of the government and its agencies.

sections.heading: Qualified immunity shall not be a valid affirmative defense if the Solicitor General refuses to
sections.text: Qualified immunity shall not be a valid affirmative defense if the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government.

sections.heading: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, and the torts are allege
sections.text: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, and the torts are alleged under this section, then the Solicitor General shall provide the relief as requested within the bounds of the law, charter, and constitution.

sections.heading: The courts shall dismiss with prejudice all claims in which the Solicitor General refuses to de
sections.text: The courts shall dismiss with prejudice all claims in which the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent, and that the Solicitor General provides relief as requested within the law, charter, and constitution.

sections.heading: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, then that agent shall be
sections.text: If the Solicitor General refuses to defend an agent of the government, then that agent shall be liable for the equitable offenses in his individual capacity, and the government shall cease to be a party and have interest in the case.

sections.heading: Any individual seeking compensation for damages or other forms of relief, declaratory, injuncti
sections.text: Any individual seeking compensation for damages or other forms of relief, declaratory, injunctive, or otherwise, arising from tortious acts authorized by this section against the state, county, or municipal agencies and employees of the State and any political or administrative subdivision thereof must submit their claim to the Department of Justice. The claim should include detailed information about the nature of the tort, the alleged wrongful conduct, and the damages sought. The Attorney General shall prescribe regulations that detail additional elements that must be included in a claim.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.1. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Upon receipt of the claim, the Department of Justice shall have a set period of seven (7) days
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: If the Department of Justice chooses to deny the claim, then it shall be construed as a final d
sections.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to deny the claim, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.3. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: If the Department of Justice chooses to request for more information, the claimant must respond
sections.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to request for more information, the claimant must respond within seven (7) days. If the claimant does so within this window, then the Department of Justice shall receive five (5) more days to process the claim. If the Department of Justice does not enter any action on the claim within this window, then it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b). If the claimant does not provide the Department of Justice with the requested information within this window, then the Department of Justice shall not be required to review the claim any further and it shall be construed as if the claim was never sent to the Department of Justice.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.4. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: If the Department of Justice chooses to open arbitration, it must end within ten days of its in
sections.text: If the Department of Justice chooses to open arbitration, it must end within ten days of its initiation. In the event that it does not end within ten days, it shall be construed as a final denial for the purposes of this act, similar to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.2(b).
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.5. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: An individual must file a claim within three months from the date the claim accrued
sections.text: An individual must file a claim within three months from the date the claim accrued. Failure to file the claim within this specified period will result in the claim being barred and therefore not actionable in a State court.

sections.heading: An action shall not be instituted upon a claim against the State of Mayflower, or any political
sections.text: An action shall not be instituted upon a claim against the State of Mayflower, or any political or administrative subdivision thereof for relief for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment, unless the claimant shall have first presented the claim to the Department of Justice and his claim shall have been finally denied by the agency in writing. The failure of the Department of Justice to make final disposition of a claim within one (1) month after it is filed shall, at the option of the claimant at any time thereafter, be deemed a final denial of the claim for purposes of this section.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Action under this section shall not be instituted for any sum in excess of the amount of the cl
sections.text: Action under this section shall not be instituted for any sum in excess of the amount of the claim presented to the Department of Justice, except where the increased amount is based upon newly discovered evidence not reasonably discoverable at the time of presenting the claim to the Department of Justice, or upon allegation and proof of intervening facts, relating to the amount of the claim.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.2. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Disposition of any claim by the Attorney General or his designee shall not be competent evidenc
sections.text: Disposition of any claim by the Attorney General or his designee shall not be competent evidence of liability or amount of damages.

sections.heading: The Attorney General or his designee, may consider, ascertain, adjust, determine, compromise, a
sections.text: The Attorney General or his designee, may consider, ascertain, adjust, determine, compromise, and settle any claim for money damages against the State of Mayflower for injury or loss of property or personal injury or death caused by the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the agency while acting within the scope of his office or employment, under circumstances where the State of Mayflower, if a private person, would be liable to the claimant in accordance with the law of the place where the act or omission occurred.

sections.heading: Subject to the provisions of this title relating to civil actions on tort claims against the St
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of this title relating to civil actions on tort claims against the State of Mayflower, any such award, compromise, settlement, or determination shall be final and conclusive on all officers of the Government, except when procured by means of fraud.

sections.heading: The acceptance by the claimant of any such award, compromise, or settlement shall be final and
sections.text: The acceptance by the claimant of any such award, compromise, or settlement shall be final and conclusive on the claimant, and shall constitute a complete release of any claim against the State of Mayflower and against the employee of the government whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, by reason of the same subject matter.

sections.heading: The Attorney General or his designee, shall report semiannually to the Legislature all claims p
sections.text: The Attorney General or his designee, shall report semiannually to the Legislature all claims paid by it under 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3204.1-3204.3, stating the name of each claimant, the amount claimed, the amount awarded, and a brief description of the claim.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3206.1. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The State of Mayflower shall be liable, respecting the provisions of this title relating to tor
sections.text: The State of Mayflower shall be liable, respecting the provisions of this title relating to tort claims, in the same manner and to the same extent as a private individual under like circumstances, but shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for punitive damages.

sections.heading: If, however, in any case wherein death was caused, the State of Mayflower shall be liable for a
sections.text: If, however, in any case wherein death was caused, the State of Mayflower shall be liable for actual or compensatory damages, measured by the pecuniary injuries resulting from such death to the persons respectively.

sections.heading: With respect to any claim under this chapter, the State of Mayflower shall be entitled to asser
