sections.text: With respect to any claim under this chapter, the State of Mayflower shall be entitled to assert any defense based upon judicial or legislative immunity which otherwise would have been available to the employee of the State of Mayflower whose act or omission gave rise to the claim, as well as any other defenses to which the State of Mayflower is entitled.

sections.heading: The Attorney General or his designee may arbitrate, compromise, or settle any claim initiated,
sections.text: The Attorney General or his designee may arbitrate, compromise, or settle any claim initiated, after the commencement of an action thereon.

sections.heading: The remedy against the State of Mayflower provided by this act for injury or loss of property,
sections.text: The remedy against the State of Mayflower provided by this act for injury or loss of property, or personal injury or death arising or resulting from the negligent or wrongful act or omission of any employee of the Government while acting within the scope of his office or employment is exclusive of any other civil action or proceeding for money damages by reason of the same subject matter against the employee whose act or omission gave rise to the claim. Any other civil action or proceeding for money damages arising out of or relating to the same subject matter against the employee is precluded without regard to when the act or omission occurred.

sections.heading: The previous paragraph does not extend or apply to a civil action against an employee of the Go
sections.text:
The previous paragraph does not extend or apply to a civil action against an employee of the Government—

(a) which is brought for a violation of the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, or

(b) which is brought for a violation of a statute of the State of Mayflower under which such action against an individual is otherwise authorized.

sections.heading: The Solicitor General shall defend any civil action or proceeding brought in any court against
sections.text: The Solicitor General shall defend any civil action or proceeding brought in any court against any employee of the Government for any such damage or injury.

sections.heading: The Solicitor General shall certify whether the defendant employee was acting within the scope
sections.text: The Solicitor General shall certify whether the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose.

sections.heading: Upon certification by the Solicitor General that the defendant employee was acting within the s
sections.text: Upon certification by the Solicitor General that the defendant employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment at the time of the incident out of which the claim arose, any civil action or proceeding commenced upon such claim in a Mayflower district court shall be deemed an action against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

sections.heading: In the event that the Solicitor General has refused to certify scope of office or employment un
sections.text: In the event that the Solicitor General has refused to certify scope of office or employment under this section, the employee may at any time before trial petition the court to find and certify that the employee was acting within the scope of his office or employment. Upon such certification by the court, such action or proceeding shall be deemed to be an action or proceeding brought against the State of Mayflower under the provisions of this title and all references thereto, and the State of Mayflower shall be substituted as the party defendant.

sections.heading: Whenever an action or proceeding in which the State of Mayflower is substituted as the party de
sections.text:
Whenever an action or proceeding in which the State of Mayflower is substituted as the party defendant under this subsection is dismissed for failure first to present a claim pursuant to 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1, such a claim shall be deemed to be timely presented under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.2 if—

(a) the claim would have been timely had it been filed on the date the underlying civil action was commenced, and

(b) the claim is presented to the Department of Justice within fifteen days after dismissal of the civil action.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.7. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Every civil action commenced against the State of Mayflower shall be barred unless the complain
sections.text: Every civil action commenced against the State of Mayflower shall be barred unless the complaint is filed within three months after the right of action first accrues.

sections.heading: A tort claim against the State of Mayflower shall be forever barred unless it is presented in w
sections.text: A tort claim against the State of Mayflower shall be forever barred unless it is presented in writing to the Department of Justice within three months after such claim accrues.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3210.2. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The provisions of this act shall not apply to
sections.text:
The provisions of this act shall not apply to:

(a) Any claim based upon an act or omission of an employee of the Government, exercising due care, in the execution of a statute or regulation, whether or not such statute or regulation be valid, or based upon the exercise or performance or the failure to exercise or perform a discretionary function or duty on the part of a state agency or an employee of the Government, whether or not the discretion involved be abused.

(b) Any claim arising out of the combatant activities of the national guard, during time of war.

(c) Any claim arising in a foreign country.

(d) Any claim arising from the assessment or collection of any customs duty, or the detention of any goods, merchandise, or other property by any port authority officer or other law enforcement officer, applies to claims based on injury or loss of goods, merchandise, or other property while in the possession of these officers if—

(i) the property was seized for the purpose of forfeiture under any provision of state law providing for the forfeiture of property other than as a sentence imposed upon conviction of a criminal offense;

(ii) the interest of the claimant was not forfeited;

(iii) the interest of the claimant was not remitted or mitigated (if the property was subject to forfeiture); and

(iv) the claimant was not convicted of a crime for which the interest of the claimant in the property was subject to forfeiture under a state criminal forfeiture law.

sections.heading: Any law, policy, order, procedure, action, or directive that impedes on an individuals rights,
sections.text:
Any law, policy, order, procedure, action, or directive that impedes on an individuals rights, immunities, or privileges secured by law, charter, or the constitution shall be subject to the injunctive relief of a permanent restraining order against the government prohibiting them from enacting this policy, order, procedure, action, or directive; and injunctive relief reversing any harm done.

(a) Plaintiffs must demonstrate that they received, or are at an imminent threat of receiving, concrete, non-hypothetical harm from the law, policy, order, procedure, action or directive.

(b) The courts may subpoena any sensitive policy, procedure, order, or directive that relates to the issue.

sections.heading: Public officials sued in their individual capacity for conduct engaged in the course of their d
sections.text:
Public officials sued in their individual capacity for conduct engaged in the course of their duties shall be immune from claims at law unless—

(a) Their course of conduct transgresses a legal right; and

(b) The offending official knew or should have known about that legal right; or

(c) The legal right would not have otherwise been transgressed if the officer were acting in accordance with their training, policy, directives, or the law.

sections.heading: Any public official who refrains from performing a duty lawfully imposed on their office or cle
sections.text:
Any public official who refrains from performing a duty lawfully imposed on their office or clearly inherent to it, or who engages in a course of conduct relating to their office but constituting an unauthorized exercise of their official functions, is liable to the party injured.

(a) Suits under this provision shall proceed against a Defendant’s quasi-official capacity such that the official office shall be liable for the equitable remedy and the individual capacity of the Defendant shall be liable for the monetary damages.

(b) The party injured may obtain relief in the form of compensatory damages, punitive damages, and injunctive relief ordering a certain action to be taken or restraining a certain action from being taken.

(c) The Solicitor General shall represent Defendants sued in accordance with this provision.

(i) The Solicitor General, at their discretion, and upon careful consideration of the State’s sovereign interests, may refuse to represent an individual sued in accordance with this provision.

sections.heading: Any person subject to the directive authority of the Attorney General in accordance with Articl
sections.text:
Any person subject to the directive authority of the Attorney General in accordance with Article VI, section 3 of the Mayflower Constitution who violates a lawful order or directive issued by the Attorney General may be subject to suit at the discretion of the Attorney General on behalf of the State who shall have a cause of action for injunctive relief and punitive damages not exceeding two hundred thousand (200,000) dollars against the offending individual.

(a) The State of Mayflower may sue parens patriae and may sue in its sovereign capacity for injury to its own interests.

sections.heading: All sections of this act shall apply retroactively to all claims arising from tortious acts tha
sections.text: All sections of this act shall apply retroactively to all claims arising from tortious acts that occurred prior to the enactment of this act, including the time that has elapsed between the date of release, the twenty-fourth of August, 2001, to the date of this act’s completion, provided that the claim has not been previously settled or adjudicated.

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as the "Mayflower Tort Claims Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as the "Mayflower Tort Claims Act."

sections.heading: In this Subtitle, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pro
sections.text: In this Subtitle, any reference to a pronoun shall be interpreted to include all respective pronouns, regardless of gender. Terms such as 'he,' 'him,' or 'his' shall be deemed to include 'she,' 'her,' 'hers,' 'they,' 'them,' 'theirs,' or any other pronoun as applicable. This inclusive interpretation applies to all provisions, ensuring gender neutrality and inclusivity throughout this Subtitle.

sections.heading: The term “physician” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “physician” shall refer to:

(a) Any member employed or appointed to the State Medical Examiner’s Office as a medical doctor.

(b) Any employee of a fire department, selected by their department head, with the necessary qualifications prescribed in standards written by the respective fire department.

(c) Any otherwise qualified individual to deliver medical advice and opinions pursuant to the judgment of the County Fire Chief.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4101. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as the "Capital Punishment Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as the "Capital Punishment Act."

sections.heading: “Capital punishment” or “death penalty” shall be defined as the judgment of death upon an indiv
sections.text: “Capital punishment” or “death penalty” shall be defined as the judgment of death upon an individual convicted of a crime described in this act as a “capital felony”.

sections.heading: A “capital felony” shall refer to any of the following crimes listed in this subsection that sh
sections.text:
A “capital felony” shall refer to any of the following crimes listed in this subsection that shall be punishable by death upon the court deeming such sentence appropriate, unless otherwise provided further by law:

(a) 1 M.S.C. § 1105 "Treason."

(b) 1 M.S.C. § 1104 "Criminal Anarchy."

(c) 1 M.S.C. § 1102 "Espionage."

(d) 1 M.S.C. § 2101 "First-degree murder."
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4202. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: A “death warrant” shall refer to the issuance of a warrant by the court upon a judgment of deat
sections.text: A “death warrant” shall refer to the issuance of a warrant by the court upon a judgment of death ordering for the search and seizure of all property, seizure of all properties leased, burning of any vehicles, aircrafts or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed, as well as capital punishment to be executed at a specific date prescribed by the court.

sections.heading: A person, upon whom has been imposed the judgment of death, shall be transferred to the custody
sections.text: A person, upon whom has been imposed the judgment of death, shall be transferred to the custody and care of the Attorney General through the Mayflower State Police.

sections.heading: A death warrant shall be signed by the Court upon a judgment of death
sections.text:
A death warrant shall be signed by the Court upon a judgment of death.

(a) A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences unless otherwise prescribed.

sections.heading: A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or re
sections.text: A death warrant shall allow the search and seizure of all property stored within vehicles or residences, the seizure of all properties leased, burning of all vehicles, aircrafts, or boats owned, seizure of all money, and revocation of all certifications held from the individual imposed.

sections.heading: Upon the completion of the death warrant seizure and the issuance of a warrant receipt to the c
sections.text:
Upon the completion of the death warrant seizure and the issuance of a warrant receipt to the court. The court shall issue the maximum sentence time allowed by law within the in-game interface.

(a) If there is no maximum sentence limit, then the court shall issue a jail sentence of no more than 3 days, and no less than 1 day.

sections.heading: The judgment of death shall be executed either at the Mayflower State Detention Complex, or at
sections.text:
The judgment of death shall be executed either at the Mayflower State Detention Complex, or at any Mayflower National Guard base confined within a military exclusion zone.

(a) The Mayflower National Guard may not inhibit the movement or access of civilian law enforcement, prescribed witnesses, or attorneys present for the purposes of the execution.

sections.heading: The punishment of death shall be carried out by firing squad
sections.text:
The punishment of death shall be carried out by firing squad.

(a) Four (4) Troopers from the Mayflower State Police shall be appointed to serve as members of the firing squad, with one (1) Trooper at the rank of Sergeant or above serving as leader of the firing squad.

(b) If selected officers from either the Mayflower State Police are unavailable, The Department of Justice may request the use of other law enforcement officials from municipal or county political subdivision(s) to meet the requirement listed in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4306(a).
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4306. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Department of Justice shall develop rules and standards for the method and process of execu
sections.text: The Department of Justice shall develop rules and standards for the method and process of execution that do not violate the person’s constitutional rights.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4307. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: A physician may attend an execution for the purpose of pronouncing death and may provide advice
sections.text:
A physician may attend an execution for the purpose of pronouncing death and may provide advice to officials for the purpose of developing an execution protocol to minimize the risk of pain to the inmate.

(a) The presence of a physician is not required unless prescribed by standards written by the Department of Justice or by mandate of the court.

(b) The physician, upon completion of the execution will prescribe and record the time of death of the inmate to be presented in the death warrant and returned to the court.

(c) If there is no physician present, the ranking official of the Justice Department present during the execution will record the time of death.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4308. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Department of Justice may allow witnesses to be present during the execution
sections.text:
The Department of Justice may allow witnesses to be present during the execution;

(a) No more than ten (10) members may be present, not including officials carrying out the punishment.

(b) No person shall be a witness to an execution unless they are a resident of the State of Mayflower.

(c) At the request of the inmate, spiritual members or ministers of the gospel shall be permitted to be present at the execution not exceeding more than one person.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4309. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Upon the completion of the execution, a death certificate shall be issued by the State Medical
sections.text:
Upon the completion of the execution, a death certificate shall be issued by the State Medical Examiners’ Office with the time of recorded death, cause of death, and other necessary information prescribed in developed policy.

(a) The cause of death shall be listed as "lead poisoning," unless the execution is carried out by alternative means.

(b) The certificate shall be issued to the recipient and the Department of Justice in a timely manner.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 4310. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The death certificate issued shall be enforceable upon signature by the Chief Medical Examiner,
sections.text: The death certificate issued shall be enforceable upon signature by the Chief Medical Examiner, and cannot be challenged by the recipient alone without a legal petition to the Mayflower Supreme Court.

sections.heading: A person imposed with a judgment of death by a court of law may petition an appeal of their sen
sections.text:
A person imposed with a judgment of death by a court of law may petition an appeal of their sentence to the Mayflower Supreme Court for a stay of execution.

(a) They shall be remanded in the custody of the Mayflower State Police until their hearing.

sections.heading: Any sentence of death upon acceptance of a Writ of Certiorari shall be stayed and paused until
sections.text: Any sentence of death upon acceptance of a Writ of Certiorari shall be stayed and paused until a decision by the Supreme Court is made in favor or against an appeal.

sections.heading: The Governor may grant a Stay of Execution to anyone whom is scheduled to be executed, indefini
sections.text: The Governor may grant a Stay of Execution to anyone whom is scheduled to be executed, indefinitely postponing their execution unless said stay is vacated by the Governor.

sections.heading: “Justified homicide” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 5 M
sections.text: “Justified homicide” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 7101.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 5101. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: “Trespassing” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 1 M
sections.text: “Trespassing” shall refer to the provisions as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3205.

sections.heading: “Attempting to trespass” shall refer to the attempt to commit a violation of 1 M
sections.text: “Attempting to trespass” shall refer to the attempt to commit a violation of 1 M.S.C § 3205.

sections.heading: “Trespassers” shall be defined as anyone actively trespassing or attempting to trespass
sections.text: “Trespassers” shall be defined as anyone actively trespassing or attempting to trespass.

sections.heading: “Unauthorized third party” shall refer to any person who is occupying or attempting to occupy p
sections.text: “Unauthorized third party” shall refer to any person who is occupying or attempting to occupy private property without authorization.

sections.heading: “Innocent third party” shall refer to any person who is not in the commission of a crime
sections.text: “Innocent third party” shall refer to any person who is not in the commission of a crime.

sections.heading: “Identifiable public servant” shall refer to any person employed within the Mayflower National
sections.text: “Identifiable public servant” shall refer to any person employed within the Mayflower National Guard, any Union of Columbia Law Enforcement Agency, Lee County Transportation Authority, or Lee County Regional Hospital who is acting in their official capacity, and is easily marked by a department or company uniform. Law enforcement officers who are in an unmarked capacity as defined by specific department policy shall be considered easily identifiable if they are wearing a badge of their respective agency on their person.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 5107. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: This chapter may be cited as "The Castle Doctrine Act
sections.text: This chapter may be cited as "The Castle Doctrine Act."

sections.heading: A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest for using lethal, or any degree
sections.text: A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest for using lethal, or any degree of force less-than-lethal, given it is a Justified Homicide.

sections.heading: A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims
sections.text: A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is actively trespassing or attempting to trespass and has been given ample warning(s) to leave and reasonable time to do so.

sections.heading: A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims
sections.text:
A person is justified in and cannot face prosecution nor arrest and is immune from civil claims for using lethal or less-than-lethal force if an unauthorized third party is—

(a) has committed 1 M.S.C. § 3201 (Breaking and entering) and is actively trespassing on private property; or

(b) is actively attempting to commit breaking and entering.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 5203. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: A person is justified justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from
sections.text:
A person is justified justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:

(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would cause serious bodily injury or death.

(b) The innocent third party is actively being kidnapped.

(c) The innocent third party is actively a victim of armed robbery as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3101.

sections.heading: A person is justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil clai
sections.text:
A person is justified in, and cannot face prosecution nor arrest, and is immune from civil claims for using less-than-lethal force in defense of an innocent third party given:

(a) The innocent third party is actively being assaulted to a degree that would not cause serious bodily injury or death.

(b) The innocent third party is actively being robbed as defined in 1 M.S.C § 3102.

sections.heading: Except as otherwise expressly provided, a prosecution may only be commenced for a felony offens
Except as otherwise expressly provided, a prosecution may only be commenced for a misdemeanor o
sections.text:
Except as otherwise expressly provided, a prosecution may only be commenced for a misdemeanor offense—

(a) where involving the unauthorized distribution, possession, or sale of police-grade or non-civilian equipment, or misconduct on the part of any employee of the government, within forty (40) days;

(b) where involving the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against another person or property of another, or any conspiracy to that effect, within forty-five (45) days; and

(c) in any such other case, within thirty (30) days.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this section, a prosecution is deemed commenced when—
sections.text:
For the purposes of this section, a prosecution is deemed commenced when—

(a) an indictment, information, or complaint is filed; or

(b) an arrest or bench warrant is issued, provided that the warrant names or describes the defendant with the same degree of particularity required for an indictment, information, or complaint.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the offense is committed,
sections.text:
For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the offense is committed, and does not run during a time where—

(a) the accused is not a resident or inhabitant of the State; or

(b) the accused hides himself within the State or otherwise renders himself non-amenable to processes being served upon him.

sections.heading: Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to offenses committed or pro
sections.text: Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to offenses committed or prosecutions commenced before the date of enactment.

sections.heading: Except as otherwise expressly provided, a civil action may only be commenced for a tort—
sections.text:
Except as otherwise expressly provided, a civil action may only be commenced for a tort—

(a) where pursuant to title 5, subtitle 1, chapter 3, subchapter 1, parts 1, 2, and 4, Mayflower State Code, within forty (40) days;

(b) where pursuant to title 5, subtitle 1, chapter 3, subchapter 1, parts 3 and 5, Mayflower State Code, within thirty-five (35) days; and

(c) in any such other case, within thirty (30) days.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this section, a civil action is deemed commenced whenacivil complaint or ma
sections.text: For the purposes of this section, a civil action is deemed commenced whenacivil complaint or matter is filed or docketed with a court of competent jurisdiction.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the tort is committed, an
sections.text:
For the purposes of this section, time starts to run on the day after the tort is committed, and does not run during a time where—

(a) the tortfeasor is not a resident or inhabitant of the State; or

(b) the tortfeasor hides himself within the State or otherwise renders himself non-amenable to processes being served upon him.

sections.heading: Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to torts committed or civil
sections.text: Nothing in this section shall be construed nor read so as to apply to torts committed or civil actions commenced before the date of enactment.

sections.heading: All felony criminal convictions in the State of Mayflower are eligible for the following convic
sections.text:
All felony criminal convictions in the State of Mayflower are eligible for the following conviction sentencing guidelines, applicable at the discretion of the sentencing court:

(a) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 1, Chapter VII “Prohibited Items” may carry a penalty of up to two times its statutory sentence.

(b) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 2 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Against the Player” may carry a penalty of up to four times its statutory sentence.

(c) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 3 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Against Property” may carry a penalty of up to two times its statutory sentence.

(d) All codified offenses under Title 1, Subtitle 6 of the Mayflower State Code “Crimes Involving Firearms and Explosives” may carry a penalty of up to three times its statutory sentence.

(e) All aforementioned guidelines shall be applicable to both the codified sentence and citation penalties.

(i) No citation imposed with respect to these guidelines shall exceed a total of $25,000.00 UCD.

sections.heading: When pursed through a criminal trial, the maximum incarceration time that can be awarded for a—
sections.text:
When pursed through a criminal trial, the maximum incarceration time that can be awarded for a—

(a) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be eighteen (18) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(b) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Criminal Code shall be thirteen (13) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(c) Felony class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be fifteen (15) times the length of its usual standard sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

(d) Misdemeanor class offense with an Active status within the Mayflower Vehicle Code shall be ten (10) times the length of its standard prison sentence length, rounded to the highest minute.

sections.heading: No person shall be sentenced to a cumulative term of imprisonment exceeding one hundred twenty
sections.text: No person shall be sentenced to a cumulative term of imprisonment exceeding one hundred twenty (120) hours for violations or enhancements imposed solely under this subchapter with respect to statutes designated as Active status, regardless of the number or combination of applicable enhancements. Statutes designated as By Conviction shall be exempt from this limitation, and any sentence authorized under such statutes may be imposed in addition to the maximum cumulative term permitted under Active status statutes.

sections.heading: “Qualified immunity” means legal protection shielding a law enforcement officer from civil liab
sections.text: “Qualified immunity” means legal protection shielding a law enforcement officer from civil liability for actions performed in the line of duty, unless the officer’s conduct violates clearly established statutory or constitutional rights of which a reasonable person would have known.

sections.heading: A law enforcement officer shall not be held personally liable for civil damages for any act or
sections.text:
A law enforcement officer shall not be held personally liable for civil damages for any act or omission arising out of the performance of their duties, if such act or omission—

(a) was not manifestly outside the scope of the officer’s lawful authority; and

(b) did not violate a clearly established right of which a reasonable law enforcement officer would have known.

sections.heading: Any motion to dismiss based on qualified immunity shall be decided by the court as a matter of
sections.text: Any motion to dismiss based on qualified immunity shall be decided by the court as a matter of law prior to trial. A court may grant qualified immunity at any stage of litigation.

sections.heading: Nothing in parts (1), (2), or (3) of this subchapter shall be construed to limit criminal prose
sections.text: Nothing in parts (1), (2), or (3) of this subchapter shall be construed to limit criminal prosecution of an officer for conduct constituting a criminal offense under state or local law.

sections.heading: Qualified immunity shall not apply where a law enforcement officer is found, by clear and convi
sections.text:
Qualified immunity shall not apply where a law enforcement officer is found, by clear and convincing evidence, to have—

(a) acted with malicious intent to cause harm;

(b) engaged in conduct that shocks the conscience; or

(c) willfully violated state constitutional rights.

sections.heading: Qualified immunity shall not apply to actions taken by officers that are entirely unrelated to
sections.text: Qualified immunity shall not apply to actions taken by officers that are entirely unrelated to their duties, or while acting in a purely personal or private capacity.

sections.heading: Homicide by any person is justifiable when
For the purposes of this act, the term “euthanasia” or “euthanization” shall refer to the succe
sections.text: For the purposes of this act, the term “euthanasia” or “euthanization” shall refer to the successful act of committing a homicide or otherwise causing the death of another person in a manner wholly compliant with subchapter (II) of this act.

sections.heading: The term “authorized healthcare provider” shall refer to any employee, agent, or assign of the
sections.text: The term “authorized healthcare provider” shall refer to any employee, agent, or assign of the Lee County Regional Hospital, a private healthcare contractor for Lee County, Mayflower, who has completed training and maintains a Paramedic certification, or the RHC540 certification course; or any employee, agent, or assign of the same who holds a doctorate degree in medicine from any accredited university within the Union of Columbia.

sections.heading: Any person who conducts a lawful euthanization under the complete compliance of the provisions
sections.text:
Any person who conducts a lawful euthanization under the complete compliance of the provisions of this act shall be free from criminal liability and prosecution for the actions taken to conduct that euthanization, including freedom from liability for the crimes of:

(a) Any crime that would otherwise have been considered to be committed under Title 1, Subtitle 2 of the Mayflower State Code, excepting crimes committed that were reasonably unnecessary or otherwise medically irrelevant to the euthanization process.

(b) Any crime that would otherwise have been considered to be committed under Title 1, Subtitle 7, Chapter I of the Mayflower State Code, excepting crimes committed that were reasonably unnecessary or otherwise medically irrelevant to the euthanization process.

sections.heading: Euthanasia shall be considered lawful when conducted by any individual who is not an authorized
Euthanasia shall be considered lawful when conducted by an individual who is an authorized heal
Any individual who conducts a euthanization and subsequently faces law enforcement investigatio
sections.text: Any individual who conducts a euthanization and subsequently faces law enforcement investigation, detainment, subpoena or other search and seizure shall bear the burden of proof for statutory compliance, and such proof shall evidently show the entire euthanization process from start to finish and the actions taken to meet all statutory requirements to render the euthanization lawful; and that no negligence occurred to where any statutory condition becomes unsatisfied.

sections.heading: Any individual who fails to meet any statutory requirement stipulated by this act when conducti
sections.text: Any individual who fails to meet any statutory requirement stipulated by this act when conducting a euthanization, or otherwise conducts a euthanization under a provision that they do not otherwise meet the conditions and authorization for shall not be protected under section (a) of this subchapter and shall face full criminal liability for any conduct that would otherwise be considered a criminal action notwithstanding euthanasia.

sections.heading: An individual shall be guilty of 1 M
sections.text:
An individual shall be guilty of 1 M.S.C. § 2101 “First-degree murder” when they—

(a) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in the commission or attempted commission of one of the following crimes:

(i) 1 M.S.C. § 1302 “Felony Misconduct."

(ii) 1 M.S.C. § 1308 “Felony Evasion."

(iii) 1 M.S.C. § 1311 “Escape."

(iv) 1 M.S.C. § 1312 “Obstruction of Justice."

(v) 1 M.S.C. § 4103 “Inciting a Riot."

(b) Kill, or causes another individual to be killed, while in commission or attempted commission of a felony under the following sections of Title 1 of the Mayflower State Code:

(i) Subtitle 1, Chapter I.

(ii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VI.

(iii) Subtitle 1, Chapter VIII.

(iv) Subtitle 2, Chapter II.

(v) Subtitle 3, Chapter I.

(vi) Subtitle 3, Chapter II.

(vii) Subtitle 4, Chapter III.

(viii) Subtitle 5 or 6.

(c) Are jointly engaged in the commission or attempted commission of any aforementioned felony, and does so with another individual who commits 1 M.S.C. § 2101 First-degree murder in the course of such a felony, and who thereafter continues to participate in any criminal conduct with that individual following the commission of said murder.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 1 § 9101. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: SHORT TITLE
sections.text: SHORT TITLE. This chapter may be cited as the "Federal Civil Rights Claims Enforcement Act."

sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.text: DEFINITIONS. The term “Union” or “Union of Columbia” shall refer to the United States of America.

sections.heading: The term “federal civil rights law” shall refer to any law of the Union of Columbia codified in
sections.text: The term “federal civil rights law” shall refer to any law of the Union of Columbia codified in Title 42 of the Union of Columbia Code that protects individual rights against unlawful discrimination, official misconduct, or deprivation of rights under color of law, including but not limited to 42 U.S.C. §§ 1981, 1982, 1983, 1985, 1986 and related provisions.

sections.heading: “Person” shall include any natural person, corporation, partnership, association, union, or oth
sections.text: “Person” shall include any natural person, corporation, partnership, association, union, or other legal entity, and where applicable, includes individuals acting under color of law.

sections.heading: The term “color of law” shall mean any act done by a government official, employee, or agent—wh
sections.text: The term “color of law” shall mean any act done by a government official, employee, or agent—whether lawful or unlawful—that is made possible by the authority or appearance of authority granted by law.

sections.heading: The term “court of competent jurisdiction” shall refer to any trial court of general or limited
sections.text: The term “court of competent jurisdiction” shall refer to any trial court of general or limited jurisdiction established by the laws of the State of Mayflower that is authorized to hear civil cases.

sections.heading: The term “state actor” shall include any official, employee, or agent of the State of Mayflower
sections.text: The term “state actor” shall include any official, employee, or agent of the State of Mayflower or any of its subdivisions, municipalities, or public institutions, as well as any person or entity acting jointly or in concert with such officials or institutions.

sections.heading: Pursuant to the sovereign legislative authority of the State of Mayflower and in accordance wit
sections.text: Pursuant to the sovereign legislative authority of the State of Mayflower and in accordance with Article One, Section Eleven of the Constitution thereof, the causes of action enumerated in subsection (b) of this Section are hereby adopted into law and may be enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower.

sections.heading: The following federal civil rights statutes, as interpreted and applied by the courts of the Un
sections.text:
The following federal civil rights statutes, as interpreted and applied by the courts of the Union of Columbia, are hereby given force and effect as state law:

(a) 42 U.S.C. § 1981.

(b) 42 U.S.C. § 1982.

(c) 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

(d) 42 U.S.C. § 1985.

(e) 42 U.S.C. § 1986.

sections.heading: Any court of general jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower is hereby vested with subject m
sections.text: Any court of general jurisdiction within the State of Mayflower is hereby vested with subject matter jurisdiction to hear, adjudicate, and render final judgment on any civil action brought under this Section. Venue, standing, justiciability, and procedural posture shall be determined in accordance with the laws of this State, except where such standards would contravene the substantive rights incorporated herein.

sections.heading: Courts of this State shall be empowered to award all forms of legal and equitable relief author
sections.text: Courts of this State shall be empowered to award all forms of legal and equitable relief authorized under the incorporated provisions, including compensatory and punitive damages (where applicable), declaratory and injunctive relief, costs of litigation, reasonable attorney’s fees, and such other relief as may be necessary to effectuate the remedial purposes of the adopted statutes.

sections.heading: The defenses of qualified immunity, absolute immunity, and any other immunities recognized unde
sections.text: The defenses of qualified immunity, absolute immunity, and any other immunities recognized under the laws of the Union of Columbia shall apply with equal force and effect to actions brought under this Section, unless otherwise abrogated by an act of the legislature or prohibited by the Constitution of the State of Mayflower. No immunity of the State, its political subdivisions, or any of its officers shall operate to bar claims brought under this Section unless expressly preserved by statute.

sections.heading: The provisions of this Section shall be interpreted in pari materia with the laws of the courts
sections.text: The provisions of this Section shall be interpreted in pari materia with the laws of the courts of the Union of Columbia. In construing the scope, contours, and operative effect of the incorporated statutes, courts shall afford persuasive and, where appropriate, controlling weight to decisions of the Supreme Court and subordinate tribunals of the Union interpreting such statutes, unless a deviation is compelled by state constitutional mandate or express legislative instruction.

sections.heading: Nothing in this Section shall be construed to preclude or displace the availability of causes o
sections.text: Nothing in this Section shall be construed to preclude or displace the availability of causes of action under the Constitution or laws of the State of Mayflower. A claimant may pursue remedies under both state and federal authority simultaneously or in the alternative.

sections.heading: Unless otherwise provided by statute or the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, all civil a
sections.text: Unless otherwise provided by statute or the Constitution of the State of Mayflower, all civil actions arising under subchapter 2 of this chapter shall be governed by the rules of civil procedure as promulgated by the Supreme Court of Mayflower, including rules of pleading, service of process, discovery, joinder, and appeal. Where such rules are silent or ambiguous, courts may reference federal procedural precedent for guidance, provided such reliance does not conflict with the laws of this State.

sections.heading: Actions brought pursuant to this Act shall be subject to the following limitations periods, whi
Equitable tolling, estoppel, or other doctrines recognized under the common law of this State m
sections.text: Equitable tolling, estoppel, or other doctrines recognized under the common law of this State may apply to actions brought under this Act, provided that such doctrines are not inconsistent with the remedial purposes of the incorporated provisions. No right of action under this Act shall be deemed extinguished due to inadvertent mislabeling or mispleading, provided the claim arises from the same nucleus of operative fact.

sections.heading: A complaint alleging a cause of action under this Act shall contain a short and plain statement
Any final judgment rendered under this Act shall be accorded full force and effect throughout t
sections.text: Any final judgment rendered under this Act shall be accorded full force and effect throughout the State and shall operate as a final adjudication on the merits, subject to the doctrines of res judicata and collateral estoppel as applied by the courts of this State.

sections.heading: This Section shall be liberally construed to ensure the broad protection and full enforcement o
sections.text: This Section shall be liberally construed to ensure the broad protection and full enforcement of civil rights, and no technical defect in form shall be grounds for dismissal where substantive rights may still be adjudicated on the merits.

sections.heading: Subject to the provisions of 5 M
sections.text: Subject to the provisions of 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3201–3209, the State of Mayflower, its agencies, and its employees acting within the scope of their official duties shall not be deemed to have waived sovereign immunity except where such waiver is explicitly authorized by statute. Nothing in this Act shall be construed to create a general waiver of sovereign immunity beyond what is provided in those sections.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1401. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, no individual, agency, or subdivision of the S
sections.text: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, no individual, agency, or subdivision of the State of Mayflower shall be liable for punitive damages in any civil action brought under this Act. The State shall not be liable for interest prior to judgment or for damages beyond those authorized in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3207.1.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1402. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Liability for compensatory damages in actions against the State, its agencies, or employees sha
sections.text: Liability for compensatory damages in actions against the State, its agencies, or employees shall be limited to actual economic loss, consistent with the standards and procedures set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 §§ 3203–3205. No action for money damages may be instituted unless a claim is first submitted to the Department of Justice in accordance with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3204.1.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1403. Review: legacy cross-references need checking; agency compatibility review

sections.heading: State officials and employees shall be entitled to qualified immunity in individual-capacity su
sections.text: State officials and employees shall be entitled to qualified immunity in individual-capacity suits brought under this Act, unless the Solicitor General certifies under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3209.4 that the official was acting outside the scope of employment, or unless the plaintiff shows a violation of a clearly established constitutional or statutory right of which a reasonable person would have known.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1404. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Nothing in this Section shall be construed to provide immunity for acts of malfeasance, gross n
sections.text: Nothing in this Section shall be construed to provide immunity for acts of malfeasance, gross negligence, or willful misconduct, where such acts fall outside the scope of employment or otherwise fail to meet the standards of protection under 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.5.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1405. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: This Act does not impair a plaintiff’s right to seek equitable relief, including injunctive or
sections.text: This Act does not impair a plaintiff’s right to seek equitable relief, including injunctive or declaratory relief, against the State, its agencies, or subdivisions for violations of civil rights, provided such relief is consistent with constitutional limits and does not conflict with 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3202.2.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1406. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: Any claim for relief under this Act must comply with the procedural requirements set forth in 5
sections.text: Any claim for relief under this Act must comply with the procedural requirements set forth in 5 M.S.C. 1 § 3203.6, including the three-month filing deadline from the date the cause of action accrues. Failure to comply with these requirements shall bar the claim.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 5 M.S.C. 2 § 1407. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The State shall not be liable for claims based on conduct occurring before the effective date o
sections.text: The State shall not be liable for claims based on conduct occurring before the effective date of this Act, unless the plaintiff demonstrates that timely filing was prevented by fraud, concealment, or misconduct by the defendant, consistent with equitable tolling doctrines recognized under State law.

sections.heading: It shall be the duty of the courts of the State of Mayflower to ensure that all actions brought
sections.text: It shall be the duty of the courts of the State of Mayflower to ensure that all actions brought under this Act are handled in a timely and efficient manner. The court shall make every reasonable effort to resolve such cases without unnecessary delay, consistent with the complexity of the case and the rights of the parties involved. The court may, in its discretion, issue scheduling orders to ensure the expeditious progression of the case.

sections.heading: In any action brought under this Act, the court may, upon motion by a party or sua sponte, gran
sections.text: In any action brought under this Act, the court may, upon motion by a party or sua sponte, grant summary judgment when it finds that there is no genuine issue of material fact and that the movant is entitled to judgment as a matter of law. Summary judgment may be entered at any stage of the proceedings, including prior to trial, when the facts and law are sufficiently clear to resolve the dispute.

sections.heading: In all actions brought under this Act, the court shall have broad discretion in determining the
sections.text: In all actions brought under this Act, the court shall have broad discretion in determining the appropriate remedies, sanctions, and procedural steps, provided that such actions are consistent with the principles of justice, fairness, and the protection of civil rights. This discretion shall extend to the management of case schedules, the granting of extensions, and the determination of the propriety of evidentiary rulings.

sections.heading: Any judicial officer, attorney, or party involved in a case under this Act who has reason to be
sections.text: Any judicial officer, attorney, or party involved in a case under this Act who has reason to believe that misconduct has occurred in the course of the proceedings, including but not limited to fraud, bribery, or abuse of power, shall have a duty to report such misconduct to the appropriate disciplinary authority or to the court itself.

sections.heading: In the event that a defendant fails to respond to a complaint brought under this Act within the
sections.text: In the event that a defendant fails to respond to a complaint brought under this Act within the time prescribed by law, the court may enter a default judgment against the defendant. The plaintiff shall be entitled to proceed with the case as though the defendant had admitted liability, unless the court finds good cause to set aside the default.

sections.heading: In any case involving a settlement of claims under this Act, the court shall review the terms o
sections.text: In any case involving a settlement of claims under this Act, the court shall review the terms of the settlement to ensure that the agreement is fair, adequate, and in the best interests of justice, particularly where the settlement involves claims on behalf of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups.

sections.heading: In any action brought under this Act, the prevailing party shall be entitled to remedies, as ap
sections.text: In any action brought under this Act, the prevailing party shall be entitled to remedies, as applicable and consistent with the nature of the violation.

sections.heading: In cases where the defendant’s actions were willful, malicious, or reckless, the court may awar
sections.text: In cases where the defendant’s actions were willful, malicious, or reckless, the court may award punitive damages to punish the defendant and deter future violations. Such damages shall be determined based on the defendant’s conduct and the need to deter similar behavior in the future.

sections.heading: The court may issue an order for injunctive relief to prevent further harm, including but not l
The court may issue a declaratory judgment to determine the rights, duties, and obligations of
sections.text: The court may issue a declaratory judgment to determine the rights, duties, and obligations of the parties involved, particularly where there is uncertainty about the application of the law to the facts of the case.

sections.heading: The prevailing party shall be entitled to attorneys’ fees and litigation costs incurred in brin
sections.text: The prevailing party shall be entitled to attorneys’ fees and litigation costs incurred in bringing or defending the action. The court may also award such fees and costs to the defendant if the court finds that the plaintiff's claim was frivolous or without merit.

sections.heading: Each day that a violation of this Act continues shall be considered a separate offense for purp
sections.text: Each day that a violation of this Act continues shall be considered a separate offense for purposes of calculating remedies, penalties, and enforcement actions. The court shall have discretion to impose additional penalties for each day a violation persists.

sections.heading: All remedies and penalties under this Section may be enforced by the courts of the State of May
sections.text: All remedies and penalties under this Section may be enforced by the courts of the State of Mayflower, including the issuance of orders of execution, garnishment, or other mechanisms as necessary to ensure compliance with any judgment, injunction, or restitution order.

sections.heading: The amount of punitive damages awarded in any case under this Act shall not exceed three (3) ti
sections.text: The amount of punitive damages awarded in any case under this Act shall not exceed three (3) times the amount of compensatory damages, except where the defendant’s actions are determined to be particularly egregious or where statutory exceptions apply.

sections.heading: Any party who prevails in an action under this Act shall have the right to recover any penaltie
sections.text: Any party who prevails in an action under this Act shall have the right to recover any penalties or damages awarded as part of the judgment, through any available lawful means of enforcement, including execution of judgment or garnishment.

sections.heading: It shall be unlawful for any person, entity, or government official to retaliate against any in
sections.text:
It shall be unlawful for any person, entity, or government official to retaliate against any individual for exercising their rights under this Act, including but not limited to:

(a) Any individual who files or has filed a civil rights claim under this Act shall not be subject to retaliation, including threats, harassment, or adverse action taken against them in employment or in other aspects of their personal life.

(b) No person shall face retaliation for providing testimony, evidence, or assistance in any civil rights action brought under this Act, even if the action is ultimately dismissed or withdrawn.

(c) No person shall be retaliated against for opposing practices or policies that they reasonably believe to be discriminatory or violative of civil rights under this Act.

sections.heading: Retaliation under this Section includes, but is not limited to
sections.text:
Retaliation under this Section includes, but is not limited to:

(a) Any adverse employment action, as stipulated under Title 4, Subtitle 7, Chapter 1, against an individual for exercising their rights under this Act.

(b) Physical or verbal harassment, threats of violence, or actions intended to intimidate or coerce an individual for asserting their civil rights.

(c) Refusal to provide goods, services, or benefits to an individual or group because they have exercised their civil rights or filed a claim.

(d) Any deliberate efforts to harm an individual's reputation, relationships, or social standing through wrongful means as a result of their involvement in civil rights litigation.

sections.heading: Any person who proves retaliation under this Section shall be entitled to the following remedie
sections.text:
Any person who proves retaliation under this Section shall be entitled to the following remedies:

(a) As provided in paragraph 1601 of this chapter, compensatory damages for harm suffered as a result of retaliation, including but not limited to:

(i) Harm to reputation or social standing;

(ii) Loss of opportunities for advancement.

(b) As provided in paragraph 1602 of this chapter, the court may award punitive damages if the retaliation is found to be willful, malicious, or grossly negligent.

(c) The court may issue an order requiring the defendant to cease retaliation or restore the affected individual's rights or benefits.

(d) Where an individual's employment, services, or benefits were adversely affected by retaliation, the court may order the restoration of such rights or benefits, including re-employment or reinstatement to the same position.

(e) As provided in paragraph 1605 of this chapter, the prevailing party may be entitled to reimbursement for attorneys' fees and litigation costs incurred as a result of the retaliation claim.

sections.heading: In any action alleging retaliation, the plaintiff shall be required to demonstrate, by a prepon
Nothing in this Section shall be construed to waive any other legal remedies available to indiv
sections.text: Nothing in this Section shall be construed to waive any other legal remedies available to individuals under state law for retaliation, nor shall it limit any rights individuals may have to bring a separate cause of action under applicable laws for retaliatory conduct outside of the provisions of this Act.

sections.heading: The term “State highway” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “State highway” shall refer to:

(a) The Jones Beltway

(b) State Route 55

(c) Any road operated by the State or any political subdivision thereof with a posted speed limit of greater then seventy (70) studs per second.

sections.heading: State Highways and Public Roads may not be subject to full closure without the permission of th
sections.text: State Highways and Public Roads may not be subject to full closure without the permission of the Secretary of Transportation, Colonel of the State Police, the Governor, a municipal police chief, or a county sheriff.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1102. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The stud per second unit shall be analogous and equivalent to the mile per hour unit
sections.text: The stud per second unit shall be analogous and equivalent to the mile per hour unit.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall be responsible for the maintenance, upkeep, and ad
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall be responsible for the maintenance, upkeep, and administration of all highway entrances and exits, public roads, state highways, and overpasses within the state.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the even
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occurring on any overpass, public roadway, highway entrance or exit, or state highway.

sections.heading: Members of the Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the authority to enact reduced spe
DESYNCING
sections.text: DESYNCING. “Desyncing” shall refer to the act of purposefully swerving a vehicle across a lane whilst at high speeds to exploit a bug that causes any vehicles behind the actor to be flung about and crash.

sections.heading: “Law Enforcement Officer” shall refer to any peace officer formally recognised under the state
sections.text: “Law Enforcement Officer” shall refer to any peace officer formally recognised under the state code as a Law Enforcement Officer, holds an active LETI certification and is an on-duty officer of a Law Enforcement Agency.

sections.heading: The act of desyncing a vehicle shall be considered as reckless driving and shall be arrestable
sections.text: The act of desyncing a vehicle shall be considered as reckless driving and shall be arrestable under the ‘Reckless Driving’ offence in the Mayflower State Vehicle Code, at the discretion of the arresting law enforcement officer.

sections.heading: All law enforcement officers whilst on-duty and protecting the peace shall be exempt from this
sections.text: All law enforcement officers whilst on-duty and protecting the peace shall be exempt from this law and may utilize desyncing at their discretion during pursuits/as per their department standard operating procedure code.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1110. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Citizens acting in a vigilante capacity to assist law enforcement officers in the apprehension
sections.text: Citizens acting in a vigilante capacity to assist law enforcement officers in the apprehension of a fleeing suspect that drive recklessly in the commission of desyncing a suspect, shall not be exempt from the aforementioned law and may be arrested per the discretion of a law enforcement officer.

sections.heading: A “road Closure” or “full Road Closure” shall be defined as the blockage and/or restriction of
sections.text: A “road Closure” or “full Road Closure” shall be defined as the blockage and/or restriction of a roadway from civilians and/or individuals who are not essential to the given situation or circumstance(s). The individual(s) who are restricted from the closed roadway shall be designated at the discretion of the individual leading or commanding the circumstance/situation/incident that caused the road closure.

sections.heading: A “road closure” shall also include the partial restriction and/or blockage of a roadway
sections.text: A “road closure” shall also include the partial restriction and/or blockage of a roadway. Any government authority authorized by this section to initiate a road closure may initiate a partial road closure instead. The term “Road Closure” shall also include a partial road closure any time it is referenced in this section.

sections.heading: A “partial road closure” shall be defined as a road closure that does not require a detour and
sections.text: A “partial road closure” shall be defined as a road closure that does not require a detour and still allows two-way travel on the partially closed road.

sections.heading: The term “roadway," “road,” or "highway" includes a common and public highway, street, avenue,
sections.text: The term “roadway," “road,” or "highway" includes a common and public highway, street, avenue, parkway, driveway, square, place, bridge, viaduct or trestle, any part of which is intended for or used for the passage of vehicles and includes the area between the lateral property lines thereof.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to execute the closure of certain
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the ability to execute the closure of certain roads, either in the support of a law enforcement closure or for maintenance and repair to road infrastructure.

sections.heading: Law enforcement officers execute road closures for
sections.text:
Law enforcement officers execute road closures for:

(a) The preservation of a crime scene

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.

(e) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or endanger the lives of responding officers, or hinder the ability to combat crime

(f) Situation where the flow of traffic on a roadway near the situation may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1206. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Fire/Rescue personnel may execute road closures for
sections.text:
Fire/Rescue personnel may execute road closures for:

(a) Any active scene relating to their official duties, where the flow of traffic may endanger or obstruct on-scene personnel or patients

(b) The securing of governmental or non-governmental property in connection with an authorized exercise of authority

(c) Officer or civilian safety in light of ongoing criminal activity

(d) An approved event, either a civilian assembly/event with the permission of the County Sheriff or State Police Colonel, or a government-sanctioned event with the approval of the relevant department head.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1207. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Fire/Rescue Services at the Municipal and County levels may also execute the closure of certain
sections.text: Fire/Rescue Services at the Municipal and County levels may also execute the closure of certain roads in connection with active fire/rescue scenes, training, or operations.

sections.heading: Medical services, both private and government-owned, may close off the immediate area, includin
sections.text: Medical services, both private and government-owned, may close off the immediate area, including roads, connected to a medical call or situation.

sections.heading: Specific roads or streets may be closed for government events or training at the direction of a
sections.text: Specific roads or streets may be closed for government events or training at the direction of a Department Head or Governor.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1210. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Civilians wishing to host an assembly, event, or demonstration may, with or without connection
sections.text: Civilians wishing to host an assembly, event, or demonstration may, with or without connection to a protest permit, request for the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority to order the closure of certain roads connected to said assembly, event, or demonstration.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1211. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Any person who stands on any equipment placed on or near any highway with the textual markings
sections.text: Any person who stands on any equipment placed on or near any highway with the textual markings containing "POLICE" that could or may obstruct the efficacy of the equipment shall be guilty of Obstruction of Justice.

sections.heading: The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall have the
sections.text:
The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall have the authority to execute the closure of roads going one-hundred-fifty (150) studs before, or across, through, or around any tunnel or bridge under their administration, or anywhere else where it requires, for maintenance or upkeep of public infrastructure, or any other scene relating to their official duties, that being a fire, rescue, or medical scene.

(a) Should the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission need to establish a closure on a roadway or state highway more than one-hundred-fifty (150) studs before or around any tunnel or bridge they gain authorization pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1102.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1213. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee, shall be responsible for publishing a road
sections.text:
The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee, shall be responsible for publishing a road closures handbook, which may be aesthetically renamed, that promulgates the rules and regulations for conducting road closures, partial road closure, checkpoints, or modifying the speed limit on a public road, as decided by the Secretary of Transportation.

(a) The road closures handbook must contain rules about, but shall not be limited to include:

(i) Placing signage that warns drivers about road closures ahead;

(ii) Placing signage that warns drivers about changed road conditions on the road ahead; and

(iii) Placing signage that notifies drivers when a road closure or changed road condition has ended.

(b) Any authority that is authorized to conduct a road closure or partial road closure must comply with this handbook.

(c) The Secretary of Transportation may direct the Mayflower Transportation Police to issue citations or arrest any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1214. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: Any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook shall be liable to be issued
sections.text: Any individual who does not comply with the road closures handbook shall be liable to be issued a citation or arrested for 2 M.S.C. § 1211 “Obstruction of Traffic”.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1215. Review: legacy cross-references need checking

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority (hereinafter “Mayflower Transportation Authority”, “Tran
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Authority (hereinafter “Mayflower Transportation Authority”, “Transportation Authority”, “Authority”, or “MTA”) shall be a subordinate agency of the Mayflower Department of Transportation.

(a) The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall provide public transit, road maintenance, traffic accident management, and other related services.

(i) The Transportation Authority shall provide these services to every county political subdivision with a population of at least twenty-thousand (20,000) state residents, or if the county political subdivision houses the capital of the State.

(b) The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall be responsible for all public urban rail transit systems primarily designed for the mass transportation of passengers within a metropolitan area or between metropolitan areas.

(c) The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall administer and maintain public transit systems, routes and infrastructure which shall include the following:

(i) Bus Stops.

(ii) Bus Terminals.

(1) This shall not include Bus Terminals administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit.

(iii) Subway Terminals.

(1) This shall not include Subway Terminals administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Trans-Henry Railroad.

(iv) Subway Stations.

(1) This shall not include Subway Stations administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Trans-Henry Railroad.

(v) Subway Platforms.

(1) This shall not include Subway Platforms administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Trans-Henry Railroad.

(vi) Subway Tunnels.

(1) This shall not include Subway Tunnels administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Trans-Henry Railroad.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1301. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Secretary of Transportation shall have oversight of the authority and appoint an Administra
sections.text: The Secretary of Transportation shall have oversight of the authority and appoint an Administrator, who shall serve at the pleasure of the Secretary of Transportation and shall be responsible for the direction and management of the Transportation Authority.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1302. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Administrator of the Transportation Authority shall
sections.text:
The Administrator of the Transportation Authority shall:

(a) Have the authority to delegate in writing any powers and duties in this act, or its regulations, to a member or office of their respective department, subject to any limitations, conditions or requirements set out in the delegation.

(b) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Transportation Authority relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Transportation Authority (other than gubernatorial and political appointees); the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Transportation Authority; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, circulars, bulletins, and other official publications of the Transportation Authority, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Administrator.

(c) Appoint a Deputy Administrator which shall assist the Administrator with directing the Transportation Authority and shall be deemed the second-in-command of the Transportation Authority.

(d) Have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of, to an officer or employee of the Transportation Authority any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Administrator unless such delegation is prohibited by law.

(e) While performing the functions of the Administrator and the Transportation Authority, have the authority to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as necessary to carry out those functions.

(f) Have the authority to establish ranks and offices as deemed necessary.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1303. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee(s), shall create, maintain, and enforce Rule
sections.text:
The Secretary of Transportation, or their designee(s), shall create, maintain, and enforce Rules of Conduct that the public is expected to observe when using public transportation, or when within property owned by the MTA.

(a) The Rules of Conduct shall be publicly accessible.

(b) The Rules of Conduct shall only be amended when approved by the Secretary of Transportation or their designee(s), however the effective date of such an amendment shall be at least 3 days after public proclamation of the update.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1304. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: EXPANSION
The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duti
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the operation of public transportation, the maintenance and operation of public roads, and the clearance of motor vehicle accidents and hazards on public roads throughout the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel."

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duti
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the maintenance, inspection, and operation of public commuter rail systems within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duti
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to conduct their lawful duties which shall include the clearance of motor vehicle accidents, and the clearance of hazards on any bridge or tunnel within the state and shall not be obstructed.

(a) Those in violation of this section shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”.

sections.heading: The Department of Transportation shall incorporate a subordinate agency (hereinafter “Mayflower
sections.text: The Department of Transportation shall incorporate a subordinate agency (hereinafter “Mayflower Transportation Police”, “Transportation Police”, “agency”, or “MTP”); which shall be the principal law enforcement and protective entity of the Department of Transportation.
sections.notes: Unapproved consolidation draft. Source: 6 M.S.C. 1 § 1501. Review: agency compatibility review

sections.heading: The Secretary of Transportation shall have direct supervision of the Mayflower Transportation P
sections.text:
