sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Police shall
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Police shall:

(a) Enforce and/or investigate elements of the criminal code (Title 1 of the M.S.C.) and elements of the vehicle code (title 2 of the M.S.C.), subject to the limitation that at least one of the following criteria must be met:

(i) The offender endangers or harms Department of Transportation (including subordinate agency) personnel or a person utilizing Department of Transportation (including subordinate agency) services.

(ii) The offense was committed against, in relation to, or under the purview of the Department of Transportation or any of its subordinate agencies.

(iii) The offense was committed within or in eyesight of any of the following: property or infrastructure owned, maintained, or administered by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies (e.g., MTA, MAA); official operations or events conducted by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies; MTA bus stops; MTA bus routes; or road closures managed by the Department of Transportation or its subordinate agencies.

(iv) The offense relates to a motor vehicle accident or a commercial vehicle.

(v) A Transportation Police officer witnesses a felony offense or an offense that poses a significant danger to the general public or a threat to public safety.

(vi) A Transportation Police officer is participating in an inter-agency task force or any other similar assignment; or is providing assistance to another law enforcement agency.

(vii) A State of Emergency is declared.

(b) Provide protective and/or security services to the Department of Transportation and its subordinate agencies.

(c) Have the principal jurisdiction to investigate any motor vehicle accident on any roadway in the state. This jurisdiction is subordinate only to the Mayflower State Police.

(d) Have the authority to conduct commercial vehicle enforcement functions, including conducting commercial vehicle inspections and establishing commercial vehicle checkpoints. This authority is subordinate only to the Mayflower State Police.

(e) Overall ensure public safety, support the Department of Transportation, and collaborate with other law enforcement and public safety agencies to support the agency’s duties.

(i) Transportation Police officers shall have the authority to assist other peace officers who request assistance. This includes but is not limited to “10-58”, “58” (or its equivalent, e.g., panic buttons) calls on the radio or when Transportation Police assistance is specifically requested.

(ii) Transportation Police officers shall have the authority to engage in pursuits if an offender flees from MTP police or security officers who are actively attempting to detain or arrest an individual, given the aforementioned criteria for enforcing the criminal or vehicle code are met; or if assisting other peace officers as per this act.

(f) Perform any other reasonable duties or functions at the discretion of the Secretary of Transportation and/or Chief of Police.

sections.heading: Police Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall
sections.text:
Police Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall:

(a) Have peace officer status and possess all the authorities, powers, privileges, and responsibilities of any other peace officer, in addition to those granted by this legislation.

(b) Be considered employees of the Department of Transportation. For the purposes of employment limits, persons employed by the Department of Transportation and the agency shall have both positions count as one specific employment position.

sections.heading: Security Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall
sections.text:
Security Officers of the Mayflower Transportation Police shall:

(a) Not hold peace officer status nor be classified as private security officers. However, shall:

(i) Be granted the powers, authorities, and privileges afforded to private security officers under the Security Services Act. This includes but is not limited to being designated as an "authorized officer."

(ii) Be authorized, in accordance with department guidelines, to issue citations for the following offenses under the Mayflower State Code:

(1) 1 M.S.C. § 1314 “Obstruction of Transportation Authority Personnel”

(2) 1 M.S.C. § 4107 “Violation of MTA Rules of Conduct”

(3) Any other offense under the direction of a peace officer. Such citations shall be issued on behalf of the peace officer rather than the security officer.

(iii) Be authorized, in accordance with department guidelines, to operate emergency vehicles and utilize emergency lights and sirens.

(b) Be considered employees of the Department of Transportation. For the purposes of employment limits persons employed by the Department of Transportation and the agency shall have both positions count as one specific employment position.

sections.heading: LONG TITLE
sections.text: LONG TITLE. An act to ensure that checkpoints in the state are established and precedents are set up for departmental leadership to start doing checkpoints.

sections.heading: SHORT TITLE
sections.text: SHORT TITLE. This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Mayflower Checkpoint Act.”

sections.heading: The term “checkpoint” or “checking station” shall refer to the following
sections.text:
The term “checkpoint” or “checking station” shall refer to the following:

(a) Barriers set up to block traffic by law enforcement to check for BOLOs, warrants, firearms licenses, or driver’s licenses, or for commercial vehicle officers to conduct commercial vehicle inspections.

sections.heading: The term “commercial vehicle officer” shall refer to the following
sections.text:
The term “commercial vehicle officer” shall refer to the following:

(a) Any member of the state police’s commercial vehicle enforcement task force, otherwise known as CVE.

(b) An Officer of the Mayflower Transportation Police designated as such by the Chief of Police or his designee(s).

sections.heading: The term “commercial vehicle inspection” shall refer to the following
sections.text:
The term “commercial vehicle inspection” shall refer to the following:

(a) The inspection (search) of cargo, shipping documents, and commercial driver’s license(s).

sections.heading: The term “natural resources inspection” shall refer to the following
sections.text:
The term “natural resources inspection” shall refer to the following:

(a) The inspection (search) of fish, lumber, fishing license(s), and lumber license(s).

sections.heading: Commercial vehicle officers of the state police shall have the ability to establish checkpoints
sections.text:
Commercial vehicle officers of the state police shall have the ability to establish checkpoints on any public roadway and establish checkpoints on state highways for the purpose of conducting commercial vehicle inspections.

(a) The state police shall have the sole authority and power to establish checkpoints on state highways, unless an agency has proper authority from the colonel of the state police to establish one.

sections.heading: Any municipal or county law enforcement agency shall have the ability to establish checking sta
sections.text:
Any municipal or county law enforcement agency shall have the ability to establish checking stations on any municipal or county roadway within their administration for the purpose of checking driver’s license(s).

The National Guard shall have the ability to establish checkpoints anywhere within a Military Exclusion Zone or on any road directly adjacent to a Mayflower National Guard installation with the authorization from a Senior Officer or Command Group Personnel. During a deployment by the governor, the National Guard shall have the ability to establish a checkpoint on any roadway or state highway within the deployment area. Military police must be present for all established checkpoints.

sections.heading: Each department stated above shall set up its own internal regulations on how checkpoints or ch

sections.heading: To prevent the unnecessary halt of members of the public, a vehicle shall only be stopped at a
sections.text:
To prevent the unnecessary halt of members of the public, a vehicle shall only be stopped at a checkpoint or checking station for a maximum of five (5) minutes, unless the following are met:

(a) there is an active threat to the checkpoint or checking station;

(b) the vehicle is subject to a commercial vehicle or natural resource inspection; and

(c) a peace officer or member of the national guard, with reasonable suspicion of a crime, orders the individual to exit their vehicle.

sections.text:
"Bridge" shall be defined as:

(a) A lawful bridge over navigable waters of the Union of Columbia, including approaches, fenders, and appurtenances thereto, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying railroad traffic, or both railroad and highway traffic, or if a State, county, municipality, or other political subdivision is the owner or joint owner thereof, which is used and operated for the purpose of carrying highway traffic.

sections.heading: The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall be respon
sections.text:
The Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission, shall be responsible for maintenance, upkeep, and administration of all tunnels and bridges within the state.

(a) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall additionally be responsible for all firefighting, rescue, and medical efforts and operations on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(b) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall contract private companies/entities, or request other government agencies, to assist with or complete certain maintenance-related tasks on tunnels and bridges under their administration.

(c) The Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall, with the consent of the Governor of the State of Mayflower, officially name any tunnel or bridge under its administration, and must notify the public of the change through forms of public documentation or notification, such as a letter or press release.

(d) The Port Authority’s Tunnel and Bridge Commission shall maintain a plan for emergency response in the eventuality of any emergency occurring within any tunnel or bridge under its administration.

sections.heading: "Tunnel" shall be defined as
sections.text:
"Tunnel" shall be defined as:

(a) An underground, underwater, or undersea passageway which is used and operated for the purposes of vehicle, pedestrian, or railroad traffic, or any combination of the three.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to clear obstructions and ha
sections.text:
The Mayflower Transportation Authority shall have the jurisdiction to clear obstructions and hazards as well as manage traffic accidents in tunnels or on bridges administered by the Port Authority of Mayflower and Quanahassit's Tunnel and Bridge Commission.

(a) When operating in a tunnel or on a bridge administered by the Tunnel and Bridge Commission, the Mayflower Transportation Authority’s jurisdiction shall be subordinate only to the that of the Port Authority's Tunnel and Bridge Commission.

sections.text:

This measurement begins at one side of the top of the arm and extends to the opposite side of the top of the arm, while the character is standing in a standard, upright position; or

(b) The rectilinear distance light propagates, in a vacuum, in 0.00000000093357 seconds.

(a) Any person who is employed by a company or contractor to perform work in connection with the operation, maintenance, or construction of a railroad, including but not limited to engineers, conductors, brakemen, switchmen, trackmen, signalmen, and any other position designated by a company for the purposes of this clause.

sections.heading: “Railroad” shall be defined as
sections.text:
“Railroad” shall be defined as:

(a) The set of two parallel lines, usually made out of metal, of which railroad equipment operates on and includes:

(i) Branches, extensions, sidings, railroad bridges, tunnels, stations, depots, wharfs, equipment, stores or other things connected with the railroad; and

(ii) Communications or signaling systems and related facilities and equipment used for railroad purposes.

sections.heading: “Railroad equipment” shall be defined as
sections.text:
“Railroad equipment” shall be defined as:

(a) A machine exclusively designed for movement on a railroad, whether or not the machine is capable of independent motion; or

(b) A vehicle that is designed for movement both on and off a railroad while the adaptations of that vehicle for movement on a railroad are in use.

sections.text:

(a) A distinct audible signal emitted from a railroad equipment’s horn device, consisting of a loud and prolonged sound produced by the activation of the railroad equipment’s horn mechanism; or

(b) Intermittent, high-intensity lights mounted on the front of railroad equipment which create a flashing pattern when in operation.

No pedestrian shall enter, cross, remain upon or traverse on any railroad, nor walk alongside a railroad within five studs.

(a) A pedestrian may walk alongside a railroad if there is a clearly established path intended for pedestrian traffic, or if directed to do so by a peace officer or employee.

sections.text:
An employee and a peace officer shall have the ability, given that the peace officer has a burn permit, to lawfully burn a vehicle that is stuck or otherwise reasonably obstructing any part of a railroad or road crossing.

(a) All reasonable attempts must be made to move a vehicle off of a railroad or road crossing before burning such vehicle.

sections.heading: Subject to the Class I Railway Act, railroad police officers shall be given the authority to en
sections.text:
Subject to the Class I Railway Act, railroad police officers shall be given the authority to enforce all the laws of the State throughout the State with a focus in any way to the protection of properties that the company owns, possesses or administers and the persons upon those properties.

(a) Railroad police officers may carry out enforcement of all the laws of the State in the interest of public safety and in order to protect life and property and to assist law enforcement of local jurisdiction.

(b) This section shall not be construed to supersede or override any provision of the Class I Railway Act.

sections.heading: Every person who contravenes a provision of this act shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Railroa
sections.text:
Every person who contravenes a provision of this act shall be guilty of “Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(a) If such contravention endangers the life of another individual, the person shall instead be guilty of “Felony Obstruction of Railroad Operations.”

(b) Every business entity who contravenes a provision of this act is guilty of an offense and on conviction, in addition to any other penalty or punishment to which the business entity may be liable, is liable to a fine not less than two thousand dollars and not more than ten thousand dollars.

(a) A license, issued by the State of Mayflower, that permits an individual to drive on public roads.

The term “Commercial Driver’s License” and “CDL” shall refer to:

(a) A license, issued by the State of Mayflower, permits an individual to drive vehicles classified as ‘Commercial Vehicles’.

sections.text: No person shall be able to operate a motor vehicle on public roads without a valid driver’s license issued by the State of Mayflower.

sections.text: No person shall be able to operate a commercial vehicle on public roads without a valid commercial driver’s license issued by the State of Mayflower.

sections.text: Law Enforcement shall have the authority to suspend a driver’s license or CDL for a given period of time when issuing an infraction for a violation of the vehicle code.

sections.text: Any individual who also has committed three (3) traffic violations within no more than a twenty-four (24) hour period shall be eligible for suspension of their driver’s license or CDL.

sections.heading: The term “weight-units” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “weight-units” shall refer to:

(a) The amount of inventory weight that can be stored in a vehicles’ inventory.

sections.heading: The term “Commercial Vehicle” shall refer to
sections.text:
The term “Commercial Vehicle” shall refer to:

(a) a vehicle with a gross weight-unit rating of five-hundred (500) or more;

(b) is designed to transport more than 15 persons, including the driver; or

(c) a vehicle that is specified by the game’s developers to require a Commercial Driver’s License to purchase.

sections.heading: Any commercial vehicle transporting cargo on any State highway may be required to stop and be s
sections.text: Any commercial vehicle transporting cargo on any State highway may be required to stop and be subject to inspection of shipping documents or commercial license by the Mayflower State Police or an employee of the Mayflower Transportation Authority with necessary certification to inspect commercial vehicles.

sections.heading: Any law enforcement officer within their respective jurisdiction may require commercial vehicle
sections.text: Any law enforcement officer within their respective jurisdiction may require commercial vehicles to stop and subject them to inspection of shipping documents, commercial license; or cargo. If the vehicle or driver is found to be operating in an unsafe condition, or if any required part or equipment is not present or is not in proper repair or adjustment, and the continued operation would present an unduly hazardous operating condition, the officer may require the vehicle or the driver to be removed from service until necessary adjustments are made.

sections.heading: The Mayflower State Police Colonel is authorized to establish a certification program for non-l
sections.text:
The Mayflower State Police Colonel is authorized to establish a certification program for non-law-enforcement employees of the Mayflower Transit Authority. If such a program is established, the Colonel shall liaison with the department head of the Mayflower Transportation Authority. This program shall allow certified employees to:

(a) inspect commercial vehicles operating within the political subdivision in compliance with applicable laws and regulations; and

(b) request and verify commercial drivers license documentation from operators of commercial vehicles on State highways and local roads.

sections.heading: Commercial Vehicles with a gross weight-unit rating exceeding five-hundred (500) traveling on s
sections.text:
Commercial Vehicles with a gross weight-unit rating exceeding five-hundred (500) traveling on state highways or public roads with two or more lanes in one direction shall be prohibited from occupying the leftmost lane unless are using the lane to:

(a) Make a left turn.

(b) Yield to an emergency vehicle traveling in the right lane.

(c) Avoiding a road closure or emergency scene.

(d) Posted signage is present that states left lane travel is required or permissible.

sections.heading: It shall be prohibited to operate a commercial vehicle on roads designated by the department he
sections.text:
It shall be prohibited to operate a commercial vehicle on roads designated by the department head Mayflower Department of Transportation or their designee, which has appropriate signage on the road which can be clearly read—

(a) Unless it is:

(i) A state-owned commercial vehicle being lawfully operated; or

(ii) Being escorted by law enforcement or transportation authority.

(b) Any individual who unlawfully operates a commercial vehicle on a road which has been designated a no-commercial-vehicle zone shall be subject to a citation for 2 M.S.C. § 2103 “Driving in a No-Commercial-Vehicle Zone”

sections.heading: The term ‘Warning Light’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Warning Light’ shall refer to:

(a) Any device capable of flashing, steady, rotating, or oscillating an emissive light in amber or amber-and-white colors. This definition shall not include factory-installed vehicle lighting used exclusively for signaling turns, lane changes, hazard lights, or manual headlight flashing.

sections.heading: The term ‘Emergency Light’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Emergency Light’ shall refer to:

(a) Any device capable of flashing, steady, rotating, or oscillating an emissive light in red, blue, red-and-blue, blue-and white, or red-and-white color combinations. This definition shall not include factory-installed vehicle lighting used exclusively for braking, signaling turns, lane changes, reverse operation, tail illumination, or manual headlight flashing.

sections.heading: The term ‘Siren’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Siren’ shall refer to:

(a) Any mechanical, electronic, or electro-mechanical device capable of producing a loud, high-pitched oscillating sound, typically intended to signal urgency, assert right-of-way, or alert nearby individuals or vehicles to the presence of an emergency or special-purpose vehicle.

sections.heading: The term ‘Airhorn’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Airhorn’ shall refer to:

(a) Any mechanical, electronic, electro-mechanical, or pressure-powered device designed to emit a loud, non-oscillating tone, typically used to provide warning of a vehicle’s approach or to clear traffic. Airhorns are distinct from standard vehicle horns in volume, function, and purpose, and are commonly associated with emergency or special-purpose vehicles.

sections.heading: The term ‘Restricted Signal Light’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Restricted Signal Light’ shall refer to:

(a) Any device capable of flashing, steady, rotating, or oscillating a green or purple emissive light, whether used alone or in combination with other colors. These lights are typically associated with specialized functions outside of typical emergency or warning lights.

sections.heading: The term ‘Special Equipment’ shall refer to
sections.text:
The term ‘Special Equipment’ shall refer to:

(a) Any non-standard equipment affixed to a motor vehicle or equipment that is intended to provide visual or auditory signals for the purpose of asserting presence, indicating authority, ensuring operational safety, or responding to emergencies. This includes, but is not limited to, emergency lights, warning lights, sirens, airhorns, restricted signal lights, beacons, and any similar signaling devices. “Special Equipment” does not include factory-installed lighting or horns intended solely for standard vehicle signaling or manufacturer compliance with traffic safety regulations.

sections.heading: No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipm
sections.text:
No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipment that displays, shows, or is equipped with emergency lights, unless the vehicle falls under one of the following categories:

(a) Vehicles owned or leased by a government agency and operated by a law enforcement officer, correctional officer, conservation officer, or other individual authorized by statute while acting in the course of their official duties.

(i) Personally owned or civilian vehicles may only be equipped with or display emergency lights for official on-duty use, and only if first approved by the head of the employing agency and the individual holds a valid and active emergency light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

(1) However, a personally owned or civilian vehicle operated by a law enforcement officer may be temporarily equipped with emergency lighting issued directly by their employing agency (such as lighting devices distributed through department-authorized equipment lockers/shops) provided such use is strictly limited to official on-duty assignments and the lighting is deactivated, removed, and properly discarded during off-duty periods. This shall not require a separate permit from the Division of Motor Vehicles, so long as the use is authorized by the officer’s employing agency and conducted in accordance with official agency policy and Division of Motor Vehicles regulation.

(b) Vehicles owned or leased by a government agency, or by an organization that is formally contracted or designated by the government of a county or municipality to provide emergency medical or fire protection services, where such government is legally responsible for such services under applicable law, and operated by a firefighter, emergency medical technician, paramedic, or other emergency services personnel while acting in the course of their official duties.

(i) Personally owned or civilian vehicles may only be equipped with or display emergency lights when used for official on-duty purposes, or by county or municipal volunteer firefighters while responding directly to a designated headquarters or response station to report for duty in response to an actual emergency. In either case, such use must be first approved by the head of the employing agency, and the individual must hold a valid and active emergency light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

(c) Vehicles owned or operated by an individual or organization that holds a valid and active emergency light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

sections.heading: No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipm
sections.text:
No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipment that displays, shows, or is equipped with warning lights, unless the vehicle falls under one of the following categories:

(a) Vehicles owned or leased by a licensed private patrol operator (PPO), operated by a state-certified private security officer, and clearly marked as a private security vehicle, while actively engaged in the performance of official security duties on private property. A PPO must hold a valid and active warning light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles in order to lawfully equip or display warning lights if the vehicle is unmarked or is not a vehicle explicitly added by the game developers for use by the PPO.

(i) Warning lights on vehicles owned or leased by a licensed private patrol operator may only be displayed on public property when the vehicle is operated by a state-certified security officer, and when such use is essential to the performance of official security duties, or when expressly authorized for temporary use during an active emergency by an on-duty supervisor of a law enforcement agency. Any such use must comply with the provisions of 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1504. Warning lights shall not interfere with the normal flow of public traffic or the operations of emergency services, except where temporary traffic control or road closures have been expressly authorized under 4 M.S.C. 6 § 1504 due to a significant public safety concern. Unauthorized or non-essential use of warning lights on public property is strictly prohibited. All private security officers and their vehicles remain subject to the provisions of the Mayflower Traffic Code (Title 2 of the M.S.C.) at all times.

(b) Vehicles owned or leased by a government agency and operated as road or street maintenance equipment, road service vehicles, mail carrier vehicles, or public transit vehicles, when actively in operation or when a hazard exists.

(c) Vehicles owned or leased by a government agency, when actively engaged in official duties and the use of warning lights is necessary due to hazardous conditions, operational safety, or public visibility, provided such use is permitted by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

(d) Vehicles owned or operated by an individual or organization that holds a valid and active warning light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

sections.heading: No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipm
sections.text:
No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipment that displays, shows, or is equipped with restricted signal lights, unless the vehicle falls under one of the following categories:

(a) Vehicles owned or leased by a government agency, or by an organization formally contracted or designated by a county or municipal government to provide emergency medical or fire protection services, where such government is legally responsible for said services under applicable law, and operated by incident commanders, supervisory personnel, or other authorized public safety officials during active emergency operations, where green restricted signal lights are used exclusively for scene coordination and visibility. Use under this category shall not require a separate Restricted Signal Light Permit if the vehicle is owned and operated by a government agency or contractor described above, and the use is limited to official incident management duties authorized by agency policy.

(b) Vehicles operated by licensed funeral homes or contracted funeral escort services, operated by an authorized employee or agent, when actively leading or managing a funeral procession. Use under this category requires that the individual or organization operating the vehicle holds a valid and active restricted signal light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

(i) All purple restricted signal permittees remain subject to the Mayflower Vehicle Code (Title 2 of the M.S.C.) at all times.

(c) Vehicles owned or operated by a government agency, public institution, or licensed organization, and operated by authorized personnel, when used during parades, demonstrations, training, or similar pre-approved special events where green restricted signal lights are necessary for visibility or event coordination. Use under this category requires that the individual or organization operating the vehicle holds a valid and active restricted signal light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

(d) Vehicles owned or operated by an individual or organization that holds a valid and active restricted signal light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401.

sections.text:
No individual or organization shall operate or cause to be operated any motor vehicle or equipment that is equipped with or emits sound through an airhorn, unless the vehicle falls under one of the following categories:

(a) Vehicles authorized to use a siren pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3301(a) or 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3301(b).

(b) Vehicles authorized to use warning lights pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3203(a), provided their use is essential to the performance of official security duties. Use of airhorns by private security shall be limited to active emergencies, hazardous conditions, or similar situations requiring immediate attention.

(c) Vehicles authorized to use warning lights pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3203(b) or (c), when engaged in public safety, protective services, or governmental security functions.

(d) Vehicles owned or operated by an individual or organization that holds a valid and active warning light permit or restricted signal light permit issued by the Division of Motor Vehicles pursuant to 6 M.S.C. 4 § 3401, and has received separate, express authorization from the Division to equip and utilize an airhorn. sections.heading: The Division of Motor Vehicles shall be authorized, at its discretion, to issue written permits
sections.text: The Division of Motor Vehicles shall be authorized, at its discretion, to issue written permits authorizing an individual or organization to equip and utilize vehicles with special equipment, in accordance with the provisions of this Chapter. Such authorization shall permit the use of special equipment on vehicles owned or operated by the permit holder, subject to all applicable laws, Division regulations, and any conditions specified in the permit. The Division may issue such permits upon determining that the proposed use of special equipment is reasonably necessary to ensure the safety of personnel, equipment, or the general public during the performance of official duties or operational functions, or is otherwise deemed necessary by the Division based on unique operational needs or circumstances. Nothing in this section shall obligate the Division to approve any permit application. All permits shall be subject to periodic review and may be modified, suspended, or revoked at the sole discretion of the Division.

sections.text: “Pilot Training Program” or “PTP” shall be defined as: The mandated curriculum enacted by the State Aviation Advisory Board for individuals seeking a pilot certification.

sections.text: “Pilot-in-Command” or “PIC” shall be defined as: The person who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of the flight; who has been designated as the PIC before or during the flight; and who holds the appropriate category, class, and type rating, if appropriate, for the conduct of the flight.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Person” shall be defined as
sections.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Person” shall be defined as: An individual, firm, partnership, corporation, company, association, joint-stock association, or governmental entity. It includes a trustee, receiver, assignee, or similar representative person.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Aircraft” shall be defined as
sections.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Aircraft” shall be defined as: A device or machine that is used or intended to be used for flight in the air.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Airport” shall be defined as
sections.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Airport” shall be defined as: An area of land or water that is used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of aircraft, and includes its buildings and facilities, if applicable.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Practical Test” shall be defined as
sections.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Practical Test” shall be defined as: A test on the areas of operations for an airman certificate, rating, or authorization is conducted by having the applicant respond to questions and demonstrate maneuvers in flight, in a flight simulator, or a flight training device.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Heliport” shall be defined as
sections.text: For the purposes of this subchapter, “Heliport” shall be defined as: An area of land, water, or structure used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of helicopters.

sections.heading: The Administrator of the Aviation Administration shall
sections.text:
The Administrator of the Aviation Administration shall:

(a) Be the final authority for carrying out all functions, powers, and duties of the Administration relating to: the appointment and employment of all officers and employees of the Administration (other than gubernatorial and political appointees); the acquisition and maintenance of property, services, and equipment of the Administration; the promulgation of regulations, rules, orders, circulars, bulletins, and other official publications of the Administration, except as otherwise provided; and any other obligation imposed on or power conferred upon the Administrator.

(b) Appoint a Deputy Administrator which shall assist the Administrator with directing the administration.

(c) Have no interest or stake in any aviation-related business or industry after the date of their employment. This also applies to the Deputy Administrator of the Administration.

(d) Offer advice and counsel to the Governor with respect to the civil and military aviation of the State of Mayflower.

(e) Have the authority to delegate and authorize successive re-delegations of, to an officer or employee of the Administration any function, power, or duty conferred upon the Administrator, unless such delegation is prohibited by law.

(f) Have the authority, while in the performance of the functions of the Administrator and the Administration, to issue, rescind, and revise such regulations as are necessary to carry out those functions.

sections.text:

All airman’s licenses and certifications shall be issued in the name of the Administrator but shall be issuable only by the Flight Standards Office in accordance with the process set out in this act.The “Flight Standards Office”, which shall be responsible for the issuance of airman’s licenses and certifications. All airman’s licenses and certifications shall be issued in the name of the Administrator but shall be issuable only by the Flight Standards Office in accordance with the process set out in this act.

(ii) The “Office of Commercial Space Transportation”, which shall be responsible for the administration and approval of any non-military rocket launch operations.

(iii) The Administrator may delegate their authority to additional offices that they may form, but may not detract from the authority of the afore-listed statutory offices.

(b) Perform any other reasonable duties or functions at the discretion of the Secretary of Transportation and/or Administrator.

sections.text: The mission of the Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall be to determine the probable cause of transportation accidents and incidents and to formulate safety recommendations to improve transportation safety.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall make recommendations to the Administrator, to t
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall make recommendations to the Administrator, to the Senate, to the Governor, to the Commanding Officer of the Mayflower National Guard’s Air Unit, and to the public.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board has the primary authority to investigate every civil
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board has the primary authority to investigate every civil aviation accident in the State of Mayflower. The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall also be authorized to conduct investigations involving both civilian and military aircraft with the participation of appropriate military authorities.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall cooperate with the Mayflower Bureau of Investig
sections.text: The Mayflower Transportation Safety Board shall cooperate with the Mayflower Bureau of Investigation and/or the Mayflower Transportation Police on any investigations of aviation incidents of a criminal nature.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall be empowered to create and enforce regulation on mi
sections.text: The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall be empowered to create and enforce regulation on military, law enforcement, civil, and commercial aviation.

sections.heading: An individual not holding one of the certificates or licenses outlined in this section may not
sections.text: An individual not holding one of the certificates or licenses outlined in this section may not operate or serve as the pilot in command of an aircraft. Individuals holding a certificate or license under this section shall only operate aircraft or serve as pilots in command within the limitations of their certificate and license.

sections.heading: The Student Pilot Certificate
sections.text:
The Student Pilot Certificate:

(a) To be eligible for a Student Pilot Certificate, an applicant must ⎼

(i) be enrolled in the Pilot Training Program;

(ii) be physically and mentally able to operate an aircraft;

(iii) not had an airman’s certification or license revoked in the past.

(1) This requirement may be waived by the Administrator for good cause.

(iv) Meet any and all requirements set by the Mayflower Aviation Administration for this certificate.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have the authority to promulgate regulations and fu
sections.text: The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have the authority to promulgate regulations and further criteria pertaining to the Student Pilot Certification.

sections.heading: Applications for a Recreational Pilot Certificate must be submitted to the Flight Standards Off
sections.text: Applications for a Recreational Pilot Certificate must be submitted to the Flight Standards Office in a form acceptable to the Administrator.

sections.heading: The Private Pilot Certificate
sections.text:
The Private Pilot Certificate:

(a) To be eligible for a Private Pilot Certificate, an applicant must ⎼

(i) Pass the required knowledge certification examination created, dictated, and administered by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.

(1) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have full authority over this examination.

(ii) Receive flight training and an endorsement from an authorized flight instructor under the appropriate guidelines set out by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.

(iii) Pass the practical flight examination created, dictated, and administered by the Mayflower Aviation Administration.

(iv) Hold a student pilot certificate.

(v) Meet any and all requirements set by the Mayflower Aviation Administration for this certificate.

(b) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have the authority to promulgate regulations and further criteria pertaining to the Private Pilot Certification.

(c) Applications for a Private Pilot Certificate must be submitted to the Flight Standards Office in a form acceptable to the Administrator.

sections.heading: The Commercial Pilot Certificate
sections.text:
The Commercial Pilot Certificate:

(a) To be eligible for a Certificate Pilot Certificate, an applicant must ⎼

(i) Actively hold a Private Pilot Certificate, and have held said certificate for at least 12 days;

(1) The Administrator may provide exemptions to this section.

(ii) Have 6 logged hours as the pilot in command of an aircraft.

(iii) Have no significant infractions on their Airman’s record.

(iv) Meet any and all requirements set by the Mayflower Aviation Administration for this certificate.

(b) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall have the authority to promulgate regulations and further criteria pertaining to the Commercial Pilot Certification.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Aviation Administration (hereinafter "the Administration") shall have the power t
sections.text: The Mayflower Aviation Administration (hereinafter "the Administration") shall have the power to create, amend, and enforce regulations necessary to ensure the safety, security, and efficiency of aviation operations within its jurisdiction.

sections.heading: The Administration may establish rules governing
The Administration is authorized to
sections.text:
The Administration is authorized to:

(a) Conduct inspections, audits, and investigations to ensure compliance with aviation laws and regulations;

(b) Issue fines, penalties, or other administrative sanctions for violations; and

(c) Suspend or revoke licenses, certifications, and permits for non-compliance.

sections.heading: In cases where immediate action is required to address aviation safety threats, the Administrat
sections.text: In cases where immediate action is required to address aviation safety threats, the Administration may issue temporary regulations, effective immediately upon issuance, with a validity period of up to 30 days, subject to formal legislative review.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this chapter, “Aircraft” shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, “Aircraft” shall be defined as:

(a) A device or machine that is used or intended to be used for flight in the air.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this chapter, “Civilian Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, “Civilian Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as:

(a) The person who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of a privately owned Aircraft.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this chapter, “State Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, “State Pilot-in-Command” shall be defined as:

(a) The person, who is an on-duty guardsman or government employee, who is authorised to operate an aircraft and who has final authority and responsibility for the operation and safety of a government owned Aircraft.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this chapter, “Airport” shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, “Airport” shall be defined as:

(a) An area of land or water that is used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of aircraft, and includes its buildings and facilities, if applicable; this definition shall not refer to or include heliports.

sections.heading: For the purposes of this chapter, “Heliport” shall be defined as
sections.text:
For the purposes of this chapter, “Heliport” shall be defined as:

(a) An area of land, water, or structure that is used or intended to be used for the landing and takeoff of helicopters, and includes its buildings and facilities, if applicable.

sections.heading: The Port Authority Police Department and Mayflower Transportation Police shall be responsible f
sections.text:

(a) This shall not prohibit other law enforcement agencies from assisting with or conducting law enforcement duties within an Airport unless otherwise directed by an officer of the Port Authority Police Department or Mayflower Transportation Police.

sections.text: DEFINITIONS. “Tail Number” shall be defined as the combination of letters and numbers assigned to a specific civilian aircraft displayed on the upper sides of a civilian aircraft.

sections.text: For the purposes of this act, “Registry” or “Registries” shall refer to any database, registry, list, document, or collection containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.

sections.heading: REGISTRY PROHIBITIONS
sections.text: REGISTRY PROHIBITIONS. Notwithstanding 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1401 and 6 M.S.C. 6 § 1601, the Mayflower Aviation Administration may not create any regulation, rule, directive, mandate, order, announcement, or policy forcing owners of civilian aircraft to submit their tail numbers to a registry.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not create any registry containing tail numbers of ci
sections.text:
The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not create any registry containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.

(a) The Mayflower Aviation Administration shall destroy and erase all registries containing tail numbers of civilian aircraft.

(b) The Aircraft Identification Registry and all of its related documents shall be destroyed and deleted.

sections.heading: The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not force any pilot to leak the tail number associate
sections.text:
The Mayflower Aviation Administration may not force any pilot to leak the tail number associated with any civilian aircraft.

(a) All pilots shall enjoy the right of keeping their tail numbers private.

(b) All pilots shall enjoy the right of not having their tail number noted down on any registry.
